14. State Management

  • useSession (Zustand, memory): { accessToken, role, userId, profileId, instituteId, setTokens(), clear() }.
  • useAppFlags (Zustand + MMKV): { installId, onboardingSeenVersion, lastRole, pushPromptShownAt, pendingDeepLink }.
  • useOfflineQueue (Zustand + MMKV): { items: QueuedMutation[], enqueue(), flush(), remove() }.
  • Query keys: meKeys.me, mastersKeys.all, mastersKeys.areas(cityId). useMe has staleTime 60 s and refetches on app foreground.
  • Upload state lives in useUpload (per call site) — { progress, status: idle|presigning|uploading|confirming|done|error, fileId }.

15. Offline Handling

  • GET /me and GET /masters are persisted; the app can start fully offline with a cached session.
  • PUT /devices/me is queued (latest wins — the queue keeps only the newest device update).
  • POST /events batches are kept in MMKV (max 500 events) and flushed when online.
  • Uploads: online only to start; if interrupted, the sheet shows "Paused — will resume when online" and restarts from presign on reconnect.

16. Push Notification Requirements

This module provides the delivery infrastructure; it sends no events of its own. Android channels are created at first launch: leads (high), account, payments, reviews (default), general (low). The app handles notification taps in the three states described in conventions §9 and marks the item read via M48.

17. Security Rules

  • Refresh token and install id only in secure store; encrypted MMKV key generated per install.
  • /files/:id/url checks ownership (uploaded_by_id = sub) or a module-specific rule (e.g. a complaint attachment visible to its reporter only).
  • Presigned URLs are single-object, short-lived, and never cached or logged.
  • /events is rate limited (60 batches/min per install) and rejects PII keys; IPs are truncated before storage in analytics.
  • /masters and /bootstrap are public but cached at the CDN edge for 5 minutes.
  • Screens flagged secure (documents, OTP, payments) enable FLAG_SECURE / iOS snapshot blur through a useSecureScreen() hook.

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code App behaviour
No network NETWORK_OFFLINE (client) Offline banner; cached data; queued actions
Request timed out NETWORK_TIMEOUT (client) Retry button in ErrorState
Access token expired AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRED Silent refresh + retry
Refresh invalid AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID Sign out → Login with message
Account suspended ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED AccountBlocked screen
Upload URL expired before PUT R2 403 Re-presign automatically once
Uploaded object doesn't match presign FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED / FILE_TOO_LARGE Inline error on the picker, file row deleted
Too many pending uploads LIMIT_REACHED "Finish or cancel your other uploads first."
Unknown deep link — Home + toast

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T0.1 Launch with no session → Auth stack; with a valid refresh token → role tabs; with a revoked token → Login with "Please sign in again."
  • T0.2 Two requests get 401 at the same time → exactly one /auth/refresh call; both retried once.
  • T0.3 Airplane mode: app opens from cache, banner visible; favourite added offline is sent once on reconnect (server sees one row).
  • T0.4 FCM token changes → PUT /devices/me sent once; same token signed in on another account → first account's device revoked.
  • T0.5 Upload 9.8 MB PDF succeeds; 10.5 MB rejected client-side; mismatched Content-Type rejected on confirm.
  • T0.6 Kill the app mid-upload → upload resumes after relaunch; pending file cleaned after 24 h if abandoned.
  • T0.7 /masters returns 304 with matching ETag; cache refreshes when mastersVersion changes.
  • T0.8 Events containing a phone prop are rejected with VALIDATION_FAILED; analytics off → only operational events sent.
  • T0.9 NotificationService called twice with the same dedupe key → one inbox row, one push.
  • T0.10 Push during quiet hours (non-urgent) is delivered at 08:00 IST; urgent push delivered immediately.

20. Audit Log Events

Event When
app.device_registered First PUT /devices/me for an install (platform, app version; no token)
app.device_revoked DELETE /devices/me or token invalidated
app.file_uploaded Upload confirmed (purpose, size, mime; no file name for identity documents)

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Certificate pinning (TrustKit / react-native-ssl-public-key-pinning) with a backup pin once the API domain is stable.
  • Play Integrity API and Apple App Attest tokens on sensitive calls (OTP request, payments) to block emulators and scripted abuse.
  • Move analytics to a dedicated pipeline (e.g. PostHog / BigQuery) when event volume passes ~5M/day.
  • Partition user_notifications by month and archive items older than 12 months.
  • Offline-first local database (WatermelonDB) only if a future feature needs heavy offline editing; the query cache is enough for v1.

Module 1 · Splash Screen

Phase 1 · App Foundation · Used by: Everyone (before sign-in and on every launch) · Depends on: M00; Admin M04 (settings for versions and maintenance) · New tables: none · Uses: system_settings · Build estimate: 1–2 days

1. Module Purpose

The first screen on every cold start. It shows the GuruConnect logo while the app loads its configuration from GET /bootstrap, then decides where to go: maintenance screen, forced update, optional update prompt, onboarding, login, registration resume, or the user's home. The brief's app_versions and maintenance_settings tables are implemented as admin-editable keys in system_settings (Admin M04), so admins change versions and maintenance without a deploy.

2. User Stories

  • As a user, I want the app to open quickly and tell me clearly if it is down for maintenance so that I'm not stuck on a blank screen.
  • As a user on an old version, I want to be told to update, with a button to the store, so that the app keeps working.
  • As an admin, I want to force everyone below a version to update when an API change breaks old builds.
  • As a returning user, I want to land directly on my home screen without signing in again.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-1.1 Launch sequence (target ≤ 2.5 s to first interactive screen on a mid-range Android).

  1. Native splash (static logo on brand background) shows while JS loads — expo-splash-screen.preventAutoHideAsync().
  2. JS splash (same image, plus a small spinner after 800 ms) renders; the native splash is hidden to avoid a flash.
  3. In parallel: read secure store (refresh token, install id), read cached bootstrap and /me, call GET /bootstrap (timeout 5 s).
  4. Evaluate gates in this order: maintenance → force update → session → onboarding → optional update.

BR-1.2 Maintenance. If maintenance.enabled is true → Maintenance screen with the admin message and expected end time. The screen polls /bootstrap every 60 s while open and on "Try again"; when maintenance ends the app continues the launch sequence. Admins listed in maintenance.allowInstallIds (QA devices, settings key optional) bypass it.

BR-1.3 Version check. Compare the running version (expo-application nativeApplicationVersion) with the platform's values:

  • below minVersion (app.android_min_version / app.ios_min_version) → ForceUpdate screen (no dismiss, back button exits app on Android).
  • below latestVersion but ≥ min → optional update bottom sheet after reaching home, at most once per 3 days per latest version (updatePromptDismissedFor in MMKV).
  • Semver comparison; build number ignored. The API independently enforces the minimum with 426 APP_UPDATE_REQUIRED (conventions §5).

BR-1.4 Bootstrap failure. Network error or timeout: if a cached bootstrap (≤ 7 days old) exists, continue with it and show the offline banner; if no cache (very first launch offline) show the NoConnection state with Retry.

BR-1.5 Session routing. Refresh token present → POST /auth/refresh then GET /me (M00). Result:

  • ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED → AccountBlocked (M00).
  • registration incomplete (/me.registration.nextStep) → resume that registration step (M06/M07/M11/M14/M15/M21/M22).
  • otherwise → role tabs. Offline with a cached /me → role tabs from cache. No token → if onboardingSeenVersion < app.onboarding_version → Onboarding (M02), else RoleSelect (M03).

BR-1.6 Deep link on launch. A link that opened the app is captured before routing (Linking.getInitialURL() / notification tap) and stored as pendingDeepLink; it is replayed after the gates pass (and after login if needed).

BR-1.7 What bootstrap returns. Public settings only (is_public = true): platform versions, update message, store URLs, maintenance state/message/end, onboarding version, enabled login methods, support contacts, legal URLs, feature flags, limits the app displays (max children, review min chars), mastersVersion, server time (to detect wrong device clocks > 5 min — shows a hint because OTP and payments can fail).

BR-1.8 Caching. /bootstrap is cached at the CDN for 60 s (no user data) and in MMKV on the device. Response is < 5 KB.

4. Screen List

Screen Route name Purpose
Splash Splash Logo while bootstrap, session and caches load
Maintenance Maintenance Admin message, expected end time, Try again
Force update ForceUpdate Blocks the app below the minimum version, opens the store
Optional update sheet UpdateSheet (modal) Suggests updating; dismissible
No connection NoConnection First launch without internet and no cached bootstrap

6. Screen Wireframe Description

Splash — full-screen brand background (light: white with the green logo mark centred; dark: near-black). Logo 120 dp. Below it, after 800 ms, a small 20 dp spinner. Bottom: "GuruConnect" wordmark and tagline "Find a teacher you can trust" in 14 sp muted text. No buttons.

Maintenance — illustration of tools at top third; heading "We'll be right back"; body = admin message (max 3 lines); if end time: "Expected back by 6:30 PM today"; primary button "Try again"; secondary text link "Contact support" showing email and phone as selectable text.

Force update — app icon 72 dp; heading "Update required"; body = app.update_message; small text "You have 1.0.3 · Required 1.2.0"; primary button "Update now" (opens Play Store / App Store URL from bootstrap); no close button.

Optional update sheet — bottom sheet: heading "New version available", body = update message, buttons "Update" (primary) and "Later".

No connection — cloud-off icon, heading "No internet connection", body "Connect to Wi-Fi or mobile data to set up GuruConnect.", button "Retry".

  • Maintenance end time must be in the future to be shown; otherwise the line is hidden.

13. Relationships

No database relationships (client-side module).

14. State Management

  • bootstrapKeys.current — persisted query; the whole app reads flags from useBootstrap().data.
  • useAppFlags: onboardingSeenVersion, updatePromptDismissedFor: { version, at }, pendingDeepLink.
  • Launch state machine inside useLaunchSequence (not global): booting → gating → routing → done, exposed to tests.

15. Offline Handling

  • Cached bootstrap up to 7 days old is accepted; older cache is treated as missing (shows NoConnection on first-run devices only).
  • Maintenance and force-update decisions made from cache are re-checked as soon as the network returns.
  • Offline with a cached session goes straight to role tabs (M00 BR-0.3/0.4).

16. Push Notification Requirements

None sent by this module. A notification tap that cold-starts the app passes through Splash; its deep link is replayed after the gates (BR-1.6).

17. Security Rules

  • /bootstrap is public and contains no user data; response is identical for all users of a platform/version (safe to CDN-cache).
  • Store URLs come from the server but are only opened if the host is play.google.com or apps.apple.com (prevents a compromised setting redirecting users).
  • Wrong device clock (> 5 min from serverTime) is surfaced as a hint, not blocked.

Module 2 · Onboarding Screens

Phase 1 · App Foundation · Used by: Everyone, signed out (first launch, or after an admin bumps the onboarding version) · Depends on: M00 (bootstrap, app flags), M01 (Splash routes here) · New tables: none · Build estimate: 1–2 days

1. Module Purpose

A short, swipeable slide carousel shown once before RoleSelect (M03), explaining what GuruConnect is and why it can be trusted: verified teachers, an honest Trust Score, free demo classes before paying, and safe on-platform payments. It is entirely client-side — no API of its own — and is skipped for anyone who already has a session (Splash routes signed-in users straight to their role tabs). An admin can force it to show again for signed-out installs by bumping app.onboarding_version in system_settings (Admin M04); no app release is needed.

2. User Stories

  • As a first-time user, I want a quick, honest explanation of what the app does before I'm asked to sign in, so that I trust it enough to hand over my phone number.
  • As a parent on a slow connection, I want the onboarding slides to appear instantly with no spinner, so that the first impression of the app isn't a loading screen.
  • As a returning user who already has an account, I never want to see onboarding again, even if the admin changes the slide content.
  • As a low-vision user, I want to skip straight to sign-in with one accessible tap, so that I'm not forced through slides I can't read comfortably.
  • As product, I want to update the slide copy or images without an app store release, so that we can react to what new users are confused about.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-2.1 Trigger. Splash (M01, BR-1.5) shows Onboarding only when there is no refresh token and useAppFlags.onboardingSeenVersion < bootstrap.onboardingVersion (default seeded value 1, key app.onboarding_version). Any signed-in launch — even offline from a cached session — bypasses onboarding entirely regardless of version; onboarding is a pre-account experience only, never re-shown to an existing account. BR-2.2 Slide content (4 fixed slides, English only at launch; strings in en.json from day one for the Hindi rollout).

  1. Find verified teachers — Aadhaar, PAN and certificates checked before anyone appears in search.
  2. See an honest Trust Score — built from verification, real reviews and complaint history, not payment.
  3. Book a free demo first — try a class before you commit to a plan.
  4. Pay safely, in the app — Razorpay-secured payments, refund protection, and support that responds. Each slide is { illustration, heading (≤ 40 chars), body (≤ 110 chars) }, bundled as local assets (no CDN fetch, so the very first offline launch still works). BR-2.3 Navigation. Horizontal paging with a dot indicator (4 dots, active dot 24 dp wide, others 8 dp). Skip sits top-right on slides 1–3 (44×44 dp touch target). Slide 4 replaces Skip/Next with a single primary button Get started. Swiping past slide 4 does nothing (no wrap-around). BR-2.4 Persistence. Tapping Skip or Get started writes useAppFlags.onboardingSeenVersion = bootstrap.onboardingVersion to MMKV synchronously, then navigates to RoleSelect (M03). If the write fails (corrupt storage), navigation still proceeds — onboarding may show once more next launch, which is a cosmetic-only failure mode. BR-2.5 Version bump re-show. When an admin increases app.onboarding_version (Admin M04), only installs that are currently signed out see the slides again on their next launch; an install that is signed in never sees it, even after signing out later that session, until the next cold start re-evaluates BR-2.1 with a fresh onboardingSeenVersion comparison. BR-2.6 No network calls. The screen reads bootstrap.onboardingVersion (already fetched by Splash, M01) and nothing else; there is no dedicated onboarding endpoint. BR-2.7 Accessibility. Each slide's illustration has accessibilityLabel matching its heading; dots are not individually focusable (decorative); Skip and Get started have 48 dp minimum touch height and are the first two elements in swipe/tab order after the slide content.

Screen Route name Purpose
Onboarding Onboarding Full-screen 4-slide swipeable carousel

5. Screen Flow & Navigation

Back button on Android moves to the previous slide, not out of the app; pressing back on slide 1 exits the app (it is the first screen in the signed-out stack). There is no error state — the screen never calls the network.

6. Screen Wireframe Description

Onboarding, slide 1 of 4 — full-bleed illustration (top 55% of screen, a parent and teacher on a video call over a soft green background), heading "Find verified teachers", body "Aadhaar, PAN and certificates checked before anyone appears in search.", dot row (● ○ ○ ○) centred below the body, Skip text button top-right (16 sp, muted).

Slide 2 — illustration of a star rating and a shield badge, heading "See an honest Trust Score", body "Built from verification, real reviews and complaint history — never bought.", dots (○ ● ○ ○).

Slide 3 — illustration of a calendar with a "Free" tag, heading "Book a free demo first", body "Try a class before you commit to a plan.", dots (○ ○ ● ○).

Slide 4 — illustration of a phone with a UPI/card icon and a lock, heading "Pay safely, in the app", body "Razorpay-secured payments, refund protection, and support that responds.", dots (○ ○ ○ ●), sticky bottom button "Get started" (primary, full width) replaces the Skip link.

7. UI Components & Component Tree

OnboardingScreen
├─ SlideCarousel (FlashList, horizontal, pagingEnabled, 4 items)
│  └─ OnboardingSlide({ illustration, heading, body })
├─ DotIndicator({ count: 4, activeIndex })
├─ SkipButton               (hidden on slide 4)
└─ StickyActionBar          (only rendered on slide 4: "Get started")

useOnboarding() — reads bootstrap.onboardingVersion, exposes markSeen() which writes useAppFlags.onboardingSeenVersion and calls navigation.replace('RoleSelect'). No other hooks; the slide content array is a static constant (onboardingSlides.ts), not fetched.

8. Validation Rules

No user input on this screen. The only "value" handled is the onboarding version number read from bootstrap, which is validated by M01 (BR-1.7 public settings are typed by Admin M04 on save); a missing or non-numeric value is treated as 1 (never blocks the carousel).

9. API Endpoints

Method Path Auth Description
— — — None. This module has no endpoints; it reads onboardingVersion from M01's GET /bootstrap.

10. Request Payloads

No requests. The screen makes no network calls of its own.

11. Response Payloads

No responses. See M01 @responses for the bootstrap.onboardingVersion field this module reads.

12. PostgreSQL Tables & Columns

No database tables. This module is client-side only.

13. Relationships

No database relationships (client-side module).

14. State Management

  • Reads bootstrapKeys.current (M01) for onboardingVersion; no query of its own.
  • Writes useAppFlags.onboardingSeenVersion (Zustand + MMKV, shared store owned by M00) — the only state this module touches.
  • No TanStack Query keys, no mutations, nothing persisted beyond that one flag.

15. Offline Handling

Fully offline-first: all illustrations and copy are bundled in the app binary, so the carousel renders identically with or without network. markSeen() is a local MMKV write and never queues or waits for connectivity.

16. Push Notification Requirements

None. This screen is shown before any device is registered for push (M00 BR-0.6 registration happens after sign-in).

17. Security Rules

No PII is collected or displayed. The screen is not FLAG_SECURE (nothing sensitive on it). No tokens, no rate limits — there is nothing to abuse on a client-only screen.

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
MMKV write fails when marking seen — (client-only) — Navigation to RoleSelect proceeds anyway; onboarding may reappear once more next launch — cosmetic only, never blocks sign-in
bootstrap.onboardingVersion missing/malformed — (client-only) — Treated as version 1; carousel still shows correctly for a true first launch

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T2.1 First-ever launch, no cached flags → Onboarding shows; Maestro flow onboarding_first_launch.
  • T2.2 Swipe left through all 4 slides; dot indicator updates each time; swiping past slide 4 does nothing.
  • T2.3 Tap Skip on slide 2 → lands on RoleSelect; onboardingSeenVersion is written immediately (check MMKV).
  • T2.4 Tap Get started on slide 4 → lands on RoleSelect.
  • T2.5 Relaunch after seeing onboarding, still signed out → RoleSelect directly, no carousel.
  • T2.6 Admin bumps app.onboarding_version from 1 to 2 → next signed-out launch on the same install shows the carousel again; a signed-in install on another test device does not see it.
  • T2.7 First launch fully offline (airplane mode) → carousel still renders from bundled assets, no error state, no spinner.
  • T2.8 Android hardware back on slide 1 → app exits; on slide 3 → returns to slide 2.
  • T2.9 Screen reader on: each illustration announces its heading text via accessibilityLabel; Skip and Get started are reachable by a single swipe-right gesture.
  • T2.10 System font scaled to 130% → slide 2's body text (the longest) does not clip or overlap the dot indicator.

20. Audit Log Events

None. The screen changes no server-side data and involves no account — there is nothing to attribute an audit event to (no user_id exists yet).

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Personalise slide order or copy by acquisition channel (e.g. a teacher-focused variant for institute referral links) using the same onboardingVersion mechanism, versioned per audience segment.
  • A/B test slide copy through a remote-config layer once one exists (see M00 scalability).
  • Video or Lottie illustrations instead of static images once bundle size budget (conventions §17, 6 MB) allows it.
  • Track onboarding_slide_viewed / onboarding_skipped analytics events (M00 POST /events) to see where users drop off, once the analytics pipeline can slice by slide index.

Module 3 · Authentication Selection

Phase 1 · App Foundation · Used by: Everyone, signed out · Depends on: M00, M01, M02; M04 (screens this module hands off to) · New tables: none · Build estimate: 1 day

1. Module Purpose

The single front door into sign-in: one screen offering "Continue with phone number" (primary), "Continue with Google" and a small "Sign in with email instead" link. It decides nothing about role — role is chosen later, during registration (M05) — it only chooses which credential flow the person takes into Login (M04). It is client-only: the choice just navigates into M04's phone, email or Google screens, which do the actual API calls.

2. User Stories

  • As a new parent, I want one clear "Continue with phone number" button so that I don't have to think about which sign-in method to pick.
  • As a teacher who prefers Gmail, I want a one-tap Google option so that I skip typing a password.
  • As a returning user without SMS signal, I want an email option so that I can still sign in.
  • As product, I want to hide a sign-in method instantly (e.g. Google outage) without an app release, so that support isn't flooded with a broken button.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-3.1 Method visibility. Buttons are shown/hidden from bootstrap.auth (M01): phoneOtp (always true in v1; phone OTP cannot be disabled, it is the only method that also identifies India-only users reliably), email (auth.email_login_enabled), google (auth.google_login_enabled). If both email and google are false, only the phone button shows and the divider/links are hidden. BR-3.2 Order and prominence. Phone is always the primary full-width button (highest conversion, matches conventions §2 OTP autofill investment). Google is a secondary full-width button directly below it, with the standard Google "G" mark and "Continue with Google" text (per Google's branding guidelines — no custom colours on the G). Email is a plain text link below a thin "or" divider, not a button — it is a fallback, not a first choice. BR-3.3 Navigation, not authentication. Tapping Phone pushes M04's PhoneEntry screen (collects the number, calls POST /auth/otp/request). Tapping Email pushes M04's EmailEntry screen (email + password, or a link to switch to "email OTP instead"). Tapping Google does not navigate anywhere first — it immediately opens the native Google account picker (GoogleSignin.signIn()); on success the resulting ID token is sent straight to M04's POST /auth/google from this screen's own handler, and the result (existing user → home; new user → registration) is what decides the next screen, exactly as it would from inside M04. BR-3.4 Legal footer. Below the buttons, small centred text: "By continuing, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy." Both phrases are tappable links opening legal.termsUrl / legal.privacyUrl (from bootstrap) in an in-app browser tab (expo-web-browser), never leaving the app or requiring sign-in. BR-3.5 No account created here. No account, OTP challenge or registration token is created by this screen itself; those only start once a method is chosen and its M04 screen (or the Google handler) makes its first API call. BR-3.6 Back behaviour. AuthSelect is the base of the signed-out stack after Onboarding. Android hardware back exits the app with a "Press back again to exit" toast (2-second window) rather than exiting on the first press, to avoid accidental exits while re-reading the legal footer. BR-3.7 Offline. If the device has no cached bootstrap at all (very first launch, offline — see M01 BR-1.4 NoConnection), this screen is never reached; Splash keeps the user on NoConnection until a bootstrap response (fresh or cached) exists. Once reached, the screen itself never blocks on network — only the method screens it hands off to do.

4. Screen List

Screen Route name Purpose
Auth select AuthSelect Choose phone, Google or email to continue

5. Screen Flow & Navigation

Diagram loads when this page is online…

Back from PhoneEntry or EmailEntry returns here; a cancelled Google picker (user dismisses it) simply stays on AuthSelect with no error shown (cancellation is not a failure).

6. Screen Wireframe Description

AuthSelect — vertically centred content on a plain white (dark: near-black) background. GuruConnect logo mark, 64 dp, top third. Heading "Welcome to GuruConnect" (24 sp, bold). Subtext "Find a teacher you can trust" (16 sp, muted). Below, stacked with 12 dp gaps: primary full-width button "Continue with phone number" (phone icon, left-aligned icon + centred text); secondary full-width button "Continue with Google" (white background, grey border, Google G icon); thin horizontal divider with centred "or" (12 sp, muted); text link "Sign in with email instead" (centred, 15 sp, underlined on press). Fixed footer (not sticky-scrolling, always visible): two-line legal text with the Terms/Privacy links underlined.

7. UI Components & Component Tree

AuthSelectScreen
├─ BrandLogo · Heading · Subtext
├─ Button "Continue with phone number" (primary) → navigate PhoneEntry
├─ Button "Continue with Google" (secondary, GoogleIcon) → useGoogleSignIn()
├─ Divider "or"                          (hidden if email disabled)
├─ TextLink "Sign in with email instead" → navigate EmailEntry   (hidden if email disabled)
└─ LegalFooter (Terms, Privacy)          → openInAppBrowser(url)

useAuthMethods() — derives { showPhone, showGoogle, showEmail } from useBootstrap().data.auth. useGoogleSignIn() — wraps GoogleSignin.hasPlayServices() → signIn() → posts the ID token to M04's googleLogin mutation; surfaces GATEWAY_ERROR (Play Services missing/outdated) and silent cancellation separately.

8. Validation Rules

No form fields on this screen. The only implicit "input" is which button is tapped, and visibility of each is already gated by BR-3.1 so a hidden method can never be tapped.

9. API Endpoints

Method Path Auth Description
— — — None owned here. Phone/email navigation is client-only; Google immediately calls M04 POST /auth/google (documented there) directly from this screen's handler.

10. Request Payloads

No requests of this module's own. See M04 @requests for POST /auth/google, which this screen's Google button triggers directly.

11. Response Payloads

No responses of this module's own. See M04 @responses for the POST /auth/google result this screen acts on (route to Home or to Registration).

12. PostgreSQL Tables & Columns

No database tables. This module is client-side only.

13. Relationships

No database relationships (client-side module).

14. State Management

  • Reads bootstrapKeys.current (M01) for auth.phoneOtp/email/google flags — no store of its own.
  • useAppFlags.lastRole (if present, from a previous session on this install) is read only to decide which role tab to warm the query cache for after Google login succeeds — it never changes which buttons are shown.

15. Offline Handling

The screen itself renders fully from the cached bootstrap (no additional network call). Phone/email buttons remain tappable offline (they only navigate); Google's button is disabled with a small inline "Needs internet" hint when NetInfo reports no connection, since the native picker and the server verification both require network.

16. Push Notification Requirements

None. No device is registered yet at this point (M00 BR-0.6 happens after a session exists).

17. Security Rules

No credentials are entered or stored on this screen. The Google ID token is passed in memory straight from the native SDK callback to the API call and is never persisted, logged or cached (client meta: { persist: false } on that call, per M00 BR-0.4). The in-app browser opens only guruconnect.in URLs from bootstrap (never an arbitrary link).

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Google Play Services missing/outdated GATEWAY_ERROR (client-mapped) — Toast "Google Sign-In isn't available on this device. Try phone or email."
User cancels the Google picker — (not an error) — Silently stays on AuthSelect; no toast
Offline, Google tapped NETWORK_OFFLINE (client) — Google button shows "Needs internet"; phone/email still work
Both email and Google disabled by admin — (config) — Divider and email link hidden; only the phone button renders

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T3.1 All three methods enabled → all three controls visible in BR-3.2 order; Maestro flow auth_select_all_methods.
  • T3.2 auth.google_login_enabled = false → Google button hidden, phone and email still shown.
  • T3.3 auth.email_login_enabled = false and Google disabled → only the phone button and legal footer render.
  • T3.4 Tap "Continue with phone number" → lands on PhoneEntry with an empty field.
  • T3.5 Tap "Continue with Google", complete picker with an existing account's email → lands on role tabs.
  • T3.6 Tap "Continue with Google", cancel the native picker → remains on AuthSelect, no error toast.
  • T3.7 Tap "Sign in with email instead" → lands on EmailEntry.
  • T3.8 Tap "Terms of Service" → in-app browser opens legal.termsUrl; back button returns to AuthSelect without navigating away from the app.
  • T3.9 Airplane mode → phone/email buttons still navigate; Google button shows "Needs internet" and is disabled.
  • T3.10 Android back on AuthSelect → toast "Press back again to exit"; second back within 2 s exits the app.

20. Audit Log Events

None. No account or server data changes on this screen — the eventual sign-in (Google) is audited by M04, not here.

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Apple Sign-In alongside Google once the iOS App Store guideline requirement is confirmed to apply (mandatory when any third-party social login is offered).
  • WhatsApp OTP as a channel alongside SMS (schema already supports channel = 'whatsapp' on otp_challenges) if SMS delivery cost or reliability becomes an issue.
  • Remember the last successful method per install (useAppFlags.lastAuthMethod) and visually promote it to the top on return visits.
  • Single Tap / One Tap Google prompt (no button press) for returning Google users, once product wants a more aggressive default.

Module 4 · Login

Phase 1 · App Foundation · Used by: All (signed out) · Depends on: M00 (session storage, device registration), M03 (entry screens), M05 (registration handoff); Admin M01 (rotation/reuse-detection pattern this module mirrors) · New tables: otp_challenges, app_sessions, user_auth_identities · Uses: app_users, user_devices · Build estimate: 6–7 days

1. Module Purpose

Every way into a GuruConnect account: phone OTP (the default and only method that cannot be disabled), email + password, email OTP for people who forget their password or haven't set one, Google Sign-In with server-side ID-token verification, and the session machinery every other module relies on — refresh with rotation and theft detection, logout, logout-all, and a sessions list. It owns the three identity tables (otp_challenges, app_sessions, user_auth_identities) and decides, for every successful credential check, whether the phone/email belongs to an existing account (log in) or not (hand back a 30-minute registrationToken for M05). It also detects and explains ROLE_MISMATCH when a sign-in was entered from a role-specific context that doesn't match the account found.

2. User Stories

  • As a new parent, I want to type my phone number, get a 6-digit code by SMS, and be either signed in or moved straight to registration, so that I never have to think about "do I have an account already?".
  • As a teacher without cell signal on the school Wi-Fi, I want to sign in with email and password so that I'm not blocked by SMS delivery.
  • As a returning user who forgot their password, I want to reset it with an OTP emailed to me, without calling support.
  • As a user who tapped a teacher-referral link intending to join as a teacher, I want to be told clearly if that phone already has a Parent account, and be offered to continue as a parent instead of silently landing in the wrong app experience.
  • As a security-conscious user, I want to see every device I'm signed in on and sign one out, so that a lost phone doesn't keep my account open.
  • As product, I want a stolen refresh token to be useless the moment it's replayed, so that a leaked token from an old device backup can't quietly re-enter an account.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-4.1 Phone OTP request. POST /auth/otp/request { phone }.

  1. Normalise to E.164 (+91##########); reject non-Indian numbers in v1 (VALIDATION_FAILED).
  2. Resend guard: if an unconsumed otp_challenges row exists for (destination = phone, purpose = 'login') created less than auth.otp_resend_after_seconds (30 s) ago, return 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After = remaining seconds — no new SMS is sent.
  3. Hourly guard: count challenges for this destination in the last hour; at auth.otp_max_per_hour (5) → 429 OTP_LOCKED "Too many codes requested. Try again in an hour."; a secondary IP guard (20/hour per IP) catches spraying across numbers.
  4. Generate a code of auth.otp_length (6) digits, HMAC-SHA256 it with a server-side pepper into code_hash (raw code never stored or logged), insert otp_challenges (channel='sms', purpose='login', destination=phone, expires_at = now() + auth.otp_ttl_seconds (5 min), ip_address, install_id from X-Install-Id), send via the SMS provider (MSG91/Gupshup), store provider_message_id.
  5. Response: { challengeId, expiresInSeconds: 300, resendAfterSeconds: 30 }. In non-production builds, numbers +91 90000 0000x are test-mode and the code is always 123456 (conventions §16); real SMS is never sent for these. BR-4.2 OTP verify (channel-agnostic — used for phone SMS and email OTP alike). POST /auth/otp/verify { challengeId, code, intendedRole? }.
  6. Load the challenge; NOT FOUND or already consumed_at → 410 OTP_EXPIRED. Past expires_at → 410 OTP_EXPIRED.
  7. Compare code_hash. Wrong code → attempts += 1; at attempts = 5 set consumed_at = now() (the challenge is burned) and return 429 OTP_LOCKED "Too many wrong attempts. Request a new code."; below 5 → 422 OTP_INVALID with the attempts remaining in details.attemptsLeft.
  8. Correct code → verified_at = now(), consumed_at = now() (single use).
  9. Resolve the account: for channel = 'sms', look up user_auth_identities where provider = 'phone', provider_subject = destination, deleted_at IS NULL; for channel = 'email', provider = 'password' or any identity whose email = destination (a phone-first user who later added the same email is still "found").
  10. No account found → issue a registrationToken (BR-4.8) with contactType matching the channel and subject = destination; response 409 REGISTRATION_REQUIRED { registrationToken, contactType, expiresInSeconds: 1800 }. The app routes to M05.
  11. Account found → account_status check: suspended/banned → 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED with the reason and any until date; otherwise apply the role-mismatch check (BR-4.11); on a match (or no intendedRole sent), issue a session (BR-4.9, auth_method='otp') and return it plus the /me-shaped user summary (BR-0.12). BR-4.3 Email + password login. POST /auth/email/login { email, password, intendedRole? }. Rate limit 8/minute per (IP, email). Load user_auth_identities where provider='password', provider_subject = lower(email), deleted_at IS NULL. Not found → run a dummy Argon2id verify (constant time) and return 401 AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS "Email or password is incorrect." (never reveals which is wrong, never distinguishes "no account" here — a user with no password identity is told the same thing and pointed to "Forgot password?", which itself never confirms account existence). locked_until > now() → 423-mapped as 429 OTP_LOCKED-style lockout using the same AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED-shaped payload as Admin M01 (details.lockedUntil). Verify Argon2id (m=19456, t=2, p=1); wrong → failed_attempts += 1, at 5 set locked_until = now() + 15 min, return AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS. Correct → reset failed_attempts, last_used_at = now(), role-mismatch check (BR-4.11), issue session auth_method='password'. BR-4.4 Email OTP request (passwordless path — forgotten password, or a user who registered by email OTP and never set one). POST /auth/email/otp/request { email }. Same resend/hourly guards as BR-4.1 but keyed on (destination=email, purpose='login'), channel='email', delivered via SES. Deliberately does not reveal whether the email has an account — same response shape whether it does or not — so this doubles safely as the entry point for a brand-new email-based sign-up. Verification is the same POST /auth/otp/verify as phone (BR-4.2); an email-OTP login always sets auth_method='email_otp' on the resulting session. BR-4.5 Forgot password. POST /auth/password/forgot { email }. Always sends an OTP if a password identity exists for that email (silently no-ops otherwise) and always returns the same 202-style body { sent: true } — no account enumeration. Challenge: channel='email', purpose='reset_password'. Same rate limits as BR-4.4. BR-4.6 Reset password. POST /auth/password/reset { challengeId, code, newPassword }. Verifies the challenge inline (same wrong-code/expiry rules as BR-4.2, purpose must be reset_password, single use) — this endpoint does its own verification rather than calling /auth/otp/verify first, because a successful verify here must not create a session or registration token. On success: policy-check newPassword (8–72 chars, at least one letter and one digit, must not equal the local part of the email or the phone on file), set a new Argon2id hash on the password identity (password_updated_at = now(), failed_attempts = 0, locked_until = null), and revoke every app_sessions row for that user (revoked_reason='password_changed') so a device that stole the old password is signed out everywhere; send a "Your password was changed" email/push. If the identity doesn't exist yet (email-OTP-only user resetting for the first time), this call creates the password identity instead of updating one, linked to the same user_id found via the email's other identities. BR-4.7 Google Sign-In. POST /auth/google { idToken, intendedRole? }. Server verifies the token: signature against Google's published JWKS, iss = accounts.google.com or https://accounts.google.com, aud ∈ the app's Android/iOS/Web OAuth client ids, exp in the future; extract sub, email, email_verified, name, picture. email_verified = false → 422 VALIDATION_FAILED "Verify your Google account's email address first." Lookup user_auth_identities provider='google', provider_subject = sub. Found → role-mismatch check, issue session auth_method='google'. Not found but email matches a different existing identity (phone or password user who used the same email) → auto-link: insert a new provider='google' row onto that same user_id (email = google email), audit app.identity_linked, log in normally. Not found at all → registrationToken with contactType='google', subject = sub, plus prefill: { fullName: name, photoUrl: picture } for M05/M06 to pre-populate the name field. BR-4.8 Registration tokens. JWT, aud = gc-register, 30-minute expiry, claims { sub: <verified phone|email|google-sub>, contactType: 'phone'|'email'|'google', prefill?, iat, exp }. Stateless — no DB row — so it is naturally single-purpose (M05/M06/M11/M14/M21 only accept this audience) and expires on its own; there is nothing to revoke server-side, so a user who abandons registration simply gets a new one by verifying again. BR-4.9 Session issuance (issueSession, shared helper called by this module and by M06/M11/M14/M21 at the end of registration). In one transaction: update the identity's last_used_at; resolve role = app_users.user_type and pid = the id in the matching role table (parents/students/teachers/institute_managers) by user_id (for a brand-new registration this row was just inserted by the caller); look up an existing user_devices row for (user_id, install_id) — if present, use its id as device_id, else leave device_id null (it is attached on the next PUT /devices/me, M00 BR-0.6); generate a 256-bit random refresh token and a new token_family (new family per login, not per device — so logout-all and reuse-detection scope correctly to "everywhere this user is signed in", not just one device lineage); insert app_sessions (refresh_token_hash = sha256(token), expires_at = now() + 60 days, auth_method); mint the access JWT (RS256, 15 min, aud=gc-app, claims sub, role, pid, iid (institute id, staff only), sid = app_sessions.id). Response returns { accessToken, expiresIn: 900, refreshToken, session: { id }, user: <same shape as GET /me, M00 BR-0.12> }. BR-4.10 Refresh with rotation and reuse detection. POST /auth/refresh { refreshToken } (no access token required — this is how an expired one is replaced).
  12. Hash the presented token and look it up by the unique index on app_sessions.refresh_token_hash.
  13. Found, not revoked, not expired → this is the current, valid token for its session: update that same row's refresh_token_hash to a freshly generated token (rotation is an in-place update, not a new row — one row per signed-in device for the life of the session), bump last_used_at, extend the sliding window (expires_at = min(created_at + 60 days, now() + 30 days)). Before overwriting, cache redis SET rt:used:<old_hash> = token_family EX 86400 (24 h grace/detection window). Mint a new access token from the same claims. Return the new pair.
  14. Not found by hash → check redis GET rt:used:<hash>. Present → this exact token was already rotated out once and is being replayed (theft signal): revoke every app_sessions row in that token_family (revoked_reason='reuse_detected'), delete the family's active devices' push ability is unaffected (devices stay registered, only sessions die), send a "We signed you out everywhere for your security" push/email, audit app.token_reuse_detected, return 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID. Absent → token is simply unknown/garbage (expired-and-purged, or forged): plain 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID, no special handling (indistinguishable from reuse to the caller, by design — only the server-side audit trail tells them apart).
  15. Revoked (revoked_at set, e.g. by logout/logout-all/password change) → 401 AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID, no special messaging beyond conventions §5's generic "Please sign in again."
  16. Nightly job hard-deletes app_sessions rows revoked or expired more than 30 days ago and otp_challenges rows older than 24 h (cleanup exemption to soft-delete-everywhere, per conventions §12). BR-4.11 ROLE_MISMATCH. Some entry points carry an intendedRole (parent|student|teacher|institute_staff) alongside the credential — the two current sources are an institute's "invite a teacher" SMS/email link (gc://r/<code> opened with a stored pendingDeepLink that implies teacher) and a role-specific referral code validated at M05. When intendedRole is present on otp/verify, email/login or google, and an existing account is found whose app_users.user_type differs from it, the session is not issued; the API returns 409 ROLE_MISMATCH { details: { actualRole: 'parent' } } instead. The app shows "This phone number already has a Parent account — continue as Parent?" with buttons "Continue as Parent" (re-submits the same verified challenge/credential with intendedRole omitted, which always succeeds) and "Use a different number/account". Without intendedRole (the overwhelming majority of logins — plain AuthSelect entry), the account's real role is simply used; mismatch can never happen. BR-4.12 Logout / logout-all. POST /auth/logout (Any user): revokes the caller's own session (sid from the access token, revoked_reason='logout'); the app then calls M00 DELETE /devices/me and clears local state (conventions §7). POST /auth/logout-all (Any user): revokes every non-revoked app_sessions row for the user (revoked_reason='logout_all'), including the caller's own — the app must treat its own next request as signed-out immediately rather than waiting for a 401. BR-4.13 Sessions list and single revoke. GET /auth/sessions (Any user): active (revoked_at IS NULL, expires_at > now()) sessions for the caller, joined to user_devices via device_id for a device label (platform + model) when linked, else "Unknown device"; flags isCurrent by comparing sid. DELETE /auth/sessions/:id (Any user, ownership enforced — user_id = sub): revokes that one session (revoked_reason='logout'); revoking the current session behaves like /auth/logout. BR-4.14 Combined abuse/lockout limits (reference table).
Mechanism Table.column Limit Effect
OTP resend cooldown otp_challenges (by destination+purpose) 30 s (auth.otp_resend_after_seconds) 429 RATE_LIMITED, Retry-After
OTP requests per hour otp_challenges count 5 (auth.otp_max_per_hour) 429 OTP_LOCKED
OTP wrong-code attempts otp_challenges.attempts 5 429 OTP_LOCKED, challenge burned
OTP validity otp_challenges.expires_at 5 min (auth.otp_ttl_seconds) 410 OTP_EXPIRED
Password wrong attempts user_auth_identities.failed_attempts 5 locked_until = +15 min, AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS
Email/password login rate per (IP, email) 8/min 429 RATE_LIMITED
Refresh reuse Redis rt:used:<hash> any replay whole token_family revoked

4. Screen List

Screen Route name Purpose
Phone entry PhoneEntry Collect and submit the phone number
OTP verify OtpVerify 6-digit code entry with autofill, used for phone and email
Email entry EmailEntry Email + password, with a link to email-OTP instead
Forgot password ForgotPassword Collect email to send a reset OTP
Reset password ResetPassword Enter the OTP and a new password together
Active sessions ActiveSessions List signed-in devices; sign one (or all) out

5. Screen Flow & Navigation

Diagram loads when this page is online…

Back from OtpVerify returns to PhoneEntry/EmailEntry and offers "Resend code" only after the 30-second cooldown. ResetPassword success returns to EmailEntry with a success toast, not straight into a session (the user signs in explicitly with the new password, confirming they remember it).

6. Screen Wireframe Description

PhoneEntry — heading "What's your number?", PhoneField (fixed "+91" prefix, 10-digit input, numeric keyboard), helper text "We'll text you a code to confirm it's you.", sticky button "Send code" (disabled until 10 digits entered).

OtpVerify — heading "Enter the code", subtext "Sent to +91 98765 43210" (masked destination shown in full here since the user just entered it), OtpInput (6 cells, autofill via SMS Retriever on Android / textContentType="oneTimeCode" on iOS), inline error under the cells on wrong code ("Incorrect code. 3 attempts left."), text link "Resend code" (greyed with a 30 s countdown, then active), sticky button "Verify" (also auto-submits on the 6th digit).

EmailEntry — heading "Sign in with email", TextField email (keyboard type email, autocomplete), TextField password (secure entry, eye toggle), text link "Forgot password?" right-aligned under the password field, sticky button "Sign in"; below a divider, text link "Sign in with a one-time code instead" (switches the screen into email-OTP mode: password field hides, button becomes "Send code").

ForgotPassword — heading "Reset your password", body "Enter the email on your account. We'll send you a code.", TextField email, sticky button "Send code".

ResetPassword — heading "Check your email", subtext "Enter the code and a new password.", OtpInput (6 cells), TextField new password (secure entry, live strength hint: "8+ characters, letters and numbers"), sticky button "Reset password".

ActiveSessions — list of SessionRow cards: device label ("Android · SM-A546E" or "Unknown device"), "This device" badge on the current one, last active ("Active now" / "2 days ago"), IP city if resolvable, trailing "Sign out" text button per row (hidden on the current row, which instead shows nothing destructive inline); bottom of the list, a plain-text danger link "Sign out of all devices" opens a ConfirmSheet ("This signs you out everywhere, including this device.").

PhoneEntryScreen        → PhoneField, StickyActionBar("Send code")
OtpVerifyScreen         → OtpInput(autofill), ResendLink(countdown), StickyActionBar("Verify")
EmailEntryScreen        → TextField×2, TextLink("Forgot password?"), ModeToggle(password|otp), StickyActionBar
ForgotPasswordScreen    → TextField(email), StickyActionBar("Send code")
ResetPasswordScreen     → OtpInput, TextField(newPassword), PasswordStrengthHint, StickyActionBar
ActiveSessionsScreen    → FlashList(SessionRow), ConfirmSheet("Sign out of all devices")

Hooks: usePhoneOtpRequestMutation(), useOtpVerifyMutation(), useEmailLoginMutation(), useEmailOtpRequestMutation(), useForgotPasswordMutation(), useResetPasswordMutation(), useGoogleSignIn() (M03), useSessionsQuery(), useRevokeSessionMutation(id), useLogoutMutation(), useLogoutAllMutation().

8. Validation Rules

Field Rule Message shown
phone ^\+91[6-9]\d{9}$ after normalisation "Enter a valid 10-digit mobile number."
code exactly 6 digits "Enter the 6-digit code."
email RFC-valid, ≤ 254 chars, lower-cased before send "Enter a valid email address."
password (login) 1–128 chars (policy not re-checked at login) "Enter your password."
newPassword 8–72 chars, ≥ 1 letter and ≥ 1 digit, ≠ email local-part/phone "Use 8+ characters with letters and numbers."
challengeId uuid, required on verify/reset — (never shown; carried internally)
idToken non-empty JWT string from the Google SDK "Google Sign-In failed. Try again."
intendedRole one of parent,student,teacher,institute_staff, optional — (internal; never a user-facing field)

9. API Endpoints

Method Path Auth Description
POST /auth/otp/request Public Send a phone OTP (rate limited: 5/hour/phone, 30 s resend)
POST /auth/otp/verify Public Verify a phone or email OTP; logs in, or returns a registrationToken
POST /auth/email/login Public Email + password sign-in (rate limited: 8/min per IP+email)
POST /auth/email/otp/request Public Send an email OTP for passwordless sign-in (same limits as phone)
POST /auth/password/forgot Public Send a password-reset OTP by email (never confirms account existence)
POST /auth/password/reset Public Verify the reset OTP and set a new password; revokes all sessions
POST /auth/google Public Google ID-token sign-in, with auto-link and auto-registration handoff
POST /auth/refresh Public (refresh token) Rotate the refresh token; detects and punishes reuse
POST /auth/logout Any user Revoke the current session
POST /auth/logout-all Any user Revoke every session of this account
GET /auth/sessions Any user List this account's active sessions
DELETE /auth/sessions/:id Any user (owner only) Revoke one session by id

CREATE TABLE otp_challenges (

  user_id uuid REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Known user, if any
  attempts smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (attempts BETWEEN 0 AND 5), -- Wrong-code attempts
  resend_count smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Resends of this challenge

  ip_address inet, -- Requesting IP

Existing tables this module reads or writes (full definitions in the owning module)

Table Owner Purpose
app_users Admin M00 Login identity for every mobile app account (parent, student, teacher, institute staff). Role profiles hang off this table.
user_devices App M00 Every app install a user has signed in on, with its FCM token. One row per (user, install).
  • otp_challenges: this module is the sole writer. purpose used here: login (phone/email OTP sign-in), reset_password. destination is always normalised (E.164 phone or lower-case email) before insert so lookups by (destination, purpose) are exact-match. attempts and resend_count are read on every request to enforce BR-4.14; consumed_at makes every challenge single-use regardless of outcome. M06/M11/M14/M21 also write here with purpose='signup' when a registration form needs to verify a second contact (e.g. a parent who registered by email adding a mandatory mobile number) — this module's verify endpoint treats purpose='signup' identically to login except that it does not issue a session or registration token; it just marks the challenge verified for the calling registration endpoint to check.
  • app_sessions: one row per signed-in device for the life of that sign-in; refresh rotation updates the row in place (BR-4.10) rather than inserting a new one, so token_family only changes across separate logins, never across refreshes of the same login.
  • user_auth_identities: a single user_id may hold up to three rows (phone, password, google), added over time via this module (BR-4.7 auto-link) and via M51 Account Settings; uq_user_auth_identities_subject keeps a phone/email/Google-sub from being claimed by two live accounts at once.
  • app_users: account_status is read on every login (suspended/banned block sign-in); auth_provider is set once at registration to the method first used and is display-only afterwards (all subsequent logins can use any linked identity).
  • user_devices: read (never written) to resolve app_sessions.device_id at issuance time and to render device labels on GET /auth/sessions.

14. State Management

  • useSession (Zustand, memory; owned by M00): populated by every successful login/refresh/registration with { accessToken, role, userId, profileId, instituteId }.
  • Local per-screen form state (React Hook Form) for phone/email/code/password fields; not persisted (secure, one-time entry).
  • sessionKeys.list (TanStack Query) — GET /auth/sessions, staleTime 0 (always refetch on ActiveSessions focus), invalidated after useRevokeSessionMutation and useLogoutAllMutation.
  • No query is persisted from this module (meta: { persist: false } on every mutation and on sessionKeys.list — session data must never sit in the offline cache, per M00 BR-0.4).

15. Offline Handling

Everything here is online only (conventions §8 class 3): OTP send/verify, password login, Google, refresh, logout, session revoke. Every button on every screen in this module is disabled with "Needs internet" when NetInfo reports no connection; there is nothing to queue — a stale credential attempt replayed later would be confusing and insecure. GET /auth/sessions is not persisted and simply shows a loading/error state offline rather than stale device data.

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
Password changed Account owner "Your password was changed" / "If this wasn't you, contact support immediately." gc://account/security account yes
Signed out everywhere (reuse detected) Account owner "We signed you out for your security" / "A sign-in token was reused from another device. Please sign in again." gc://login account yes
New device signed in (optional, only when > 1 active session already existed) Account owner "New sign-in to your account" / "{deviceLabel} · {city}" gc://account/security account no

17. Security Rules

  • OTP codes are never logged, returned in any response, or written to audit_logs/Sentry; only code_hash exists at rest.
  • Argon2id for both admin-mirrored password hashing here; passwords are never logged, and VALIDATION_FAILED responses never echo the submitted password back.
  • Refresh tokens live only in expo-secure-store on the device and as a SHA-256 hash server-side (conventions §6); the raw value is never in a query string, log line or analytics event.
  • Every login flow enforces ownership implicitly (a session's claims are the only source of user_id/role/pid for every other module — never trust a body-supplied id).
  • PhoneEntry, OtpVerify, EmailEntry (password mode), ForgotPassword, ResetPassword are FLAG_SECURE screens (credentials on screen).
  • Constant-time comparison for both OTP hash and password hash checks; unknown email/phone and wrong password/code return visually identical errors (no account enumeration).
  • Rate limits in BR-4.14 apply per destination and per IP so a single attacker can't spread attempts across many numbers from one connection, nor hammer one number from many.

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
OTP resent before cooldown RATE_LIMITED 429 Resend link stays disabled with the returned Retry-After countdown
Too many OTP requests/hour OTP_LOCKED 429 "Too many codes requested. Try again in an hour."
Wrong OTP code OTP_INVALID 422 Inline error under the code cells, attempts-left shown
OTP expired OTP_EXPIRED 410 "This code has expired." + auto-focus "Resend code"
5 wrong OTP attempts OTP_LOCKED 429 "Too many wrong attempts. Request a new code."; Verify button disabled, must go back and resend
Wrong email/password AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS 401 "Email or password is incorrect." under the password field
Password locked (5 fails) AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED 423 "Too many attempts. Try again after {time}."
Account suspended/banned ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED 403 Blocking screen (M00) with reason and support link
Role differs from intended context ROLE_MISMATCH 409 RoleMismatchSheet — "Continue as {actualRole}" or switch account
No account on OTP/Google verify REGISTRATION_REQUIRED 409 Routes to M05 with the returned registrationToken
Google email not verified VALIDATION_FAILED 422 "Verify your Google account's email address first."
Refresh token revoked/reused/unknown AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID 401 Clear session → AuthSelect, "Please sign in again."
Reset OTP wrong/expired OTP_INVALID / OTP_EXPIRED 422 / 410 Inline under the code cells on ResetPassword
New password fails policy VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Inline under the field, live checklist

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T4.1 Phone OTP happy path: request → SMS test code 123456 on a test number → verify → existing user → role tabs. Maestro flow login_phone_otp.
  • T4.2 Phone OTP, unknown number → REGISTRATION_REQUIRED with a registrationToken → lands on M05.
  • T4.3 Wrong OTP code 5 times → OTP_LOCKED, Verify disabled, "Resend code" required to try again.
  • T4.4 Resend tapped at 20 s → RATE_LIMITED; at 31 s → new SMS sent, old challenge's remaining attempts irrelevant (new challengeId).
  • T4.5 Email + password happy path with an existing password identity → role tabs.
  • T4.6 5 wrong passwords → AUTH_ACCOUNT_LOCKED with a countdown; correct password before the countdown ends is still rejected.
  • T4.7 "Forgot password" → OTP emailed → ResetPassword with correct code and a valid new password → success toast → EmailEntry; old sessions on another test device are now signed out (refresh fails with AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID).
  • T4.8 Google Sign-In with an email matching an existing phone-registered parent → auto-linked, logs in, user_auth_identities gains a google row; second Google sign-in with the same account reuses it (no duplicate row, uq_user_auth_identities_subject).
  • T4.9 Institute teacher-invite deep link (intendedRole=teacher) verified against a phone that already has a Parent account → ROLE_MISMATCH sheet → "Continue as Parent" logs in as the parent.
  • T4.10 Refresh rotation: refresh once → success, new token; replay the old token → AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID and every session in that family is revoked (assert via GET /auth/sessions on the other device returning empty/401).
  • T4.11 GET /auth/sessions shows two devices; DELETE /auth/sessions/:otherId revokes only that one; the calling device's session and query cache are untouched.
  • T4.12 POST /auth/logout-all from device A → device B's next /auth/refresh returns AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID.
  • T4.13 Airplane mode on every screen in this module → all primary buttons disabled with "Needs internet"; no request is queued.

20. Audit Log Events

Event When Details
app.login_succeeded Any successful login method, ip, device
app.login_failed Wrong password/OTP, account locked method, reason, ip (no phone/email/code)
app.identity_linked Google auto-linked to an existing account provider, user id
app.logout / app.logout_all Explicit sign-out session id(s)
app.session_revoked DELETE /auth/sessions/:id session id
app.token_reuse_detected Refresh replay detected token family, sessions revoked count
app.password_reset Reset completed sessions revoked count (no password)

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Move JWT signing to a KMS-backed key with kid rotation and a JWKS endpoint, matching Admin M01's future notes.
  • WhatsApp as a third OTP channel (schema-ready, otp_challenges.channel = 'whatsapp') where SMS deliverability is poor.
  • Device attestation (Play Integrity / App Attest) gating /auth/otp/request and /auth/google to cut scripted OTP abuse further than rate limits alone.
  • Step-up re-authentication (short-lived "sensitive action" token) before payment method changes or account deletion, instead of relying solely on the 15-minute access token's age.
  • Passkeys (WebAuthn) as a fourth identity provider once React Native support is mature enough for a 2 GB RAM Android baseline.

Module 5 · Registration

Phase 1 · App Foundation · Used by: Registration token · Depends on: M04 (issues the registrationToken this whole module requires), M00 (masters, uploads for later steps) · New tables: none · Uses: app_users, user_consents, referral_codes · Build estimate: 2–3 days

1. Module Purpose

The router a brand-new user lands on right after M04 verifies their phone, email or Google account and finds no existing app_users row. It has no role of its own — it lets the person choose Parent, Student, Teacher or Institute, tells the chosen role's screen (M06/M11/M14/M21) everything it needs to prefill (verified contact, Google name/photo, a referral code from a deep link), validates a referral code before it's submitted, and defines the one contract every role's submit endpoint follows: capture terms/privacy consent in the same transaction that creates the account, and let the form survive the app being killed mid-fill.

2. User Stories

  • As a new user who just verified their phone, I want to be asked once, plainly, "Who are you signing up as?" so that I'm not shown irrelevant fields for a role I'm not.
  • As a user who opened an institute's referral link, I want my referral code already filled in so that I don't have to type or remember it.
  • As a teacher filling a long registration form, I want my progress saved if I get a call and the app gets killed, so that I don't start over.
  • As legal/compliance, I want every account creation to record exactly which version of the Terms and Privacy Policy was agreed to, so that we can answer a DPDP Act data request.
  • As a low-connectivity student, I want the role choice and referral check to work even on a bad connection, so that a slow 2G moment doesn't strand me on this screen.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-5.1 Entry. The only way to reach this module is holding a registrationToken (M04 BR-4.8, aud=gc-register, 30 min). Every endpoint here — and every role's submit endpoint in M06/M11/M14/M21 — verifies that audience and rejects anything else with 401 AUTH_REQUIRED. An expired token routes back to M04's entry screen with "That took a while — let's verify your number again." BR-5.2 GET /registration/context. Returns everything the role-picker and the next form need without another round trip: contactType and the verified value (phone shown in full since the user just typed it, email likewise), prefill (from Google, if contactType='google': fullName, photoUrl), the four role tiles with a one-line description each, the current legal.termsUrl/version and privacyUrl/version (mirrors M01 bootstrap's legal block so this screen doesn't need a second bootstrap fetch), and referralCode pre-filled from useAppFlags.pendingDeepLink if it matches /r/<code> (BR-5.3 still re-validates it before use — a stored deep link is a hint, not a fact). BR-5.3 POST /registration/referral/validate { code }. Looks up referral_codes case-insensitively (upper(code)), is_active = true, not expired (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()); for a personal code checks the owner's account is not suspended; for a campaign code checks its usage_limit hasn't been reached (count of referrals rows against it, read via M42's helper — this module never writes referrals, only previews). No program_code filter is applied here — a TEACHER_REFERRAL code is shown as valid even before the user has picked "Teacher", since the role tiles haven't been chosen yet; the role-specific submit endpoint (M06/M11/M14/M21) does the final program-match check when the referral is actually recorded. Response: { valid: true, programCode, ownerFirstName } (masked, e.g. "Lakshmi") or { valid: false, reason } with reason ∈ invalid|expired|limit_reached|disabled — never a hard error, so the UI can show an inline message and let the user continue without a code. BR-5.4 Role choice is client-only. There is no POST /registration/role — tapping a tile just navigates to that role's own stack (M06/M11/M14/M21), carrying the registrationToken, the validated referralCode (or none), and any prefill forward as route params. If the user backs out and picks a different tile, nothing server-side needs to be undone (no state was created yet). BR-5.5 Shared draft persistence contract. Every role's multi-field form (all four; Parent's is short but still covered) saves its in-progress values to useRegistrationDraft(role) — Zustand + encrypted MMKV, keyed registrationDraft:<role>:<registrationTokenSubjectHash> so a draft never leaks across a different verified contact reusing the app. The draft is written on every field blur (debounced 500 ms), restored on screen mount, and cleared only on a successful submit (BR-5.6) — an error leaves the draft intact so the user can retry without retyping. Drafts older than 24 h are ignored and cleared (the registrationToken they belong to would be long expired anyway). BR-5.6 Shared consent contract. Every role's submit endpoint, inside the same database transaction that inserts app_users and the role table, inserts exactly two user_consents rows: consent_type='terms', document_version=<legal.termsVersion at submit time>, granted=true, method='checkbox' and the same for consent_type='privacy_policy', both with ip_address and install_id from the request. document_version is not re-read from the possibly-stale GET /registration/context response the client cached — the server re-reads the live system_settings legal keys at submit time, so a version bump mid-fill is still recorded correctly. Marketing consent, when the form includes an opt-in checkbox, writes a third consent_type='marketing' row with granted matching the checkbox state (a false/declined marketing choice is still recorded — DPDP Act requires proof of the choice either way, not just of consent). BR-5.7 Shared submit order (documented once here, implemented once per role module). 1) Re-verify the registrationToken and re-check the phone/email/Google-sub it names is still unclaimed (CONFLICT_DUPLICATE if another registration on a second device won the race). 2) Re-validate any referralCode against the role's actual program (LEARNER_REFERRAL for Parent/Student, TEACHER_REFERRAL for Teacher, INSTITUTE_REFERRAL for Institute) — a code valid for the wrong program is simply ignored (referralApplied: false in the response), never a hard error. 3) Insert app_users. 4) Insert the role table row. 5) Insert user_auth_identities row(s) for the method(s) verified. 6) If a referral applied, insert the referrals row (M42 owns that table; this is the one write every registration endpoint makes into it). 7) Insert the consent rows (BR-5.6). 8) Call M04's issueSession helper (BR-4.9) — Parent and Student land signed in immediately; Teacher and Institute also get a session (so they can resume registration if the app is killed) but their /me.registration.nextStep is non-null until documents/verification are done. 9) Clear the local draft (BR-5.5) and fire app.<role>_registered audit + analytics. BR-5.8 One contact, one account. Because uq_app_users_phone_live and uq_user_auth_identities_subject are both partial-unique on live rows, step 1 of BR-5.7 is a belt-and-braces re-check, not the only guard — a genuine race (two devices submitting the same phone within the same second) is caught by the database constraint and surfaces as 409 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE either way.

5. Screen Flow & Navigation

Diagram loads when this page is online…

Back from RegistrationRouter returns to M04's entry screen (AuthSelect), discarding the registration token — the user must verify their contact again to return here, which is intentional friction against abandoned-then-retried sign-ups piling up half-typed drafts.

6. Screen Wireframe Description

RegistrationRouter — heading "Welcome! Who's signing up?", subtext "You verified {maskedContact}." Four large tappable tiles, each with an icon, title and one line: "Parent — Find a teacher for your child", "Student — Find a teacher for yourself (18+, or with a parent's OK)", "Teacher — Get discovered by families near you", "Institute — List your coaching centre or school". Below the tiles, a plain-text link "Have a referral code?" opening the sheet if no code is already applied; once a code is applied it shows instead as a small dismissible chip "Referral: SCHOOLFAIR26 ✕".

ReferralCodeSheet — bottom sheet, heading "Enter a referral code", TextField (auto-uppercase, placeholder "e.g. LAKSHMI50"), inline status after a 400 ms debounce: green check "Valid — Lakshmi's code" or muted "We couldn't find that code" (never a red error — a bad code is not a form mistake, just informational), sticky button "Apply" (disabled until a code validates, or the sheet can be dismissed with no code at all via an "X").

12. PostgreSQL Tables & Columns

Existing tables this module reads or writes (full definitions in the owning module)

Table Owner Purpose
app_users Admin M00 Login identity for every mobile app account (parent, student, teacher, institute staff). Role profiles hang off this table.
user_consents App M52 Record of every consent given or withdrawn (terms, privacy policy, parental consent, marketing), as required by the DPDP Act 2023.

  • app_users: read-only here (existence checks in BR-5.8); written by the role-specific submit endpoints, not by this module.
  • user_consents: this module owns no writes to it either — BR-5.6/5.7 are the contract M06/M11/M14/M21 implement; this module only reads the live legal versions (via system_settings, not user_consents itself) to hand them to the client for display.
  • referral_codes: read-only lookup in POST /registration/referral/validate; the eventual referrals row is written by whichever role module's submit endpoint applies the code (BR-5.7 step 6), which is why this module lists referral_codes under "uses" but never referrals.

13. Relationships
