Module 33 · Profile Sharing

Phase 7 · Profiles · Used by: Any user (create a share), Public (resolve a shared link) · Depends on: M00 (share sheet plumbing), M31 (teacher profile payload), M32 (institute profile payload), M42 (referral attribution); Admin M42 · New tables: profile_shares · Uses: teachers, institutes, referral_codes · Build estimate: 3–4 days

1. Module Purpose

Lets any user share a teacher's or institute's profile — over WhatsApp or a copied link — as a short, trackable https://gcnt.in/s/<code> URL that resolves to a full Open Graph preview on the web and deep-links straight into the app when installed. It owns profile_shares, counting opens and app installs attributed to each share, and stamps the sharer's own referral code onto the link so a share that leads to a sign-up feeds M42's referral program automatically — sharing and referring are the same action from the user's point of view.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent who found a great tutor, I want to share their profile on our building's WhatsApp group with one tap.
  • As a teacher, I want to share my own profile with prospective parents outside the app.
  • As a friend who receives a shared link but doesn't have the app, I want a clean web preview so I can decide before installing.
  • As a user who shares often, I want my shares to count toward my referral rewards when someone new joins because of them.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-33.1 Creating a share — POST /shares { teacherId | instituteId, channel }. Exactly one of teacherId/instituteId. Generates a short_code — 7 chars, base62, collision-checked against uq_profile_shares_code (retry on the rare collision, expected ~1 in 3.5 trillion at this length so effectively never) — and inserts profile_shares (sharer_user_id = sub, channel, opens = 0, installs = 0). Returns the short URL https://gcnt.in/s/<code>. channel is one of whatsapp (uses react-native-share's WhatsApp target with a prefilled message + link), copy_link (copies to clipboard via expo-clipboard), sms, other (any other native share-sheet target, e.g. email or a different app) — the client tells the server which button was tapped; the server does not infer channel from the request.

BR-33.2 The prefilled message. Client-built from a template, not stored server-side: for a teacher, "Check out {fullName} on GuruConnect — {categoryName}, {subjectNames}, Trust Score {trustScore}. {shortUrl}"; for an institute, "Check out {name} on GuruConnect — rated {overallRating}★. {shortUrl}". Kept under 300 characters (WhatsApp-friendly) and never includes phone numbers or the sharer's own contact details.

BR-33.3 Resolving a share — GET /shares/:code (Public). Looks up profile_shares by short_code; 404 NOT_FOUND (rendered as a generic "This link isn't available" web page, never a raw API error, since this endpoint is hit directly by browsers and WhatsApp's link-preview crawler) for an unknown code or a share whose target teacher/institute has since been deleted. On a valid code:

  1. Increments opens (a single UPDATE ... SET opens = opens + 1, not a per-viewer log — profile_shares counts, it doesn't attribute individual opens beyond that).
  2. If the request's User-Agent matches a known link-preview crawler (WhatsApp, Facebook, Twitter/X, Slack, Google), responds with server-rendered HTML carrying Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url) built from exactly M31 BR-31.3's or M32 BR-32.5's limited public payload — no crawler ever sees more than a signed-out learner would.
  3. Otherwise (a real browser or the app's own deep-link handler), redirects: mobile browser with the app installed → opens the app via the universal/app link (conventions §4 /t/<code> doesn't apply here; the canonical share path is /s/<code> and the app's linking.ts maps it straight to TeacherProfile/InstituteProfile with the resolved teacherId/instituteId) with ?ref=<sharerReferralCode> attached (BR-33.5); mobile browser without the app → a lightweight HTML landing page (logo, the same preview card, "Get the app" store buttons that carry the referral code forward via a deferred-deep-link mechanism, section 21); desktop browser → the same landing page, no store buttons emphasised, "Open in GuruConnect" link that just deep-links (harmless no-op on desktop, matches the mobile-only nature of the app).

BR-33.4 Counting an install. The referral code carried through the store link (BR-33.3) is the same mechanism M42 already uses at registration (referralCode field on POST /registration/*); when a new app_users row is created with a referral_codes.code that traces back to a profile_shares row created by that code's owner within the last 30 days, this module's worker increments that share's installs counter (best-effort attribution, not a hard join — if several shares exist for the same sharer/target pair, the most recent one before the install is credited). This is purely a count for the sharer's own "N people installed from your shares" stat; the actual referral reward logic, fraud scoring and payout are entirely M42's, unchanged.

BR-33.5 Referral code attribution. Every share created by a signed-in user automatically carries that user's own personal referral code (referral_codes row for LEARNER_REFERRAL/TEACHER_REFERRAL/INSTITUTE_REFERRAL per the sharer's user_type, created on first need via M42 FR-42.1 if it doesn't exist yet) appended as ?ref=<code> on every resolved link (BR-33.3 step 3) and embedded in the Open Graph landing page's store buttons. A share created by a user with no personal code yet (e.g. their program is disabled) simply omits ref — the share and its open/install counts still work; only the referral attribution is skipped.

BR-33.6 My shares. GET /shares/me (not in the module map's key list but owned here, alongside the two listed endpoints) returns the caller's own shares — target name/photo, channel, opens, installs, createdAt — so "Share history" under the Profile tab shows what's working. Not paginated beyond a simple 50-row cap (shares are a light-usage feature; a heavy sharer is themselves a signal worth noticing operationally, not a pagination problem in v1).

profile_shares

Each time a user shares a teacher or institute profile, with a short code for attribution.

Column Type Null Default Constraints / References Description
id uuid no gen_random_uuid() PK Primary key

Table constraints: CONSTRAINT ck_profile_shares_target CHECK ((teacher_id IS NULL) <> (institute_id IS NULL))

<details><summary>DDL</summary>

CREATE TABLE profile_shares (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  short_code text NOT NULL, -- 8-char code in the link, e.g. https://gcnt.in/s/k7Qm2xPa
  sharer_user_id uuid REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Who shared (NULL if signed out)
  teacher_id uuid REFERENCES teachers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Shared teacher
  institute_id uuid REFERENCES institutes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Shared institute
  channel text NOT NULL CHECK (channel IN ('whatsapp','copy_link','sms','other')), -- Chosen share target
  opens integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Link opens
  installs integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- Installs attributed
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Shared
  CONSTRAINT ck_profile_shares_target CHECK ((teacher_id IS NULL) <> (institute_id IS NULL))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_profile_shares_code ON profile_shares (short_code);
CREATE INDEX idx_profile_shares_teacher ON profile_shares (teacher_id, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_profile_shares_institute ON profile_shares (institute_id, created_at DESC);

</details>

Indexes: uq_profile_shares_code (unique) on (short_code); idx_profile_shares_teacher on (teacher_id, created_at DESC); idx_profile_shares_institute on (institute_id, created_at DESC)

Existing tables this module reads or writes (full definitions in the owning module)

Table Owner Purpose
teachers Admin M16 Teacher profile and verification state. One row per teacher app account.
institutes Admin M22 Coaching centres, tuition centres, schools and academies. Rated by GuruConnect after verification.
referral_codes Admin M42 One personal referral code per app user.
  • profile_shares: one row per created link; opens/installs are simple counters incremented in place (BR-33.3/33.4), not event logs — kept lightweight since per-open detail isn't a product need in v1.
  • teachers, institutes: read to build the preview payload and prefilled message; the same eligibility as M31/M32 applies (a deleted target resolves to 404, a suspended one still resolves per those modules' own "temporarily unavailable" rule since a share link should behave exactly like a direct profile link).
  • referral_codes: read (and created via M42 FR-42.1 on first need) to attach ?ref= to resolved links (BR-33.5); this module never writes referrals itself — M42 owns that entirely from the existing registration flow.

14. State Management

  • Query keys: shareKeys.history. useCreateShareMutation has no cache dependency (fire-and-open-native-sheet); on success it also invalidates shareKeys.history so a freshly opened ShareHistoryScreen includes it.

15. Offline Handling

  • POST /shares is class 3 (online only) — creating a trackable link needs the server; the button is disabled offline with "Connect to the internet to share."
  • GET /shares/me is a persisted read (class: cached), shows "Updated 2 h ago" offline.
  • GET /shares/:code is a Public web/redirect endpoint, not something the app itself calls offline.

16. Push Notification Requirements

None.

17. Security Rules

  • POST /shares requires the target to exist and not be soft-deleted; it does not require the target to be otherwise "eligible" (BR-27.4/BR-28.2) — a user can still share a profile they already have a relationship with (e.g. a suspended teacher they'd previously booked) since sharing itself is harmless; the resolve step (BR-33.3) is what enforces what a recipient actually sees.
  • Short codes are random (not sequential/guessable) and carry no embedded user data; sharer_user_id is never exposed to the recipient or the crawler preview.
  • Rate limited (30/hour per user) to prevent short-code exhaustion spam; GET /shares/:code is public and cached at the CDN edge for crawler hits only (never for the redirect/deep-link path, which must always see live opens semantics — actually incremented server-side on origin, so the CDN rule is "cache the OG HTML variant, bypass cache for the redirect variant," decided by the User-Agent check in BR-33.3).
  • The web landing page never reveals more than M31 BR-31.3/M32 BR-32.5's limited payload, so a share link can never be used to scrape private profile detail without an app account.

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Neither/both of teacherId/instituteId VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Toast "Something went wrong. Try again."
Target deleted since share creation NOT_FOUND 404 Web page "This link isn't available."; app's own share history still shows the row with the counts it had
Too many shares in an hour RATE_LIMITED 429 Toast "You're sharing a lot right now — try again in a bit."
Network / 5xx creating a share GATEWAY_ERROR / INTERNAL_ERROR 502 / 500 Sheet stays open with Retry; native share not triggered until the link exists

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T33.1 Happy path (Maestro profile_share_happy): open a teacher profile → Share → WhatsApp → native share sheet opens with the correct prefilled message and link.
  • T33.2 GET /shares/:code with a WhatsApp crawler User-Agent returns Open Graph HTML matching M31's limited payload exactly (no extra fields).
  • T33.3 GET /shares/:code from a mobile browser with the app installed deep-links straight to the profile; without the app, shows the landing page with store buttons carrying ?ref=.
  • T33.4 A new sign-up whose referralCode traces to a share created 10 days ago by its owner increments that share's installs; one created 40 days ago is not credited (BR-33.4's 30-day window).
  • T33.5 Sharer with no personal referral code yet (program disabled) still gets a working share link with no ref parameter.
  • T33.6 31st share within an hour → 429.
  • T33.7 Share a target, then it's deleted → GET /shares/:code returns 404 web page; the sharer's ShareHistoryScreen still lists the row (counts frozen at their last value).
  • T33.8 opens increments on each resolve regardless of crawler vs. real browser vs. deep-link path; concurrent resolves don't lose increments (atomic UPDATE ... SET opens = opens + 1).
  • T33.9 Offline: "Share" button disabled with the offline hint; ShareHistoryScreen renders from cache.
  • T33.10 Idempotency-Key replay within 24 h on POST /shares returns the same short code, not a second row.

20. Audit Log Events

None. Sharing is a light user action, not an admin-relevant event; its own counters (opens, installs) are the record, matching conventions §11's "reads and searches are not audit-logged" spirit extended here to shares.

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Deferred deep linking (e.g. Branch.io-style) so a store install truly resumes into the exact shared profile even without a referral code round trip, rather than relying on BR-33.4's registration-time join.
  • Per-share analytics (which channel converts best) once volume justifies a breakdown beyond the two counters.
  • QR codes for offline sharing (a teacher's visiting card, an institute's front-desk poster) generated from the same short codes.
  • Expiring or one-time share links for time-limited promotions, as a expires_at column addition if ever needed.

Module 34 · Teacher Reviews

Phase 8 · Reviews · Used by: Parents and students (write, edit, delete, report); any signed-in user (read); teachers (report reviews on their own profile) · Depends on: M00, M31 (profile entry point), M37/M38 (interaction data), M36 (teacher replies), M49 (blocks); Admin M33, Admin M35, Admin M36 · New tables: none · Uses: teacher_reviews, review_flags, review_moderation_logs, teachers, leads, demo_requests, parent_children, app_users, user_blocks, user_privacy_settings, system_settings, audit_logs · Build estimate: 3–4 days

1. Module Purpose

Lets parents and students rate a teacher (1–5 stars) and write a review after a real interaction, edit it within the edit window, delete it, and report other people's reviews; and lets anyone signed in read a teacher's published reviews with the rating summary. Reviews are the input to the teacher's rating and to the Reviews factor of the Trust Score, so the app enforces eligibility (a completed demo or a lead older than 3 days), sends every new or edited review to the moderation pipeline of Admin M35, and never shows unpublished reviews to anyone but their author. Teachers reply to reviews in M36; institute reviews are M35.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent whose son Aarav finished a demo with Dr. Ananya Iyer, I want to rate her and describe the class so that other parents can decide faster.
  • As a student, I want to fix a typo in my review a month later so that it reads correctly, knowing it will be checked again.
  • As a parent on a patchy 3G connection, I want my half-written review saved on the phone so that I don't lose it when the app closes.
  • As a teacher, I want to report a review from someone who never took a class with me so that moderators remove fake reviews.
  • As a parent browsing teachers, I want to see the rating distribution and read recent reviews with "Took a demo" labels so that I can trust what I read.
  • As a new teacher with no reviews, I want my profile to say "No reviews yet" rather than show a low number so that I am not penalised for being new.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-34.1 Who can review. Role parent or student, app_users.account_status = 'active', role row not suspended. A student whose students.parental_consent is pending or declined cannot review (FORBIDDEN, details.reason = "parental_consent_pending"). One live review per (teacher, author) — enforced by uq_teacher_reviews_author; a second attempt returns CONFLICT_DUPLICATE with details.existingReviewId and the app opens the edit form.

BR-34.2 Eligibility (interaction). The author is eligible when at least one of these exists for teacher_id = :teacherId and requester_user_id = sub:

  1. a demo_requests row with status = 'completed', or
  2. a leads row with deleted_at IS NULL, status <> 'spam', decline_reason not starting with spam, and created_at <= now() - interval '3 days'. If neither exists and reviews.allow_unverified = true (default false), the author may still review and is_verified_interaction = false; otherwise CONFLICT_STATE with details.reason = "no_interaction". If the only lead is younger than 3 days, eligibility returns eligibleFrom = lead created_at + 3 days ("You can review Dr. Ananya Iyer from Tue, 29 Sep"). An existing user_blocks row in either direction between the author and teachers.user_id → BLOCKED.

BR-34.3 Content rules. rating integer 1–5. comment trimmed, limits.review_min_chars (30) to 1,500 characters, at least 5 words, not only emoji or repeated characters. For a parent, childId is optional but must belong to the parent (parent_children.parent_id = pid, not deleted); default = the child on the most recent demo or lead with this teacher. The client warns (does not block) when the text looks like it contains a phone number, email, UPI id or link: "Reviews with phone numbers, emails or links are not published." The server's pipeline flags these (contact_info) and never auto-publishes them.

BR-34.4 Create — server steps (one transaction).

  1. Validate ReviewInputSchema; re-run BR-34.1/34.2 (never trust the eligibility call).
  2. If the author soft-deleted a review of this teacher in the last 30 days (audit_logs action app.review_deleted, entity_id = that review, actor_id = sub) → CONFLICT_STATE, details.reason = "recently_deleted", details.retryAfter. This stops delete-and-repost to reset the edit window or bury a rejection.
  3. Insert teacher_reviews with author_type from the token role, child_id, rating, comment, status = 'pending', auto_flags = '{}', is_verified_interaction from BR-34.2.
  4. Insert audit_logs app.review_created.
  5. After commit, enqueue review:moderate (Admin M35 FR-35.1 pipeline). The pipeline sets spam_score and auto_flags and moves the review to published (score < 0.15, no flags), flagged (≥ 0.85) or leaves it pending for a moderator (target decision within 24 h). Requests carry Idempotency-Key; a replay within 24 h returns the first response.

BR-34.5 Status as seen in the app.

status Author sees Others see Counts in rating
pending "Waiting for approval · usually within 24 hours" nothing no
published "Live" the review yes
flagged "Being checked" the review, unless reviews.hide_when_flagged = true no
rejected "Not published" + reason copy (BR-34.8) + "Edit and resubmit" nothing no
hidden "Removed by GuruConnect" (no edit) nothing no

BR-34.6 Edit. PATCH /reviews/:id with If-Match: <updatedAt>. Allowed when the author owns it, now() <= created_at + reviews.edit_window_days (90) days, and status IN ('pending','published','rejected'); flagged → CONFLICT_STATE details.reason = "under_review"; hidden → CONFLICT_STATE details.reason = "removed"; window passed → CONFLICT_STATE details.reason = "edit_window_closed". In one transaction: update rating/comment/child_id, set edited_at = now(), status = 'pending', spam_score = NULL, auto_flags = '{}', rejection_reason_code = NULL; if the previous status was published, recompute teachers.rating_avg/rating_count (Admin M33 FR-33.2 ReviewRatingService.recompute(teacherId)) and enqueue trust recalculation (review_removed); audit app.review_edited with old/new rating (text lengths only); then enqueue review:moderate. The teacher's reply stays attached. The form tells the author: "Your updated review will be checked again before it appears."

BR-34.7 Delete. DELETE /reviews/:id (author only, any status except hidden): set deleted_at; if it was published, recompute the rating cache and enqueue trust recalculation (review_removed) in the same transaction; audit app.review_deleted. Confirmation sheet first. Open review_flags on a deleted review are left for moderators.

BR-34.8 Rejection reasons shown to the author (codes from Admin M35): CONTACT_DETAILS "Remove phone numbers, emails or links, then submit again." · ABUSIVE "Please keep it respectful and remove offensive words." · NOT_A_TEACHING_EXPERIENCE "Reviews should describe classes or demos with this teacher." · FAKE_OR_PAID "We couldn't confirm this review is genuine." · DUPLICATE "This looks like a copy of another review." · PERSONAL_INFORMATION "Remove personal details such as addresses or a child's school." · LEGAL_REQUEST "This review was removed after a legal request." · OTHER "It didn't meet our review guidelines." A moderator note shared by the admin arrives in the rejection notification body.

BR-34.9 Report a review. POST /reviews/:id/report { reason, details }. Reporters: any learner (on any published or flagged review) and the reviewed teacher (on reviews of their own profile only). Not allowed on your own review (FORBIDDEN). One report per reporter per review (uq_review_flags_reporter → CONFLICT_DUPLICATE). Max 10 reports per user per day (LIMIT_REACHED, details.reason = "reports_daily"). In one transaction: insert review_flags (review_type = 'teacher', status = 'open'); if the review is published and now has ≥ 3 open flags, set status = 'flagged', insert review_moderation_logs (target = 'review', action = 'flagged', from_status = 'published', to_status = 'flagged', note = '3 user reports', admin_id = NULL), recompute the rating cache and enqueue trust recalculation; audit app.review_reported. The reporter sees "Thanks. Our team will look at this review." — outcome is not reported back in v1.

BR-34.10 Reading reviews. GET /teachers/:id/reviews returns a summary (cached teachers.rating_avg, rating_count, distribution 5→1, averages by author type) and published reviews (plus flagged ones when hide_when_flagged = false), cursor-paginated 20 per page, sort = recent | highest | lowest, optional rating (1–5) and withReply=true. The viewer's own review (any status except deleted) is returned separately in data.mine so it can be pinned on top. Author display: first name + last initial ("Lakshmi V."); first name only when user_privacy_settings.show_last_name = false; label "Parent · Class 12" (child's class, never the child's name) or "Student · Class 11". is_verified_interaction shows a "Took a demo / Contacted via GuruConnect" tick. Published replies (reply_status = 'published') appear under the review. Teachers with rating_count = 0 show "No reviews yet" — never "0.0".

BR-34.11 My reviews. GET /me/reviews lists all reviews the user wrote (teacher and institute reviews, type field) with status, reason copy and editableUntil (created_at + edit_window_days), newest first.

BR-34.12 Review prompts. 24 h after a demo becomes completed (M38) and 4 days after a lead is created, a job sends a "How was it?" notification if the user is eligible, has no review for that teacher and the lead is not spam (dedupe key review_prompt:<userId>:<teacherId>; at most one prompt per teacher, ever).

If-Match (edit) equals current updatedAt "Updated on another device. Review and save again."
report.reason fake, abusive, personal_details, off_topic, spam, other "Pick a reason."
report.details 0–500 chars; 10–500 when reason = other "Tell us a little more (at least 10 characters)."

14. State Management

  • Query keys (reviewKeys): reviewKeys.teacherList(teacherId, filters), reviewKeys.eligibility(teacherId), reviewKeys.mine(). The first page of teacherList and mine are persisted; eligibility is not (persist: false, staleTime 0).
  • useReviewDraftStore (Zustand + encrypted MMKV): { drafts: Record<teacherId, { rating, childId, comment, updatedAt }>, saveDraft(), clearDraft() }; debounced save 500 ms; cleared on successful submit.
  • After create/edit: invalidate reviewKeys.teacherList(teacherId), reviewKeys.mine(), reviewKeys.eligibility(teacherId), teacherKeys.detail(teacherId) (M31). After delete: same plus optimistic removal from mine (rolled back on error). After report: mark the card locally as "Reported" (no refetch).
  • No optimistic insert of a new review into the public list (it is pending).

15. Offline Handling

  • Read: the teacher's first reviews page and "My reviews" render from cache with "Updated 2 h ago".
  • Write review / edit: class 2 save draft, submit online — the draft survives restarts; the submit button is disabled offline with the hint above.
  • Delete and report: online only (buttons disabled offline with "Connect to the internet to do this.").

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
review_published Author "Your review is live" / "Thanks, {firstName}! Your review of {teacherName} is now on their profile." /me/reviews reviews No
review_rejected Author "Your review needs a change" / "Your review of {teacherName} wasn't published: {reasonText}" /me/reviews reviews No
review_prompt Parent / student (BR-34.12) "How was {teacherName}?" / "Share a quick review to help other parents choose." /t/{publicCode}?action=review reviews No

The two moderation events are emitted by the Admin M35 decision service and the auto-moderation job; this module owns their templates and deep-link handling. Teacher-side review events are listed in M36. In-app only: none.

17. Security Rules

  • Every write is scoped by author_user_id = sub; PATCH/DELETE on someone else's review → NOT_FOUND (does not reveal existence).
  • Unpublished reviews are returned only to their author. Public DTOs never include author_user_id, phone, email, child name, spam_score, auto_flags, moderator ids or rejection_reason_code.
  • Children are shown only by class label; the child's name typed into the text is not blocked but the pipeline flags PERSONAL_INFORMATION cases.
  • Rate limits: create 5/hour, edit 10/hour, report 10/day per user; eligibility 60/min.
  • Abuse: delete-and-repost blocked for 30 days (BR-34.4); review bursts and self-reviews (same device/IP as the teacher) are detected by Admin M35 (rating_burst, self_review) — the app sends X-Install-Id so the check has device data.
  • Blocked pairs cannot review each other (BLOCKED).

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
No qualifying demo or lead CONFLICT_STATE (details.reason = "no_interaction") 409 Open ReviewEligibilitySheet
Lead younger than 3 days CONFLICT_STATE (too_early, eligibleFrom) 409 Sheet "You can review from Tue, 29 Sep"
Already reviewed CONFLICT_DUPLICATE (existingReviewId) 409 Open WriteReview in edit mode
Deleted a review of this teacher < 30 days ago CONFLICT_STATE (recently_deleted, retryAfter) 409 Toast "You can review this teacher again from 20 Oct."
Edit after the window CONFLICT_STATE (edit_window_closed) 409 Banner "This review can no longer be edited." Hide Edit
Edit while flagged / hidden CONFLICT_STATE (under_review / removed) 409 Toast with reason, refetch
Stale edit VERSION_CONFLICT 409 Reload the review, keep the user's text in the field
Text too short / invalid rating VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Inline under the field
Blocked pair BLOCKED 403 "You can't review this teacher."
Student without parental consent FORBIDDEN (parental_consent_pending) 403 Sheet explaining a parent must approve (links M11)
Report twice CONFLICT_DUPLICATE 409 Toast "You've already reported this review."
Too many reports / reviews LIMIT_REACHED / RATE_LIMITED 429 Toast, disable button until Retry-After
Review or teacher gone NOT_FOUND 404 "This is no longer available."

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T34.1 Parent with a completed demo writes a 5★ review → 201 pending; appears as "Your review · Waiting for approval" pinned; not in the public list (Maestro reviews_write_happy).
  • T34.2 Pipeline auto-approves (score 0.04) → push review_published; review visible to others; teachers.rating_count +1.
  • T34.3 Lead created 2 days ago, no demo → eligibility too_early with eligibleFrom = created + 3 days; POST also rejected server-side.
  • T34.4 No interaction, reviews.allow_unverified = true → review created with is_verified_interaction = false; no "Took a demo" tick.
  • T34.5 Second POST for the same teacher → CONFLICT_DUPLICATE; app opens edit mode with existing text.
  • T34.6 Edit a published review on day 30 → status pending, rating cache recomputed without it, trust job enqueued; edit on day 91 → edit_window_closed.
  • T34.7 Two devices edit the same review → second gets VERSION_CONFLICT; typed text is preserved.
  • T34.8 Delete a published review → gone from list, cache recomputed; new review for the same teacher within 30 days → recently_deleted.
  • T34.9 Three different users report a published review → status flagged, moderation log with admin_id NULL, excluded from the average; fourth report from the same user → CONFLICT_DUPLICATE.
  • T34.10 Teacher reports a review on another teacher's profile → FORBIDDEN; on own profile → 201.
  • T34.11 Offline: draft typed, app killed, reopened → draft restored; Submit disabled until online.
  • T34.12 Text containing "call 98450 12345" → client warning shown; server stores it; pipeline flags contact_info; rejection push shows the CONTACT_DETAILS copy.
  • T34.13 Blocked pair → eligibility blocked; POST → BLOCKED.
  • T34.14 Same Idempotency-Key replayed after a timeout → one row, same 201 body.
  • T34.15 Screen states: TeacherReviews renders loading, empty ("No reviews yet"), error and content; font scale 130 % does not clip the distribution bars.

Module 35 · Institute Reviews

Phase 8 · Reviews · Used by: Parents and students (write, edit, delete, report); any signed-in user (read); institute managers and counsellors (reply, report) · Depends on: M00, M32 (institute profile), M34 (shared review components and rules), M37/M39 (enquiries), M38 (campus visits), M26 (rating display); Admin M34, Admin M35, Admin M27 · New tables: none · Uses: institute_reviews, review_flags, review_moderation_logs, institutes, institute_managers, leads, demo_requests, app_users, user_blocks, user_privacy_settings, system_settings, audit_logs · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Purpose

Reviews of coaching centres, tuition centres and academies by parents and students: an overall 1–5 rating, optional aspect ratings for Teaching, Infrastructure, Value for money and Safety, and written feedback — plus a public reply from the institute's staff. It reuses the review rules, components and moderation pipeline of M34 with institute-specific eligibility (an enquiry older than 3 days or a completed campus visit) and feeds institutes.user_rating_avg, which the Student Feedback criterion of the GuruConnect institute rating uses (Admin M27). Institute managers and counsellors see their reviews and reply from the institute app.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent whose daughter attended a campus visit at Excel Academy, Jayanagar, I want to rate safety and infrastructure separately so that other parents know what the centre is really like.
  • As an institute counsellor, I want to reply politely to a 2★ review about fees so that parents see our side.
  • As an institute manager, I want to report a review written by a competitor so that it is removed.
  • As a student comparing two coaching centres, I want to see aspect averages side by side so that I can judge value for money.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-35.1 Same rules as M34 for who can review, content (30–1,500 chars, stars 1–5), draft behaviour, statuses (BR-34.5), the edit window reviews.edit_window_days, deletion (including the 30-day re-review block), rejection copy (BR-34.8), reports (BR-34.9 with review_type = 'institute') and prompts (BR-34.12) — with the differences below.

BR-35.2 Eligibility. At least one of, for institute_id = :id and requester_user_id = sub: a leads row (target_type = 'institute', not spam, not declined as spam, created_at <= now() - 3 days), or a demo_requests row with institute_id = :id and status = 'completed' (campus visit, M38/M39). reviews.allow_unverified applies as in M34. The institute must be verification_status = 'approved' and account_status = 'active'. A block between the author and any active institute_managers.user_id of the institute → BLOCKED.

BR-35.3 Aspect ratings. Optional object aspectRatings with any of the keys teaching, infrastructure, value, safety, each an integer 1–5; unknown keys → VALIDATION_FAILED. Stored in institute_reviews.aspect_ratings ({} when none). The form shows them after the overall stars as "Rate specific things (optional)". Aspect averages in the summary are computed over published reviews that include that aspect, and shown only when at least 3 reviews rated it.

BR-35.4 Create / edit / delete steps mirror BR-34.4, BR-34.6, BR-34.7 on institute_reviews. Every transition out of published caused by the app recomputes institutes.user_rating_avg and user_rating_count in the same transaction (Admin M34 FR-34.2 service); there is no trust-score job for institutes. child_id does not exist on institute reviews: parents pick the child only to fill the class label, which is not stored (the author label reads "Parent").

BR-35.5 Institute reply. POST /institute/reviews/:id/reply { text } by an active institute_managers row of the review's institute (staff_role manager or counsellor). Allowed only when the review is published or flagged. Creates or replaces the single reply: institute_reply = text, institute_replied_at = now(), reply_status = 'pending'; the reply goes through the same auto-moderation job (review:moderate with target = 'reply') — contact details are never auto-approved. DELETE /institute/reviews/:id/reply clears institute_reply, institute_replied_at, reply_status. Text 2–1,000 chars. Max 10 reply saves per review per day (LIMIT_REACHED). Audit app.institute_review_reply_saved / _deleted with the staff member's institute_managers.id. A rejected reply shows the reason (BR-34.8 codes) and can be edited.

BR-35.6 Institute's review list. GET /institute/reviews?filter=all|needs_reply|replied|low_rating returns the institute's published and flagged reviews (never pending/rejected/hidden), newest first, with reply and reply status, plus the summary. needs_reply = no reply or reply rejected; low_rating = rating ≤ 2.

BR-35.7 Staff reports. Institute staff may report reviews of their own institute through POST /institute-reviews/:id/report (same reasons and limits as learners). Staff cannot write reviews (role check).

BR-35.8 Display. Summary: institutes.user_rating_avg, user_rating_count, distribution, by-role averages, aspect averages. Separately and clearly labelled, the GuruConnect rating (institutes.overall_rating, Admin M27, shown by M26) — the app never mixes the two numbers: "4.5 GuruConnect rating" vs "4.7 from 486 parent & student reviews".

6. Screen Wireframe Description

InstituteReviews — header "Reviews" / subtitle "Excel Academy, Jayanagar". Two badges on top: "4.5 GuruConnect rating" (tap opens M26 explanation) and the user rating card "4.7 ★ · 486 reviews" with distribution bars. "What parents say" aspect bars (only aspects with ≥ 3 ratings): Teaching 4.8 · Infrastructure 4.5 · Value for money 4.2 · Safety 4.7. Filter chips as M34. Review cards reuse ReviewCard with an aspect row "Teaching 5 · Infrastructure 4 · Value 3 · Safety 5" and reply header "Reply from Excel Academy". Sticky "Write a review". Empty: "No reviews yet — enquire or visit the campus, then share your experience."

WriteInstituteReview — header "Review Excel Academy". Institute mini-card (logo, name, area). "Overall rating" 5 stars with labels. Collapsible section "Rate specific things (optional)" expanded by default: four rows (label + 5 small stars, 36 dp): "Teaching quality", "Classrooms & facilities", "Value for money", "Safety & supervision"; each row has a "Clear" link. Text area placeholder "How are the faculty and batches? Are classrooms clean and safe? Is the fee worth it?", counter "0 / 1,500". Guidelines accordion. Sticky "Submit review".

InstituteReviewsInbox (staff) — header "Reviews". Summary strip "4.7 ★ · 486 · Reply rate 71 %". Chips: "All", "Needs reply (3)", "Replied", "1–2 ★". Cards: author label "Parent", stars, date, text (4 lines), aspect row, reply status pill: "No reply" / "Reply waiting for approval" / "Reply live" / "Reply not approved — edit"; buttons "Reply" or "Edit reply"; kebab "Report review". Empty: "No reviews yet. Happy families are your best advertisement — ask them to review you on GuruConnect."

InstituteReviewReply — header "Reply to review". Quoted review card (read-only). Text area label "Your public reply", placeholder "Thank you for your feedback, Lakshmi. We have added a doubt-clearing hour on Saturdays…", counter 0/1,000. Tips box: "Thank the parent · Address the concern · Don't share phone numbers — parents can contact you through GuruConnect." Footer note "Replies are checked before they appear. Signed as Excel Academy." Sticky "Post reply" (edit mode: "Update reply" + text button "Delete reply" → confirm sheet "Delete your reply?").

Module 36 · Teacher Reply To Review

Phase 8 · Reviews · Used by: Teachers (read their reviews, reply, edit or delete a reply, report) · Depends on: M00, M18 (dashboard card), M34 (review rules, report endpoint, components); Admin M33, Admin M35 · New tables: none · Uses: teacher_reviews, review_flags, teachers, app_users, user_privacy_settings, audit_logs · Build estimate: 2 days

1. Module Purpose

The teacher's Reviews tab: a list of every published review on the teacher's profile with the rating summary, a "Needs reply" filter, and a screen to write one public reply per review, edit it or delete it. Replies are moderated (Admin M35) exactly like reviews, so a teacher can't use them to share phone numbers or attack a reviewer. Teachers can also report a review from here using the M34 report endpoint. Replying well is the main thing a teacher can do about reviews, so the screen gives short guidance and shows reply rate.

2. User Stories

  • As a teacher, I want to see new reviews first with a "Needs reply" count so that I thank families quickly.
  • As a teacher who got an unfair 2★ review, I want to reply calmly with my side and report it if it is fake so that parents see a balanced picture.
  • As a new teacher, I want tips on writing a good reply so that my first replies look professional.
  • As a teacher on a slow connection, I want my reply draft kept if the app closes so that I don't rewrite it.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-36.1 What the teacher sees. GET /teacher/reviews returns reviews with teacher_id = pid, deleted_at IS NULL and status IN ('published','flagged'). Pending, rejected and hidden reviews are never shown to the teacher. Flagged reviews carry underReview: true ("Being checked by GuruConnect"). Filters: all (default), needs_reply (no reply or reply_status = 'rejected'), replied (reply_status IN ('pending','published')), low_rating (rating ≤ 2). Sort newest published_at first; cursor 20 per page. Summary: teachers.rating_avg, rating_count, distribution, replyRatePct = reviews with a published reply ÷ published reviews, needsReply count. Author display as M34 BR-34.10.

BR-36.2 Reply rules. One reply per review. Allowed when the review is published or flagged; otherwise CONFLICT_STATE (review_not_public). Text trimmed 2–1,000 characters. PUT /teacher/reviews/:id/reply creates or replaces the reply; any save sets teacher_reply, teacher_replied_at = now(), reply_status = 'pending'; while a new version is pending, the previously published reply is no longer shown (the column holds one text). Max 10 saves per review per day (LIMIT_REACHED, details.reason = "reply_edits_daily").

BR-36.3 Server steps for PUT (one transaction). 1) Load the review with FOR UPDATE, check teacher_id = pid; 2) check status and limits; 3) update the reply columns; 4) insert audit_logs app.review_reply_saved (review id, text length, isEdit); 5) after commit enqueue review:moderate with target = 'reply' (Admin M35): a reply with no flags and spam score < 0.15 is published automatically; one with contact details, abuse or a reviewer's personal details waits for a moderator.

BR-36.4 Delete reply. DELETE /teacher/reviews/:id/reply sets teacher_reply, teacher_replied_at, reply_status to NULL; audit app.review_reply_deleted. Confirmation sheet.

BR-36.5 Rejected reply. The card shows "Reply not published" and the reason copy (codes as M34 BR-34.8, wording adapted: CONTACT_DETAILS → "Remove phone numbers, emails or links. Families can contact you through GuruConnect."; ABUSIVE → "Keep replies polite, even when you disagree."; PERSONAL_INFORMATION → "Don't mention the reviewer's or child's personal details."). Editing starts from the rejected text.

BR-36.6 Client guidance. The reply screen detects contact details with the shared detectContactInfo() and shows an inline warning; it also warns if the reply contains the reviewer's full name or a child's name taken from the lead (not blocked). Suggested openers (tap to insert): "Thank you, {firstName}!", "Thank you for the feedback.", "I'm sorry to hear this." — inserted text is editable.

BR-36.7 Reporting. The card menu "Report review" opens the M34 ReportReviewSheet → POST /reviews/:id/report. Teachers are told: "Reports don't remove a review automatically. Our team checks it within 24–48 hours."

BR-36.8 Edited reviews. When an author edits a review, it leaves the teacher's list until re-approved (status pending); when it returns, the existing reply is still attached and the card shows "Review edited on 3 Oct — check your reply still fits."

Module 37 · Contact Teacher

Phase 9 · Leads · Used by: Parents and students (call, message, request a call-back); teachers (lead inbox, reply, call back, change status); institute staff use the same lead and message endpoints for enquiries (M39) · Depends on: M00, M31 (profile contact bar), M10/M13 (plans sheet), M43 (CONTACT_UNLOCK payment), M44 (live subscription), M49 (blocks, reports), M38 (demo leads), M39 (institute enquiries); Admin M38, Admin M05, Admin M40, Admin M43 · New tables: lead_messages · Uses: leads, teachers, institutes, institute_managers, subscriptions, payment_configurations, transactions, user_blocks, teacher_time_off, parent_children, students, subjects, classes, app_users, user_privacy_settings, system_settings, user_notifications, complaints, audit_logs · Build estimate: 6–7 days

1. Module Purpose

Turns interest into a conversation. From a teacher's profile a parent or student can Call, Message or send a Call-back request; each creates (or reuses) a leads row that the teacher sees in the Leads tab. The module owns the lead creation rules (daily limit, one open lead per requester/teacher/subject, blocks, teacher away), the contact unlock rules (phone numbers are shared when the requester has a live membership, or after a one-time CONTACT_UNLOCK payment through M43 when that fee is enabled), a masked calling alternative that connects both phones without revealing numbers, in-app lead messages with contact-info detection, and the teacher-side lead inbox with status changes (contacted, converted, declined). Admin M38 shows the same leads to support; the lifecycle here matches it exactly.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want to request a call-back from Dr. Ananya Iyer for Aarav's Class 12 Physics with a time window so that she calls when I'm free.
  • As a student without a membership, I want to message a teacher and pay ₹49 only if I want her number so that I don't have to buy a plan to ask one question.
  • As a teacher, I want a push the moment a family contacts me and a one-tap call-back so that I respond within minutes and keep my response rate high.
  • As a new teacher, I want to decline requests I can't take with a reason so that families aren't left waiting.
  • As a parent on 2G at my village home, I want my message to send automatically when the network comes back so that I don't have to retype it.
  • As a teacher, I want numbers hidden until the family unlocks contact, but still be able to call them through a masked number so that neither side's phone is exposed.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-37.1 Lead lifecycle (same as Admin M38 FR-38.1; actors in the app):

From To Who / trigger Side effects
— new Requester: POST /leads, Call on a profile, or POST /demos (M38) public_code LD- + 6 digits (seq_lead_code); push to teacher; SMS if still new after 30 min (08:00–21:30 IST)
new viewed Teacher opens GET /leads/:id the first time Inbox-only notice to requester; first_response_at not set
new, viewed contacted Teacher sends a message, calls (call-intent), confirms a demo, or taps "Mark as contacted" first_response_at = now() if null
contacted converted Teacher "Classes started", or requester "I've started classes", or demo outcome enrolled (M38) closed_at = now()
new, viewed, contacted declined Teacher with a reason (BR-37.10) closed_at, first_response_at if null; push to requester
new, viewed, contacted converted Requester "I've started classes" (response metrics untouched) closed_at
new, viewed, contacted closed Requester closes; system after 30 days without a status change or message (Admin M38 job); block created (M49) closed_at
any spam Admin, or BR-37.11 hidden from both inboxes' open tabs
Open = new, viewed, contacted. Requesters never see the word "spam": a spam lead shows as "Closed".

BR-37.2 Who can create a lead. Role parent or student; app_users.account_status = 'active', role row active; students with parental_consent IN ('pending','declined') → FORBIDDEN (details.reason = "parental_consent_pending"). Target teacher: verification_status = 'approved', account_status = 'active', deleted_at IS NULL (else NOT_FOUND). A teacher_time_off row with pause_leads = true covering today (IST) → CONFLICT_STATE (details.reason = "teacher_away", details.awayUntil = ends_on). A user_blocks row in either direction between sub and teachers.user_id → BLOCKED.

BR-37.3 Limits.

  • Daily limit: leads created by the requester since 00:00 IST (all types, including demo leads) must be < leads.daily_limit (10) → else LIMIT_REACHED { reason: "leads_daily", limit: 10, resetsAt }.
  • One open lead per (requester, target, subject): if an open lead exists with the same requester_user_id, same teacher_id/institute_id and subject_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM :subjectId, the create returns CONFLICT_DUPLICATE with details.existingLeadId; the app opens that lead instead (for Call it silently reuses it). A per-(requester, target) advisory lock (pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(requester||target))) makes concurrent taps safe.
  • Burst guard: max 3 lead creations per minute per user (RATE_LIMITED).

BR-37.4 Lead types from the profile.

  • Call-back request → lead_type = 'callback', preferred_callback_window required (chips "Today 6–8 PM", "Tomorrow 9–11 AM", "Weekend", or custom text ≤ 60 chars), message optional.
  • Message → lead_type = 'inquiry', message required 10–500 chars; the thread opens immediately.
  • Call → reuses an open lead for the target+subject or creates lead_type = 'inquiry' with message = NULL, then calls call-intent (BR-37.7). Requires contact access.
  • Book free demo → M38 (lead_type = 'demo'). Parents pick the child (child_id must be their own live child; class defaults from the child); students send child_id = NULL and class from students.class_id. subject_id must be one of the teacher's teacher_subjects (else VALIDATION_FAILED path subjectId). source is sent by the client (profile, search, recommendation, featured, compare, institute_page, other).

BR-37.5 Contact access (evaluated at create and at unlock). ContactAccessService.resolve(userId, role) returns the first that applies:

  1. A live subscriptions row (status IN ('trial','active','grace','free_access')) for subscriber_type = role. For a student trial, access only while leads unlocked during the trial (contact_unlocked = true AND unlock_transaction_id IS NULL AND created_at >= trial starts_at) are fewer than limits.student_trial_free_contacts (5).
  2. A student with parent_link_status = 'confirmed' whose parent has a live parent subscription ("Covered by parent's plan").
  3. Otherwise none. With access, the lead is created with contact_unlocked = true. Without access: if CONTACT_UNLOCK resolves to an enabled active version (Admin M05 resolveFee), the lead is still created with contact_unlocked = false — the request and messages reach the teacher, both phone numbers stay hidden, and the requester can unlock (BR-37.6); if CONTACT_UNLOCK is disabled → SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED (details.reason = "no_plan") and the app opens the plans sheet (M10/M13). When both membership fees are switched off, everyone holds free_access, so leads are always unlocked.

BR-37.6 Unlock contact. POST /leads/:id/unlock-contact (requester only, lead open):

  • already unlocked → 200 with contact details;
  • access now exists (e.g. plan bought after the lead) → set contact_unlocked = true, insert a system message "Contact details shared", audit app.lead_contact_unlocked (method: subscription), notify the teacher → 200;
  • no access and CONTACT_UNLOCK enabled → SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED with details = { reason: "contact_locked", options: ["subscribe","pay_per_contact"], contactUnlock: { feeCode: "CONTACT_UNLOCK", amountPaise: 4900 } }. The app shows UnlockContactSheet; "Unlock for ₹49" runs the M43 flow POST /payments/orders { feeCode: "CONTACT_UNLOCK", context: { leadId } } → Razorpay → POST /payments/verify. M43 validates the order with LeadContactService.assertUnlockable(leadId, userId) (mine, open, locked) and, on capture, fulfils with LeadContactService.unlockPaid(leadId, transactionId): in one transaction set contact_unlocked = true, unlock_transaction_id, insert the system message, audit (method: paid), then notify the teacher. If the lead was unlocked meanwhile, fulfilment is a no-op and M43 raises a refund request with reason duplicate_charge. Unlocked leads stay unlocked after the plan ends.

BR-37.7 Calling (POST /leads/:id/call-intent { channel }). channel = phone or whatsapp. Returns one of:

  • direct — the other side's phone (teacher: teachers.phone; requester: app_users.phone) when the lead is unlocked and masked calling is off.
  • masked — when calls.masked_enabled = true (settings key, default false): the API asks the telephony provider (Exotel virtual numbers) for a bridge valid 30 minutes that connects the caller's registered phone to the other side; response { bridgeNumber, validUntil }. The app dials the bridge; neither number is revealed. Bridges are cached in Redis callbridge:<leadId>:<userId>.
  • whatsapp — only when unlocked and the other side's user_privacy_settings.allow_whatsapp_contact = true; returns a wa.me URL with a prefilled line ("Hi, I'm Lakshmi from GuruConnect about Class 12 Physics"). Who may call: the requester needs contact_unlocked (else SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED as BR-37.6). The teacher may always call back: direct when unlocked, masked when locked and masked calling is on; locked with masked calling off → CONFLICT_STATE (details.reason = "contact_locked_use_messages"). A teacher's call-intent moves new/viewed → contacted. Every call-intent writes app.lead_call_started (channel, mode; never the number). Limit 10 call-intents per lead per user per hour.

BR-37.8 Contact-info detection (shared packages/shared/contact-detect.ts, same code on client and server). Before matching, the text is normalised: Devanagari and full-width digits → ASCII, number words ("nine", "nau", "shunya") → digits, separators between single digits removed. Patterns: Indian mobile (\+?91|0)?[6-9]\d{9}; landline 0\d{2,4}\d{6,8}; email; UPI id [\w.-]{2,}@[a-z]{2,} without a dot TLD (e.g. lakshmi@okaxis); URLs and www.; wa.me, t.me, instagram.com, telegram. Applies to leads.message and every lead_messages.body while the lead is locked:

  • the message is stored as written with contains_contact_info = true; the receiver's DTO replaces each matched span with "•••• (hidden until contact is unlocked)"; the sender sees their text with a note "Numbers and links are hidden until contact is unlocked.";
  • audit app.lead_message_contact_detected;
  • after 3 detections by the same sender on the same lead within 24 h, further detected messages are rejected: VALIDATION_FAILED (details.reason = "contact_info_blocked") "Sharing contact details isn't allowed before contact is unlocked." Once the lead is unlocked, stored messages are returned unmasked to both sides.

BR-37.9 Messages. Enabled when messages.enabled = true (else CONFLICT_STATE messages_disabled and the app hides Message). POST /leads/:id/messages { clientMessageId, body }: sender is the requester, the lead's teacher, or (M39) active staff of the lead's institute; lead status open or converted (else CONFLICT_STATE lead_closed); no block (BLOCKED); body trimmed 1–1,000 chars. Insert with sender_role = requester / teacher / institute_staff; ON CONFLICT (sender_user_id, client_message_id) DO NOTHING then return the existing row (idempotent offline replay). A teacher's or staff member's first message moves new/viewed → contacted. Rate limits: 20 messages/min per user, 200 per lead per day. Push to the other side (collapse key lead:<id>, suppressed in-app when the thread is open). DELETE /leads/:id/messages/:messageId by the sender within 10 minutes sets deleted_at (others see "Message deleted"). POST /leads/:id/messages/:messageId/report by the receiver sets is_flagged = true and returns { reportPrefill } so the app can open the M49 report sheet with the lead attached. POST /leads/:id/messages/read { upToMessageId } sets read_at on the other side's messages up to that one. System messages (sender_role = 'system', sender_user_id = the user whose action caused them) record unlocks, demo bookings (M38) and status changes; they are never pushed.

BR-37.10 Teacher status changes (PATCH /teacher/leads/:id/status, If-Match): to contacted (from new/viewed), converted (from contacted), declined (from any open; declineReason required: not_available, subject_not_taught, too_far, fee_mismatch, batch_full, spam, other; declineNote 10–300 chars required for other). Stored as decline_reason = "<code>" or "<code>: <note>". The requester sees only the copy for the code: not_available "The teacher has no free slots right now." · subject_not_taught "The teacher doesn't teach this subject or class." · too_far "Your area is outside the teacher's travel range." · fee_mismatch "The fee didn't work out." · batch_full "Batches are full at the moment." · other and spam "The teacher couldn't take this request." Declining closes any open demo on the lead (M38 cancel with cancelled_by = 'teacher').

BR-37.11 Spam reports. Declining with spam counts as a receiver report. When a requester has leads declined as spam by 3 different receivers within 30 days, a job sets those leads to spam and each counts as a strike; 5 spam leads in 30 days creates a Module 43 complaint (complaint_type = 'fraud', reporter_type = the most recent receiver's role, description generated) — Admin M38 FR-38.1.

BR-37.12 Requester status changes (PATCH /leads/:id/status): closed with reason found_teacher, not_needed, no_response, other (stored in decline_reason is not used — the reason goes to the audit row), or converted ("I've started classes with this teacher"). Closing cancels an open demo on the lead (cancelled_by = 'requester').

BR-37.13 Teacher registration lapsed. If TEACHER_REGISTRATION is enabled and the teacher has no live subscriptions row (subscriber_type = 'teacher'), new leads still arrive but the teacher's lead detail, messages and calls return SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED (details.reason = "registration_expired"); the inbox shows cards with first name, class and subject and a banner "Renew to reply to 3 waiting families" (renewal via M44/M43).

BR-37.14 Reminders and nudges. Lead still new after 30 min (inside 08:00–21:30 IST) → SMS to the teacher; after 2 h → push reminder; both deduped per lead. Requester gets an inbox-only notice when the teacher views the lead. Lead closed by the 30-day job → inbox-only notice to the requester ("Contact again anytime").

BR-37.15 What each side sees. Requester: teacher name, photo, subjects, status label (Sent / Seen / Teacher responded / Classes started / Not available + reason copy / Closed), phone only when unlocked. Teacher: requester display name (first name + last initial, or first name only per show_last_name), "Parent of Aarav · Class 12 CBSE" or "Student · Class 11", area name only when show_area_to_teachers = true, message, call-back window, phone only when unlocked, time since creation with a "Reply within 24 h" hint.

8. Validation Rules

Shared schemas in packages/shared/leads.ts: LeadCreateSchema, LeadMessageSchema, TeacherLeadStatusSchema, RequesterLeadStatusSchema, CallIntentSchema.

Field Rule Message shown
targetType teacher (M39 sends institute) —
teacherId uuid, approved active teacher "This teacher isn't available."
leadType inquiry or callback (demo via M38) —
childId parents: own live child, required when the parent has children; students: must be absent "Pick a child."
subjectId uuid in the teacher's subjects "Pick a subject this teacher teaches."
classId uuid; defaults from child/student "Pick a class."
preferredCallbackWindow required for callback; 3–60 chars "Choose when the teacher should call."
message inquiry: 10–500 chars required; callback: 0–500 "Write at least 10 characters."
source profile, search, recommendation, featured, compare, institute_page, other —
message body (thread) trimmed 1–1,000 chars "Messages can be up to 1,000 characters."
clientMessageId uuid v4 —
status (teacher) contacted, converted, declined —
declineReason not_available, subject_not_taught, too_far, fee_mismatch, batch_full, spam, other "Pick a reason."
declineNote 10–300 chars when reason = other; else 0–300 "Add a short note (at least 10 characters)."
status (requester) closed or converted; closeReason found_teacher, not_needed, no_response, other when closed "Pick a reason."
channel phone or whatsapp —
If-Match current updatedAt on teacher status change "This request changed. Review and try again."

Method Path Auth Description

12. PostgreSQL Tables & Columns

New tables owned by this module (migration sql/migrations/137_app_m37_contact_teacher_lead_messages.sql)

lead_messages

In-app messages between the requester and the teacher / institute on a lead. Text only in v1.

Column Type Null Default Constraints / References Description
id uuid no gen_random_uuid() PK Primary key
lead_id uuid no — FK → leads.id (on delete cascade) Conversation
sender_user_id uuid no — FK → app_users.id (on delete restrict) Author
sender_role text no — CHECK sender_role IN ('requester','teacher','institute_staff','system') Side of the conversation
body text no — — 1–1,000 chars
client_message_id uuid no — — Generated by the app; makes sending idempotent offline
contains_contact_info boolean no false — Phone/UPI/email detected before contact unlock (masked for the receiver)
is_flagged boolean no false — Reported by the receiver
read_at timestamptz yes — — Read by the other side
created_at timestamptz no now() — Sent
deleted_at timestamptz yes — — Soft delete by sender within 10 minutes

<details><summary>DDL</summary>

CREATE TABLE lead_messages (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  lead_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES leads(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Conversation
  sender_user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT, -- Author
  sender_role text NOT NULL CHECK (sender_role IN ('requester','teacher','institute_staff','system')), -- Side of the conversation
  body text NOT NULL, -- 1–1,000 chars
  client_message_id uuid NOT NULL, -- Generated by the app; makes sending idempotent offline
  contains_contact_info boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Phone/UPI/email detected before contact unlock (masked for the receiver)
  is_flagged boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Reported by the receiver
  read_at timestamptz, -- Read by the other side
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Sent
  deleted_at timestamptz -- Soft delete by sender within 10 minutes
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_lead_messages_client ON lead_messages (sender_user_id, client_message_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_lead_messages_lead ON lead_messages (lead_id, created_at);

</details>

Indexes: uq_lead_messages_client (unique) on (sender_user_id, client_message_id); idx_lead_messages_lead on (lead_id, created_at)

Existing tables this module reads or writes (full definitions in the owning module)

Table Owner Purpose
leads Admin M38 Enquiries and call-back requests from parents/students to a teacher or institute.
teachers Admin M16 Teacher profile and verification state. One row per teacher app account.
institutes Admin M22 Coaching centres, tuition centres, schools and academies. Rated by GuruConnect after verification.

user_blocks App M49 Users one user has blocked. Blocked users can't contact, message or review the blocker.

user_privacy_settings App M52 What a user shows to others and allows the platform to do with their data.

  • leads (Admin M38): inserted here (status = 'new', contact_unlocked per BR-37.5); updated for status, first_response_at, closed_at, decline_reason, contact_unlocked, unlock_transaction_id. admin_note is never read or written by the app. assigned_institute_teacher_id is M39.
  • lead_messages (owned): one row per message including system messages; contains_contact_info set by detection; is_flagged by receiver report; read_at by the read endpoint; deleted_at by sender within 10 minutes.

14. State Management

  • leadKeys: leadKeys.list(filter), leadKeys.detail(id), leadKeys.messages(id), teacherLeadKeys.list(tab), leadKeys.unreadTotal. Lists and details persisted; messages persisted (last 100 per lead); nothing containing full phone numbers is persisted — call-intent results are persist: false and phone fields are stripped by the persister's dehydrate filter.
  • useLeadDraftStore (Zustand + encrypted MMKV): drafts per teacherId:subjectId for the request form and per leadId for the composer.
  • useChatStore (memory): { activeLeadId } used to suppress foreground banners for the open thread.
  • Send message: optimistic append to leadKeys.messages(id) with status: 'queued' and the clientMessageId; on success replace with server row; on failure (non-network) mark failed with "Tap to retry".
  • After create lead: invalidate leadKeys.list(*), set leadKeys.detail(id) from the response. After unlock/payment: invalidate leadKeys.detail(id) and leadKeys.messages(id). After teacher status change: update detail from response, invalidate teacherLeadKeys.list(*) and teacherDashboardKeys.summary (M18).
  • Polling: useLeadMessagesQuery refetches with after=<lastId> every 5 s while the screen is focused and the app is foreground; a leads push for that lead triggers an immediate refetch.

15. Offline Handling

  • Read: My requests, Teacher leads, lead details and the last 100 messages per lead from cache.
  • Messages: class 1 queue offline — composed messages show a clock icon and are replayed FIFO on reconnect; the server dedupes by (sender_user_id, client_message_id). Mark-read is queued (latest id wins).
  • New lead (request form): class 2 — draft kept, "Send" disabled offline.
  • Unlock, payment, call-intent, status changes, delete/report message: online only.

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
lead_new Teacher "New request from {requesterName}" / "{className} · {subject} · {leadTypeLabel}. Reply within 24 h." /leads/{leadId} leads No (high-importance leads channel)
lead_unviewed_reminder Teacher (2 h after, still new) "{requesterName} is waiting" / "Reply to keep your response rate high." /leads/{leadId} leads No
lead_message Other side "{senderName}" / "{message preview, masked if locked}" /leads/{leadId} leads No
lead_contact_unlocked Teacher "Contact shared" / "{requesterName}'s number is now visible. Call them back." /leads/{leadId} leads No
lead_declined Requester "{teacherName} can't take this request" / "{reasonCopy} See similar teachers." /leads/{leadId} leads No
lead_converted Teacher (when the requester marks it) "Classes started with {requesterName}" / "Congratulations! Ask them for a review after a few classes." /leads/{leadId} leads No

In-app inbox only: lead_viewed (requester: "{teacherName} saw your request"), lead_auto_closed (requester). SMS (not push): lead_new_sms to the teacher after 30 min unviewed, template "GuruConnect: {requesterName} requested {subject} classes. Open the app to reply: https://guruconnect.in/leads/{leadId}".

17. Security Rules

  • Every lead query is scoped to one of: requester_user_id = sub; teacher_id = pid for teachers; institute_id = iid with an active institute_managers row for staff. Anything else → NOT_FOUND.
  • Phone numbers leave the API only in GET /leads/:id (when unlocked) and call-intent; never in lists, pushes, SMS, analytics, audit or Sentry. Masked calling hides both numbers.
  • Contact-info detection runs server-side on every message regardless of the client; the client check is advisory.
  • Minors: students under 18 need confirmed parental consent to create leads; child names are shown only to the lead's teacher; a child's school is never shown.
  • Rate limits: lead create 3/min and leads.daily_limit/day; messages 20/min and 200/lead/day; call-intent 10/lead/hour; unlock 10/hour.
  • Blocks (M49) stop leads, messages, calls and demos in both directions; creating a block closes open leads between the pair.
  • Abuse: mass messaging the same text to many teachers (> 20 identical first messages in 1 h) returns RATE_LIMITED and raises an Admin M38 spam signal; spam strikes per BR-37.11.
  • LeadDetail is not FLAG_SECURE, but CallOptionsSheet hides the number from screenshots on Android (FLAG_SECURE while open).

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T37.1 Parent with an active plan requests a call-back → 201 unlocked; teacher gets lead_new; teacher opens it → viewed; teacher taps Call → direct number, lead contacted, first_response_at set (Maestro lead_callback_happy).
  • T37.2 Student without plan, CONTACT_UNLOCK enabled → lead created locked; teacher sees masked phone; student pays ₹49 via M43 → contact_unlocked = true, unlock_transaction_id set, system message, teacher push lead_contact_unlocked (Maestro lead_unlock_paid).
  • T37.3 No plan, CONTACT_UNLOCK disabled → SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED no_plan; plans sheet opens; draft kept.
  • T37.4 Second request for the same teacher+subject → CONFLICT_DUPLICATE; different subject → allowed; two simultaneous taps → one lead.
  • T37.5 11th lead of the day → LIMIT_REACHED with resetsAt = next 00:00 IST; demo leads count toward the limit.
  • T37.6 Message "call me on nine eight four five 0 1 2 3 4 5" on a locked lead → stored with contains_contact_info; teacher sees the masked span; after unlock both see full text; 4th attempt within 24 h → contact_info_blocked.
  • T37.7 Offline: send 3 messages → clock icons; reconnect → sent in order once; replaying the queue twice creates no duplicates.
  • T37.8 Teacher declines with too_far → requester sees "Your area is outside the teacher's travel range." and push; open demo on the lead cancelled.
  • T37.9 Three different teachers decline one requester's leads as spam in 30 days → leads set to spam; fifth spam lead → Admin M43 complaint created.
  • T37.10 Masked calling on, teacher on a locked lead → masked bridge valid 30 min; off → contact_locked_use_messages.
  • T37.11 Blocked pair → BLOCKED for create, message and call; block created → open leads closed.
  • T37.12 Teacher with lapsed registration → inbox shows banner; lead detail → SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED registration_expired.
  • T37.13 Student trial with 5 free contacts used → 6th lead created locked with unlock options.
  • T37.14 Delete own message at 9 min → "Message deleted" for the other side; at 11 min → delete_window_passed.
  • T37.15 Teacher B requests GET /leads/:id of teacher A's lead → NOT_FOUND.
  • T37.16 Unlock paid after the lead was already unlocked by a new plan → fulfilment no-op and refund request duplicate_charge created (M43).
  • T37.17 Push tap on lead_message from cold start opens LeadDetail and marks messages read.
