21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Real-time delivery over WebSockets or SSE (/leads/stream) to replace 5-second polling when active threads exceed ~20k.
  • Image and PDF attachments in messages (syllabus, fee receipts) through M00 uploads with contact-info OCR.
  • Call recording and call-outcome logging from the masked-calling provider (needs a lead_calls table).
  • Smart replies for teachers ("Share fee details", "Propose demo time").
  • Partition lead_messages by month after ~50M rows.
  • Admin portal additions: a read-only "Messages" tab on the Admin M38 lead detail (with users.pii masking and flagged messages highlighted), a queue of flagged messages and contact-info detections, and settings UI for calls.masked_enabled and the telephony provider.

Module 38 · Demo Class Request

Phase 9 · Leads · Used by: Parents and students (book, reschedule, cancel a demo and report the outcome); teachers (confirm, reschedule, mark complete or no-show); institute staff (confirm and manage campus visits) · Depends on: M00, M19 (owns teacher_availability/teacher_time_off), M31 (profile entry point), M37 (lead lifecycle, daily limit, blocks, contact display, reused MyRequests/TeacherLeads Demos segment); Admin M38, Admin M39 · New tables: none · Uses: demo_requests, leads, teachers, institutes, institute_managers, institute_teachers, teacher_availability, teacher_time_off, teaching_modes, parent_children, students, subjects, classes, app_users, user_blocks, user_notifications, audit_logs · Build estimate: 5–6 days

1. Module Purpose

Lets a parent or student book a free demo class with a teacher, or a campus visit with an institute, from a slot computed straight from the teacher's own weekly availability, and gives both sides the full lifecycle from request through confirm, reschedule, completion or no-show, to outcome. Every demo carries a parent leads row (lead_type = 'demo') so it lives in the same Requests/Leads inbox as an ordinary enquiry (M37) — this module owns only the demo-specific screens and endpoints: the slot picker, the confirm/reschedule/cancel/complete/no-show/outcome actions, the reminder job, and the sync back to the lead that feeds Admin M39's completion, no-show and enrolment metrics.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want to see Dr. Ananya Iyer's free slots this week and book one for Aarav in two taps so that I don't have to call and ask when she's free.
  • As a teacher, I want a clash-free calendar so that a confirmed demo never double-books me against another family.
  • As a parent who can't make a booked slot, I want to reschedule instead of cancelling so that I don't lose my place in the teacher's day.
  • As a new teacher on a slow connection, I want to confirm a demo with one tap and have the meeting link generated for me so that I don't type it wrong.
  • As a student, I want a reminder an hour before my demo and a one-tap join button so that I don't miss it.
  • As an institute counsellor, I want to confirm a campus visit on the same calendar as our other appointments so that front-desk timings don't clash.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-38.1 Lifecycle (matches Admin M39 FR-39.1; actors in the app):

From To Who / trigger Side effects
— requested Requester: POST /demos inserts a leads row (lead_type = 'demo', status = 'new') and a demo_requests row (status = 'requested'); push to the teacher/institute
requested confirmed Teacher / institute staff: POST /demos/:id/confirm sets confirmed_start_at; meeting link required for online mode; lead new/viewed → contacted, first_response_at if null
requested, confirmed reschedule_proposed Either side: POST /demos/:id/reschedule new slot stored in confirmed_start_at as a proposal; push to the other side
reschedule_proposed confirmed The other side: POST /demos/:id/accept-reschedule confirms the proposed slot
requested expired System job, 1 h before requested_start_at if still requested push to the requester; the lead stays open
confirmed completed Either side after start + duration, or POST /demos/:id/complete, or a job 2 h after the window if neither side acted sets completed_at; triggers the outcome prompt and the M34 review prompt clock
confirmed no_show Either side within 24 h of the start: POST /demos/:id/no-show cancelled_by = the side that reports the other didn't attend
any open cancelled Either side or admin: POST /demos/:id/cancel cancelled_by, cancel_reason required; the lead stays open for follow-up

Open = requested, confirmed, reschedule_proposed.

BR-38.2 Who can book. Same eligibility as leads (M37 BR-37.2): role parent/student, app_users.account_status = 'active'; a student with parental_consent IN ('pending','declined') → FORBIDDEN (details.reason = "parental_consent_pending"). Target teacher verification_status = 'approved', account_status = 'active'; target institute verification_status = 'approved', account_status = 'active'. A user_blocks row in either direction → BLOCKED. A teacher teacher_time_off row covering the requested slot's date (any row, not only pause_leads = true — time off always blocks demos, per its purpose "blocks demo booking") makes that slot unavailable; it is simply absent from GET /teachers/:id/demo-slots, never surfaced as an error.

BR-38.3 Slot computation (teacher demos). GET /teachers/:id/demo-slots?teachingModeId=&from=&to= builds candidate slots for the next 21 days from teacher_availability rows where accepts_demos = true and, when teachingModeId is given, teaching_mode_id matches (otherwise every accepting mode is offered, grouped by mode): each weekly window (day_of_week, start_time–end_time) is sliced into 30-minute-aligned starts that fit the default 45-minute duration before end_time. Removed from the candidate list:

  1. any start that overlaps an existing requested, confirmed or reschedule_proposed demo_requests row for that teacher (idx_demo_requests_teacher_time);
  2. any date inside a live teacher_time_off row for that teacher;
  3. any start earlier than now + 1 hour. Response groups slots by IST calendar date with a teachingMode per slot; a day with zero slots is omitted, not returned empty. demo_available = false on the teacher (Admin M16) short-circuits to an empty list with reason: "demo_available_false".

BR-38.4 Institute campus visits. Institutes have no availability table, so there is no slot picker: the requester sends a preferred date/time as requestedStartAt (any time 1 hour to 21 days ahead, shown to the requester as a free chip set — "This week", "Next week", "Weekend" — mapped to a representative time) plus an optional note; institute staff confirm with the real confirmedStartAt from POST /demos/:id/confirm. No clash check is run for institutes (no per-institute calendar in v1).

BR-38.5 Create — server steps (one transaction, Idempotency-Key).

  1. Validate DemoRequestSchema; re-check BR-38.2 eligibility and, for a teacher target, that the slot is still free (re-run BR-38.3 inside a per-(requester,target) advisory lock, pg_advisory_xact_lock).
  2. Requester must have fewer than 3 open demos (status IN ('requested','confirmed','reschedule_proposed'), any target) → else LIMIT_REACHED (details.reason = "demos_open", details.limit = 3).
  3. Requester's total leads today (all lead_type, IST) must be under leads.daily_limit (10), shared with M37 BR-37.3 → else LIMIT_REACHED (details.reason = "leads_daily").
  4. Insert leads (lead_type = 'demo', target_type, teacher_id/institute_id, requester_type, child_id, subject_id, class_id, message = the optional note, source, status = 'new', contact_unlocked resolved exactly as BR-37.5 ContactAccessService).
  5. Insert demo_requests (lead_id, teacher_id/institute_id, requester_user_id, child_id, teaching_mode_id, requested_start_at, duration_minutes = 45 unless the client sent 15–120, status = 'requested').
  6. Audit app.demo_requested; push to the receiver (demos category, high-importance channel like leads). No duplicate-lead check runs against BR-37.3's one-open-lead-per-subject rule — a family may have an open enquiry and an open demo with the same teacher at once.

BR-38.6 Confirm. POST /demos/:id/confirm { confirmedStartAt?, meetingLink? } by the teacher, or by active institute staff (institute_managers.status = 'active') of the target institute. Teacher demos: default confirmedStartAt = requested_start_at unless a different slot is sent, in which case it must itself be a free slot (BR-38.3 checks 1–3) or CONFLICT_STATE (details.reason = "slot_taken"). meetingLink (https URL) is required when teaching_mode_id resolves to an online mode; otherwise it is optional (address is shown from teacher_locations, not stored here). Sets status = 'confirmed', confirmed_start_at; updates the lead (status new/viewed → contacted, first_response_at if null, mirroring BR-37.1). Audit app.demo_confirmed; push to the requester.

BR-38.7 Reschedule. POST /demos/:id/reschedule { startAt, durationMinutes? } by either side while the demo is requested, confirmed or reschedule_proposed; clash-checked against the teacher's other open demos exactly as BR-38.3 point 1 (institutes: no clash check). Sets status = 'reschedule_proposed', confirmed_start_at = the proposed slot; push to the other side with "Propose a different time" / "Accept" actions. Max 3 reschedule proposals per demo (LIMIT_REACHED, details.reason = "reschedule_limit") — after that, either side must cancel and rebook. POST /demos/:id/accept-reschedule by the side that did not propose sets status = 'confirmed'; a second reschedule call from the other side instead of accepting replaces the proposal.

BR-38.8 Cancel. POST /demos/:id/cancel { reason } (10–300 chars) by the requester, the teacher, active institute staff, or admin, on any open demo. Sets status = 'cancelled', cancelled_by, cancel_reason; the parent lead is not closed (FR-39.2) so the family can rebook or keep messaging. Confirmation sheet first. Audit app.demo_cancelled; push to the other side.

BR-38.9 Complete. POST /demos/:id/complete by either side once now() >= confirmed_start_at + duration_minutes, or automatically by a job 2 hours after that window if neither side has acted (cancelled_by/completed_at untouched by the auto-path other than status, completed_at). Sets status = 'completed', completed_at. Triggers: the M34 BR-34.12 review-prompt clock starts from here for teacher demos; both sides get the outcome prompt (BR-38.10).

BR-38.10 Outcome. POST /demos/:id/outcome { outcome } (enrolled, not_enrolled, undecided) by the requester or the teacher/institute staff, only once the demo is completed and outcome IS NULL; the first submission wins (CONFLICT_STATE, details.reason = "outcome_already_set" on a second call — the app shows the recorded outcome instead of the form). When outcome = 'enrolled', in the same transaction set the lead status = 'converted', closed_at = now() (FR-39.2); other outcomes leave the lead open. Audit app.demo_outcome_recorded.

BR-38.11 No-show. POST /demos/:id/no-show { noShowParty, reason } (teacher, requester or, for institute demos, institute) within 24 hours of confirmed_start_at, by the side that showed up (or admin). Sets status = 'no_show', cancelled_by = noShowParty, cancel_reason; audit app.demo_no_show; push to the reported side ("Marked as no-show for {date}. If this is wrong, contact support."). After the 24-hour window a no-show can only be recorded by an admin (Admin M39).

BR-38.12 Reminders and expiry (jobs). 1 hour before confirmed_start_at on a confirmed demo: push to both sides, sets reminder_sent_at (deduped, sent once). A requested demo not confirmed by 1 hour before requested_start_at: status = 'expired', push to the requester ("{teacherName} didn't confirm in time. Pick another slot or teacher."); the lead is untouched and stays open. The 2-hour auto-complete job (BR-38.9) and the expiry job both run every 5 minutes.

BR-38.13 What each side sees. Requester: teacher/institute name and photo, slot, status label (Requested / Confirmed / Reschedule proposed / Completed / Cancelled / No-show recorded / Expired), meeting link only once confirmed and only within the app's FLAG_SECURE join screen. Teacher/institute: requester display name, child/class as BR-37.15, subject, note.

5. Screen Flow & Navigation

Diagram loads when this page is online…

BookDemo reached from a teacher/institute profile always shows the slot picker (or the preferred-window chips for institutes); success replaces it with DemoBooked, whose "Open request" swaps in DemoDetail so Back returns to the profile. Push taps open DemoDetail directly (/demos/<id>).

6. Screen Wireframe Description

BookDemo — header "Book a free demo" / subtitle "Dr. Ananya Iyer · Physics". Summary row "For Aarav · Class 12" with "Change". Mode toggle (only modes the teacher offers): "Online", "At her place", "At home". Date strip (7 visible days, scrollable to 21), each day showing a dot if slots exist; selected day expands a grid of time chips ("4:00 PM", "4:45 PM" …), 44 dp each, disabled/greyed when full. Note field (optional) "Anything to tell the teacher? (optional)", placeholder "Aarav needs help with rotational motion.", counter 0/300. Sticky "Book demo" (disabled until a slot is picked); offline: disabled, "You're offline. Pick a slot when you're back online." Institute variant: no day/time grid — instead chips "This week", "Next week", "Weekend", "Pick a date" (opens a date picker, any day 1 h–21 days out) and the same note field.

DemoBooked — check-mark animation, heading "Demo requested", body (teacher) "Dr. Ananya usually confirms within a few hours. We'll notify you." / (institute) "Excel Academy will confirm your visit time.", reference "Wed, 1 Oct · 4:00 PM" or "This week", buttons "Open request" (primary), text link "Back to profile".

DemoDetail — header back, avatar + name, status pill (Requested amber / Confirmed green / Reschedule proposed amber / Completed grey / Cancelled red / No-show red / Expired grey), ⋮ menu. Slot card: date/time large ("Wed, 1 Oct · 4:00 PM – 4:45 PM"), mode chip, "Join class" button (only when confirmed, online, within 10 min of start; deep-links the meetingLink), address block for offline modes. Context row "Physics · Class 12 · for Aarav" (requester view) or "Parent of Aarav · Class 12 CBSE" (teacher view) plus the note if any. Proposed-reschedule banner (either side) "New time proposed: Thu, 2 Oct · 5:00 PM" with "Accept" / "Propose another time". Reminder note once confirmed: "We'll remind you 1 hour before." Sticky bar changes by status/role: requested+teacher → "Confirm" / "Reschedule" / "Decline" (declining a demo request uses the lead decline flow, M37); confirmed → "Reschedule" / "Cancel"; after the window → "Mark complete" / "Mark as no-show"; completed with no outcome yet → banner "How did it go?" with "Enrolled" / "Not enrolled" / "Still deciding" buttons. Linked lead strip "Part of your conversation with Dr. Ananya" → opens LeadDetail (M37).

RescheduleDemoSheet — heading "Propose a new time", same date-strip/time-chip picker as BookDemo (teacher) or a date/time picker (institute); note "The other side needs to accept before this time is confirmed." Buttons "Send proposal" / "Cancel".

CancelDemoSheet — "Cancel this demo?", reason field (10–300, required), "Cancel demo" (destructive) / "Keep demo".

NoShowSheet — heading "Who didn't join?", radios "The teacher" / "I (or my child) couldn't join" (labels flip for the teacher's view), note field 10–300, buttons "Report no-show" / "Cancel". Info line "This is recorded and may be reviewed by GuruConnect."

DemoOutcomeSheet — heading "How did the demo go?", three large cards: "Started classes 🎉" (enrolled), "Not going ahead" (not_enrolled), "Still deciding" (undecided); footer note "This helps other families and doesn't affect the teacher's score directly." On "Started classes" a follow-up prompt to write a review (M34) is offered.

Method Path Auth Description

10. Request Payloads

// GET /teachers/7d1c…/demo-slots?teachingModeId=3a2b…&from=2026-09-26&to=2026-10-17

// POST /demos   (Idempotency-Key: 4a7e…)
{ "targetType": "teacher", "teacherId": "7d1c2e9a-4b5f-4c8e-9a10-3f2b1c0d9e8a", "requestedStartAt": "2026-10-01T10:30:00Z",

14. State Management

  • demoKeys: demoKeys.slots(teacherId, mode) (not persisted, staleTime 30 s), demoKeys.list(role, tab), demoKeys.detail(id); lists and details persisted.
  • After create: invalidate demoKeys.list(*), demoKeys.slots(teacherId, *), and M37's leadKeys.list(*) (the new demo lead appears there too). After confirm/reschedule/cancel/complete/no-show/outcome: set demoKeys.detail(id) from the response, invalidate demoKeys.list(*) and, when the outcome converts the lead, leadKeys.detail(leadId).
  • No optimistic writes — every action changes shared calendar state that must come from the server.

15. Offline Handling

  • Read: my demos list and detail render from cache with "Updated 2 h ago"; the slot picker is online-only (no cached slots, since a stale slot may already be taken).
  • Book, confirm, reschedule, accept, cancel, complete, no-show, outcome: all class 3 online only — every action either claims a calendar slot or reports a fact needing certainty; buttons disabled offline with "You're offline. Try again once you're connected."

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
demo_requested Teacher / institute staff "New demo request" / "{requesterName} wants a demo for {subject}, {classLabel}." /demos/{id} demos No
demo_confirmed Requester "Demo confirmed" / "{targetName} confirmed {date} at {time}." /demos/{id} demos No
demo_reschedule_proposed Other side "New time proposed" / "{proposerName} proposed {date} at {time}." /demos/{id} demos No
demo_reschedule_accepted Proposer "New time accepted" / "Your demo is now {date} at {time}." /demos/{id} demos No
demo_reminder Both sides "Demo in 1 hour" / "{targetName} · {date} at {time}. Tap to join." /demos/{id} demos Yes
demo_cancelled Other side "Demo cancelled" / "{cancellerName} cancelled: {reason}" /demos/{id} demos No
demo_expired Requester "No confirmation yet" / "{targetName} didn't confirm in time. Pick another slot." /demos/{id} demos No
demo_no_show Reported side "Marked as a no-show" / "For {date}. Contact support if this is wrong." /demos/{id} demos No
demo_outcome_prompt Both sides (2 h after completion, if not yet recorded) "How did the demo go?" / "Let us know so we can keep recommendations useful." /demos/{id}?action=outcome demos No

In-app inbox only: none beyond the pushes above.

17. Security Rules

  • Every query is scoped: requester by requester_user_id = sub, teacher by teacher_id = pid, institute staff by institute_id = iid with an active institute_managers row; otherwise NOT_FOUND.
  • Meeting links are never sent in push payloads or shown in list screens — only inside DemoDetail's JoinButton, which is FLAG_SECURE while visible.
  • Slot generation never reveals another family's identity — only "3 of 5 4 PM slots taken" style unavailability, never who booked them.
  • Rate limits: create 3/min (shared bucket with M37 leads), reschedule 5/demo/hour, confirm/cancel/complete/no-show/outcome 20/min.
  • Blocks (M49) stop demo creation and every action on an existing demo between blocked pairs, same as M37.
  • A suspended teacher (teachers.account_status = 'suspended') cannot confirm, reschedule or complete (FORBIDDEN, details.reason = "account_suspended") but the requester can still cancel.

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Slot no longer free CONFLICT_STATE (slot_taken) 409 Refetch slots, keep the form open
3 open demos already LIMIT_REACHED (demos_open) 429 Sheet listing the open demos with a link to cancel one
10 leads today LIMIT_REACHED (leads_daily) 429 Same copy as M37
Action not allowed in current status CONFLICT_STATE 409 Toast with the server message, refetch
Online demo, no meeting link VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Inline under the link field
Too many reschedules LIMIT_REACHED (reschedule_limit) 429 Toast "This demo has been rescheduled too many times. Cancel and rebook."
Outcome already recorded CONFLICT_STATE (outcome_already_set) 409 Show the recorded outcome instead of the sheet
Blocked pair BLOCKED 403 "You can't book a demo with this teacher."
Student without parental consent FORBIDDEN (parental_consent_pending) 403 Sheet explaining a parent must approve (M11)
Teacher suspended FORBIDDEN (account_suspended) 403 Banner with support link
Demo or target gone NOT_FOUND 404 "This is no longer available."

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T38.1 Parent picks a free slot and books a Physics demo for Aarav → 201 requested with a linked lead; teacher confirms with an online meeting link → confirmed, requester pushed (Maestro demo_book_confirm_happy).
  • T38.2 Teacher availability Mon 4–6 PM, one demo already confirmed at 4:30 (45 min) → the 4:00 and 4:30 slots are absent from GET /demo-slots; 5:15 remains.
  • T38.3 Teacher has teacher_time_off covering the whole week → no slots returned that week.
  • T38.4 Requester at 3 open demos tries a 4th → LIMIT_REACHED demos_open.
  • T38.5 Requester reschedules a confirmed demo → reschedule_proposed; teacher accepts → confirmed with the new time; teacher instead proposes another time → replaces the pending proposal.
  • T38.6 Requested demo not confirmed by T‑1h → job sets expired; requester pushed; the parent lead is still new.
  • T38.7 Confirmed demo, nobody acts → job marks completed 2 h after the window; both sides get demo_outcome_prompt.
  • T38.8 Either side marks outcome enrolled → lead status = converted, closed_at set; a second outcome submission → outcome_already_set.
  • T38.9 Requester reports no_show for the teacher within 24 h → cancelled_by = teacher; attempt after 24 h → CONFLICT_STATE.
  • T38.10 Institute campus visit: requester picks "This week", institute counsellor confirms a real date/time → confirmed; no slot clash check applied.
  • T38.11 Blocked pair → booking BLOCKED; existing demo actions also BLOCKED.
  • T38.12 Offline: Book demo, Confirm, Cancel all disabled with the offline hint; no queued writes.
  • T38.13 Teacher B calls POST /demos/:id/confirm on teacher A's demo → NOT_FOUND.
  • T38.14 Screen states: BookDemo slot grid loading/empty ("No free slots in the next 3 weeks — send a message instead")/error/content; font scale 130% doesn't clip time chips.

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Teacher-side bulk slot templates ("copy this week to the next 4 weeks") — already served by M19, referenced here for context.
  • In-app video for the demo itself, replacing external meeting links (needs a demo_sessions table and a WebRTC/SFU provider).
  • Institute per-counsellor calendars with real slot picking, once campus-visit volume justifies it.
  • Automatic rebooking suggestion when a demo expires or is cancelled (reuse the M30 recommendation engine).

Module 39 · Contact Institute

Phase 9 · Leads · Used by: Parents and students (send an enquiry, message, call, book a campus visit); institute managers and counsellors (enquiry inbox, assignment, status, reply) · Depends on: M00, M32 (institute profile contact bar), M37 (owns lead creation, unlock, messaging, calling — this module reuses every endpoint), M38 (campus visits are demos with targetType: institute); Admin M38, Admin M25, Admin M26 · New tables: none · Uses: leads, institutes, institute_managers, institute_teachers, demo_requests, app_users, subjects, classes, parent_children, students, user_blocks, audit_logs · Build estimate: 2–3 days

1. Module Purpose

Turns interest in a coaching centre, tuition centre or academy into a conversation with its staff. A parent or student enquires about an institute exactly the way they contact an individual teacher — through M37's POST /leads { targetType: "institute" }, with the same lifecycle, limits, contact-unlock rules, messaging and calling — so this module does not redefine any of that. What it owns is the institute side: a shared enquiry inbox for every active manager and counsellor, the ability for a manager to route an enquiry to the right member of staff (institute_teachers), and the status corrections institute staff make on their own leads. A campus visit is simply a demo booked through M38 against the institute.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want to enquire about JEE coaching at Excel Academy the same way I'd contact a private tutor so that the app feels consistent everywhere.
  • As an institute manager, I want every enquiry in one inbox, unanswered ones first, so that none is missed.
  • As an institute manager, I want to assign an enquiry about a Physics batch to our actual Physics faculty so that the right person replies, not whoever happens to open the app.
  • As a counsellor, I want a "Mine" tab so that I don't duplicate a colleague's reply on the same family.
  • As an institute counsellor on the front desk tablet, I want to book a campus visit straight from an enquiry so that I don't lose an interested family while switching screens.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-39.1 Enquiry creation is entirely M37's. The contact bar on an institute profile (M32) opens the same ContactTeacherSheet-style flow (renamed for institutes) calling M37 POST /leads { targetType: "institute", instituteId, subjectId, classId, childId, leadType, message, preferredCallbackWindow, source }. Every rule that governs a teacher lead governs an institute lead identically: the lifecycle (M37 BR-37.1), the daily limit and one-open-lead-per-(requester, institute, subject) rule (BR-37.3), contact access and paid unlock (BR-37.5/37.6), calling and masked bridges (BR-37.7), contact-info detection (BR-37.8) and messaging (BR-37.9). This module reads those same leads and lead_messages rows, scoped to the institute; it never writes lead creation, unlock or message rows.

BR-39.2 Who can see an enquiry. Every institute_managers row of the target institute with status = 'active' (both staff_role values, manager and counsellor) can open and reply to any of the institute's open enquiries in the "All" tab. Once assigned (BR-39.3) to a specific institute_teachers row, the enquiry still shows to every active staff member in "All", but only the assignee (when that institute_teachers row is linked to their own teacher_id, i.e. they are also a registered teacher on the platform) sees it in "Mine" — assignment changes routing and visibility emphasis, never access.

BR-39.3 Assignment. PATCH /institute/enquiries/:id { assignedInstituteTeacherId } (If-Match), manager only (staff_role = 'manager'; a counsellor gets FORBIDDEN). assignedInstituteTeacherId must reference an institute_teachers row of the same institute with status = 'active'; null unassigns. Sets leads.assigned_institute_teacher_id; does not change leads.status. Inserts a staff-only system message ("Assigned to {teacherName} by {managerName}.") that never reaches the requester's thread (a separate internal note, not a lead_messages row — see BR-tables_note). Audit app.institute_enquiry_assigned (previous and new assignee, admin/manager id).

BR-39.4 Status changes by institute staff. PATCH /institute/enquiries/:id { status?, declineReason?, declineNote? } (If-Match), any active staff member, on the institute's own leads only: transitions and copy exactly as M37 BR-37.10 — contacted (from new/viewed), converted (from contacted), declined (from any open, with declineReason from the same code list and declineNote 10–300 chars required for other). first_response_at is set the moment any active staff member messages, calls, changes status, or confirms a campus-visit demo (Admin M38 FR-38.3) — assignment alone does not count as a response. Declining also cancels any open campus-visit demo on the lead (M38 BR-38.8, cancelled_by = 'institute'). status and assignedInstituteTeacherId may be sent together in one call; at least one of the two must be present, else VALIDATION_FAILED.

BR-39.5 Enquiry inbox. GET /institute/enquiries?filter=all|mine|unassigned|needs_reply|closed&instituteTeacherId= (any active staff): all = every non-deleted institute lead, open first then closed; mine = staff whose own teacher_id matches the assigned institute_teachers.teacher_id; unassigned = assigned_institute_teacher_id IS NULL and open; needs_reply = open and first_response_at IS NULL; closed = status IN ('converted','declined','closed','spam') (spam shown to staff as "Closed", same masking as M37). instituteTeacherId narrows to one staff member's queue (manager view only). Cursor 20/page, newest first within each filter, with tab counts and unread message counts per card.

BR-39.6 Enquiry detail. GET /institute/enquiries/:id returns the institute-facing shape of the same lead M37's GET /leads/:id already serves to institute staff (this endpoint adds nothing the requester's data model doesn't already carry) plus assignedTeacher (name, photo, subjects, from institute_teachers) and demo (the linked campus-visit demo_requests row, if any, in M38's shape). Messaging, calling and unlock stay on M37's endpoints (/leads/:id/messages, /leads/:id/call-intent, /leads/:id/unlock-contact); this module's own mutation is BR-39.3/39.4 only.

BR-39.7 Campus visits. "Book a campus visit" from the institute profile or from an open enquiry calls M38 POST /demos { targetType: "institute", instituteId, ... } unchanged; the visit is confirmed, rescheduled, completed or reported no-show entirely through M38's endpoints and lifecycle. This module only surfaces the resulting demo_requests row on the enquiry card and detail (BR-39.6) so staff see the enquiry and the visit together.

BR-39.8 Response-time metrics. Admin M38 FR-38.3 computes response rate and median first-response time for institutes from first_response_at exactly as it does for teachers; this module contributes no separate metric — the institute dashboard (M23) reads the same institute_daily_stats.leads_responded.

6. Screen Wireframe Description

InstituteEnquiries — header "Enquiries". Chips: "All", "Mine", "Unassigned (4)", "Needs reply (2)", "Closed". Manager-only staff filter chip "Any teacher ▾" opening a picker over instituteTeacherId. Cards: requester "Lakshmi V." · "Parent · Class 12 · Physics", time "12 min ago", assigned-teacher tag "Assigned: Prof. Rao" or "Unassigned" (amber), unread dot, campus-visit icon if a demo is linked, red "Reply within 24 h" timer for needs_reply. Empty (no enquiries): illustration, "No enquiries yet", body "Complete your profile and add batches to appear in more searches.", button "Edit institute profile" (M24). Empty (Mine, none assigned): "Nothing assigned to you yet."

InstituteEnquiryDetail — header back, requester name + "Physics · Class 12", status pill, ⋮ menu ("Assign", "Decline", "Report user", "Block"). Assignment row (visible to all staff): "Assigned to Prof. Rao" with "Change" (managers) or plain text (counsellors). Campus-visit card when linked (M38 DemoDetail summary: date/time, status, "Open visit"). Message thread and composer identical to M37's LeadDetail. Bottom quick-actions for open leads: "Mark as contacted", "Decline"; "Classes started" once contacted.

AssignEnquirySheet — heading "Assign this enquiry", search field "Search teachers", list of active institute_teachers (photo, name, subjects, "Currently: 3 open") with radio select, "Unassign" as the first row when already assigned. Button "Save assignment".

DeclineEnquirySheet — reused from M37 with institute-worded reasons: "We don't have space right now" (batch_full), "We don't teach this subject/class" (subject_not_taught), "Too far from our campus" (too_far), "The fee didn't work out" (fee_mismatch), "Something else" (other, note required 10–300).

  • The staff-only assignment note (BR-39.3) is stored as a lead_messages row with sender_role = 'system' and a visibility = 'staff_only' marker carried in data at the API layer, not a schema column — it is filtered out of the requester's GET /leads/:id/messages response by M37 before this module's inbox ever sees the raw table, so no new column or table is needed.

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent

17. Security Rules

  • Every query scoped by institute_id = iid from an active institute_managers row; a lead of another institute or target_type <> 'institute' → NOT_FOUND.
  • Assignment is manager-only (FORBIDDEN for counsellors); a disabled staff row (status <> 'active') gets FORBIDDEN on every action.
  • Staff-only assignment notes never reach the requester's thread or push (BR-tables_note).
  • Rate limits: 60 inbox reads/min, 20 assign/status changes/min per staff member.
  • Blocks (M49) between the requester and any active staff of the institute behave as M37 BR-37.2 — the enquiry is not created in the first place.

Module 40 · Favorite Teachers

Phase 10 · Favourites · Used by: Parents and students (save, tag, note, remove); no institute or teacher role · Depends on: M00, M27/M31 (heart control on search cards and the profile header), M30 (reads favourites as a recommendation signal); Admin M16 · New tables: user_favorites · Uses: teachers, app_users, parent_children, audit_logs · Build estimate: 2 days

1. Module Purpose

Lets a parent or student save a teacher with one tap from anywhere in the app — search results, recommendations, compare, the profile header — tag the favourite to a specific child, add a short private note, and manage the resulting list. It owns user_favorites for target_type = 'teacher'; M41 reuses every endpoint here unchanged for institutes with target_type = 'institute'. Because favouriting is the single most-repeated low-stakes tap in the app, every write is instant, optimistic and safe offline.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want to heart a teacher from a search result without leaving the list so that I can keep browsing and compare later.
  • As a parent with two children, I want to tag a favourite "for Aarav" so my saved list doesn't turn into a jumble.
  • As a student on a train with patchy signal, I want my heart tap to fill in immediately and sync later so the app never feels broken.
  • As a parent, I want a private note like "asked about weekend batch" on a favourite so I remember why I saved them weeks later.
  • As a parent, I want to undo an accidental un-favourite in the next few seconds so that I don't lose a teacher I meant to keep.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-40.1 Who can favourite. Role parent or student, app_users.account_status = 'active'. Unlike leads and reviews, a student with parental_consent = 'pending' may still favourite — bookmarking is not contact and needs no consent gate.

BR-40.2 Create (idempotent). POST /favorites { targetType: "teacher", teacherId, childId?, note? } with Idempotency-Key. One live favourite per (user, teacher) — enforced by uq_user_favorites_teacher (partial unique on deleted_at IS NULL). A repeat call for a teacher already favourited is not an error: it returns 200 with the existing row unchanged (never CONFLICT_DUPLICATE), because a filled heart tapped again — often an offline-queue replay — must always look like success to the user. childId, when sent, must be the parent's own live child (parent_children.parent_id = pid, not deleted); note trimmed 0–200 chars. The target teacher must exist (a suspended or rejected teacher can still be favourited/kept — see BR-40.6).

BR-40.3 Limit. A user may hold at most limits.favorites_max (300) live favourites in total across both target types (teachers + institutes; M41 shares the same count) → LIMIT_REACHED (details.reason = "favorites_max", details.limit = 300).

BR-40.4 Update. PATCH /favorites/:id { childId?, note? }, owner only: replaces the child tag and/or note without touching created_at, so editing a note never reorders the list. user_favorites has no updated_at column, so there is no If-Match — the last write from the (single) owning device wins, which is acceptable for a private, single-editor list.

BR-40.5 Delete. DELETE /favorites/:id, owner only: sets deleted_at. Idempotent — deleting an id that is already removed, or that never belonged to this user, returns 204 rather than NOT_FOUND, so an offline-queue replay of a delete never surfaces an error to the user. Removing a favourite frees the slot: the same teacher can be favourited again later (the unique index is partial on live rows).

BR-40.6 List. GET /favorites?targetType=teacher&childId=&sort=recent|name (cursor, 20/page). Each item is a live snapshot of the teacher card — photo, name, subjects, trust-score band, rating, fee-from, city — resolved at read time from teachers, never copied into user_favorites, so a favourite always reflects the teacher's current profile. A teacher who has since been suspended, rejected or soft-deleted is still returned (looked up by id regardless of account_status/deleted_at) with a status: "unavailable" flag and the card shows "Currently unavailable" instead of silently vanishing from the list.

BR-40.7 One control everywhere. The heart appears on TeacherCard (search, recommendations, compare, saved teachers of an institute) and the profile header (M31); every instance shares one useFavoriteMutation('teacher'), so tapping it in any one place updates every other visible card for that teacher through query-cache patching — never a refetch of the whole screen.

BR-40.8 Signal to recommendations. M30's recommendation engine reads user_favorites directly as a strong positive signal (and treats a removal within 24 hours of adding as a soft negative one); this module writes nothing beyond the row itself for that purpose.

BR-40.9 Update notifications (opt-in, user_notification_preferences.category = 'recommendations'): a job notifies the user, at most once per event, when a favourited teacher's is_verified_badge newly turns on, a fee plan changes, or demo_available turns back on after being off (dedupe key favorite_update:<userId>:<teacherId>:<eventType>).

Screen Route name Purpose

Favorite note sheet FavoriteNoteSheet (bottom sheet) Tag a child and add/edit a private note

5. Screen Flow & Navigation

Diagram loads when this page is online…

The heart never navigates; it only toggles in place. Removing from the list itself shows an "Undo" snackbar for 5 seconds before the row is actually gone from the screen (the API call still fires immediately; Undo re-adds via a fresh POST /favorites).

6. Screen Wireframe Description

Favorites — header "Saved" with segments "Teachers" | "Institutes" (M41). Filter chip "For: Aarav ▾" (child names + "All children"), sort menu "Recently saved ▾" / "Name A–Z". TeacherCard rows: photo, name, subjects, rating, trust badge, fee-from, filled heart (tap removes with 5 s undo snackbar "Removed from saved · Undo"), private note shown italic under the subjects line ("Asked about weekend batch") when set, grey "Currently unavailable" tag replacing the fee line for an unavailable teacher (card still tappable, opens the read-only last-known profile state). Empty: illustration, "No saved teachers yet", body "Tap the heart on any teacher to save them here.", button "Find teachers" (M27). Loading: card skeletons. Offline: cached list, "Updated 2 h ago"; hearts everywhere still tappable.

FavoriteNoteSheet — heading "Prof. Ananya Iyer" with mini photo. Child chips (parents with ≥ 1 child): "Aarav · Class 12", "Diya · Class 7", "No child" (default). Text field "Note (optional)", placeholder "e.g. Asked about weekend batch", counter 0/200. Button "Save".

Column Type Null Default Constraints / References Description

<details><summary>DDL</summary>

CREATE TABLE user_favorites (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Owner
  target_type text NOT NULL CHECK (target_type IN ('teacher','institute')), -- Kind
  teacher_id uuid REFERENCES teachers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Saved teacher
  institute_id uuid REFERENCES institutes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Saved institute
  child_id uuid REFERENCES parent_children(id) ON DELETE SET NULL, -- Optional: saved for which child
  note text, -- Private note, max 200 chars
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- Saved
  deleted_at timestamptz, -- Removed (soft delete)
  CONSTRAINT ck_user_favorites_target CHECK ((target_type = 'teacher' AND teacher_id IS NOT NULL AND institute_id IS NULL) OR (target_type = 'institute' AND institute_id IS NOT NULL AND teacher_id IS NULL))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_user_favorites_teacher ON user_favorites (user_id, teacher_id) WHERE teacher_id IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_user_favorites_institute ON user_favorites (user_id, institute_id) WHERE institute_id IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_user_favorites_user ON user_favorites (user_id, target_type, created_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

</details>

Indexes: uq_user_favorites_teacher (unique) on (user_id, teacher_id) WHERE teacher_id IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL; uq_user_favorites_institute (unique) on (user_id, institute_id) WHERE institute_id IS NOT NULL AND deleted_at IS NULL; idx_user_favorites_user on (user_id, target_type, created_at DESC) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL

Entity relationship diagram

Diagram loads when this page is online…

14. State Management

  • favoriteKeys.list('teacher', filters); first page persisted. A per-teacher isFavorited flag is derived client-side from a lightweight persisted id set (favoriteIds.teacher), kept in sync by every mutation, so any TeacherCard anywhere can render its heart state without its own query.
  • Add/remove: optimistic — flip the heart and the local id set immediately; roll back both on a non-network failure with a toast "Couldn't save. Try again."; queued while offline (see below) and reconciled on reconnect using the server's response, not a client-guessed id.
  • After update (note/child): patch the item in favoriteKeys.list('teacher', *) from the response; no other cache is affected (the note is private and never shown elsewhere).

15. Offline Handling

  • Read: the favourites list and the favoriteIds.teacher set render/apply from cache instantly.
  • Add / remove: class 1 queue offline — the heart toggles immediately from local state; the POST/DELETE is queued and replayed in order on reconnect, deduplicated server-side by Idempotency-Key (add) and by the idempotent-delete rule (BR-40.5) (remove) — a rapid add-then-remove while offline collapses to a no-op on replay if both are still queued.
  • Update note/child tag: class 1 as well (last one queued wins; no conflict surfaced).

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
favorite_teacher_verified User (favourited this teacher) "{teacherName} is now verified" / "One of your saved teachers just completed GuruConnect verification." /t/{publicCode} recommendations No
favorite_teacher_fees_changed User "{teacherName} updated their fees" / "Check the new plans before you decide." /t/{publicCode} recommendations No
favorite_teacher_demos_open User "{teacherName} is accepting demos again" / "Book a free demo now." /t/{publicCode}?action=demo recommendations No

17. Security Rules

  • Every query and mutation is scoped by user_id = sub; another user's favourite id → NOT_FOUND on PATCH/DELETE (not FORBIDDEN, so existence isn't leaked).
  • Notes are private: never returned to anyone but the owner, never shown to the teacher, never included in analytics or Sentry.
  • Rate limits: 60 add/remove/update per minute per user (well above normal use; guards against a scripted client).

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour

childId not the caller's child VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Inline in FavoriteNoteSheet
Teacher id unknown NOT_FOUND 404 Toast "This teacher isn't available."
Update/delete someone else's favourite NOT_FOUND 404 Toast "Couldn't find that." (never reveals ownership)

Module 41 · Favorite Institutes

Phase 10 · Favourites · Used by: Parents and students (save, tag, note, remove, compare); no institute or teacher role · Depends on: M00, M40 (owns user_favorites and every add/remove/tag/list endpoint, reused here unchanged), M32 (institute profile heart), M26 (GuruConnect rating shown alongside user rating); Admin M22, Admin M27 · New tables: none · Uses: user_favorites, institutes, institute_teachers, institute_batches, parent_child_subjects, audit_logs · Build estimate: 1–2 days

1. Module Purpose

Lets a parent or student save an institute with the identical mechanics as favouriting a teacher (M40) — same table, same endpoints, same limit, same private note and child tag, same offline queue — with target_type = 'institute' in place of 'teacher'. The one thing this module adds is institute-specific: a side-by-side comparison of up to three saved institutes across rating, fees, facilities and open batches, since choosing between coaching centres is usually a compare-and-decide task rather than a single pick.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent shortlisting JEE coaching, I want to save three centres and compare them side by side so that I can decide with my child.
  • As a student, I want to heart an institute from search results the exact same way I heart a teacher so that the app doesn't feel like two different apps.
  • As a parent, I want to swap one institute out of a comparison for another without starting the compare over.
  • As a parent on 3G, I want my institute hearts to save the same offline-first way teacher hearts do.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-41.1 Everything from M40 applies unchanged. Eligibility (BR-40.1), idempotent create with Idempotency-Key (BR-40.2, institute_id in place of teacher_id), the shared 300-favourite cap across both target types combined (BR-40.3), update/delete semantics with no If-Match (BR-40.4/40.5), the live-snapshot list read with an institutes-shaped card and an "unavailable" flag for a suspended/rejected/deleted institute (BR-40.6), one shared heart control patching every visible InstituteCard (BR-40.7), and the recommendation-engine signal (BR-40.8) all apply verbatim with targetType: "institute". This module defines no new table columns, no new create/update/delete endpoint, and no new validation beyond swapping the target id field.

BR-41.2 Compare. GET /favorites/institutes/compare?ids=a,b,c — 2 or 3 ids, each one of the caller's own live (deleted_at IS NULL) institute favourites, else VALIDATION_FAILED (wrong count) or NOT_FOUND (an id not owned by the caller, named individually so the app knows which column failed rather than dropping it silently). Returns, per institute: overallRating/infrastructureScore/facultyScore (Admin M27), userRatingAvg/userRatingCount (M35), feeMinPaise–feeMaxPaise, establishedYear, city/area, facilities (array), subjects (aggregated distinct subjects across the institute's active institute_teachers), and openBatches (count of institute_batches rows with is_active = true and seats_available > 0). Computed fresh on every call — no caching beyond the request, since ratings and open seats change often.

BR-41.3 Institute update notifications (the institute-shaped version of M40 BR-40.9): a job notifies the user, at most once per event, when a favourited institute's is_verified_badge turns on, its overall_rating (Admin M27) changes by ≥ 0.5, or a new institute_batches row opens with seats_available > 0 in a subject one of the user's children needs (matched against parent_child_subjects for the user's own children) — dedupe key favorite_update:<userId>:<instituteId>:<eventType>.

BR-41.4 Compare selection. The Favorites screen's Institutes segment (M40, reused) adds a checkbox-select mode once the user long-presses or taps "Compare"; 2–3 selections enable a sticky "Compare" bar; selecting a 4th replaces the oldest selection with a toast "You can compare up to 3 at a time."

4. Screen List

Module 42 · Trust Score Display

Phase 11 · Trust Score · Used by: Any user (view a teacher's public score); teachers (view their own detailed breakdown, tips and history) · Depends on: M00, M16 (teacher verification, the source of Aadhaar/PAN/certificate factors), M17 (profile completeness factor and its own missing-items list), M27/M31 (where the score is shown), M34 (reviews factor input); Admin M36, Admin M37 · New tables: none · Uses: trust_scores, trust_score_logs, trust_score_weights, teachers, system_settings · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Purpose

Shows every user a teacher's Trust Score — one 0–100 number the backend computes from six weighted factors (Admin M36) — as a simple ring with a one-line explanation on cards and the profile, and gives the teacher their own detailed view: the full factor breakdown, plain-language tips for raising each one, and a 90-day history. This module owns no tables and performs no calculation; it reads trust_scores, trust_score_weights and trust_score_logs exactly as Admin M36/M37 write them and is careful never to leak admin-only fields (raw weights, override reasons beyond a setting-gated line, admin ids) to the app.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want a trust score I can read in one glance without decoding jargon like "Bayesian smoothing".
  • As a teacher, I want to see exactly why my score is 82 and not 95 so that I know what to fix first.
  • As a teacher who was just downgraded, I want to know plainly whether GuruConnect paused or adjusted my score, without being handed an audit log.
  • As a new teacher with no reviews yet, I want to know my Reviews factor isn't being scored as zero so that I'm not discouraged before my first class.
  • As a teacher, I want a quick history so that I can tell a drop from a genuine complaint apart from a weights change that affected everyone.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-42.1 Public display groups. GET /teachers/:id/trust-score groups the six backend factors (Admin M36 FR-36.1) into four plain-language categories for anyone but the teacher themself:

Public category Backend factor(s) Combined weight
Verification Aadhaar (20) + PAN (10) + Certificates (20) 50
Reviews Reviews (25) 25
Complaints Complaints (15) 15
Profile completion Profile completeness (10) 10

"Verification" is shown as one bar whose value is its own weighted average ((aadhaar_score×20 + pan_score×10 + certificate_score×20) / 50); tapping it expands three one-line checks ("Aadhaar verified", "PAN verified", "2 certificates verified", or "Not yet verified" per item). This grouping is presentation only — the backend still stores and computes six separate factors and one weighted score exactly as Admin M36 FR-36.2; the app never recomputes anything.

BR-42.2 The number and its band. The public score is trust_scores.score (which is already override_score when is_overridden = true — the backend, not this module, resolves that). Bands, matching Admin M36's own distribution buckets: 90–100 "Excellent", 80–89 "Very good", 60–79 "Good", below 60 "New or building trust". A teacher without is_verified_badge cannot show above 60 (Admin M36 FR-36.2); this cap is never explained as a separate rule to the viewer — it is already folded into the number the API returns.

BR-42.3 Frozen display. is_frozen = true changes nothing in the public view (families never see that a score is frozen — the freeze exists to stop movement during an investigation, not to flag it, per Admin M36 FR-36.4). In the teacher's own view (BR-42.6) it shows a neutral banner: "Your score is temporarily paused while GuruConnect reviews an account matter." — no reason, no expiry, no appeal action; this is a trust & safety hold, and the teacher is directed to support only if they ask.

BR-42.4 Overridden display. is_overridden = true also changes nothing in the public view. In the teacher's own view it shows: "GuruConnect has set your score to {override_score} until {override_expires_at, formatted as a date}." followed, only when system_settings key trust.show_override_reason_to_teacher (boolean, default true) is on, by override_reason verbatim; when the setting is off, the line reads "Contact support for details." instead. The six-factor breakdown underneath still shows the computed factors (computed_score and its inputs), labelled "What your score would be without the current adjustment", so a teacher can see both numbers without confusion about which one is live.

BR-42.5 Public breakdown contents. GET /teachers/:id/trust-score (any signed-in user, and the public shared-link viewer per M31/M33) returns: score, band, the four grouped categories with their combined value and one plain sentence each (never raw per-factor numbers, never weightsVersion, never inputs, never admin ids, never history). Example sentences: "Verification: Aadhaar, PAN and 2 certificates verified.", "Reviews: 4.9 from 312 published reviews.", "Complaints: No upheld complaints in the last 12 months.", "Profile: 95% complete." A teacher with zero published reviews shows "Reviews: Not enough reviews yet" rather than a score, even though the backend's Reviews factor is internally 60 for zero reviews (BR-36.1) — the app never shows a specific number where there is no real signal behind it.

BR-42.6 Teacher's own detailed view. GET /teacher/trust-score (teacher role, own profile only) returns everything in BR-42.5 plus the full six-factor breakdown — factor key, label, weight, raw value (0–100), points contributed (weight × value / 100) — and one improvement tip per factor currently below its own maximum contribution:

Factor Tip shown while below its own maximum
Aadhaar "Upload and verify your Aadhaar to add up to {gapPoints} points."
PAN "Upload and verify your PAN to add up to {gapPoints} points."
Certificates Fewer than 2 approved: "Add and verify another qualification certificate to add up to {gapPoints} points." · 2+ approved, no professional certificate: "Add a verified professional certificate to add up to {gapPoints} points."
Reviews 0 published reviews: "Complete a few demos and ask families for a review — this factor starts once you have your first ones." · below 90: "Reply to reviews and keep classes on schedule — happier families raise this over time." · 90+: no tip
Complaints Any upheld complaint in the last 12 months: "Avoid upheld complaints — each one costs 35 points on this factor for 12 months." · otherwise no tip
Profile completion "Finish your profile ({missingItems, from M17's own breakdown, referenced not recomputed}) to reach 100%."

gapPoints = round(weight × (100 − value) / 100, 1), computed client-side from the already-returned weight and value — no extra backend field. A "Points to the next band" line ("12 more points would take you to Excellent (90+).") is likewise computed client-side from score and the band thresholds in BR-42.2; it is omitted once the teacher is already Excellent.

BR-42.7 History. GET /teacher/trust-score/history?days=30|90|180 (teacher, own profile; default 90) is a thin, de-identifying proxy over Admin M37's history service scoped to teacher_id = pid: it returns the (date, score) series unchanged, but replaces every event's admin-facing detail with one neutral label by trigger_type — document_decision → "Verification updated", review_published/review_removed → "A review was published"/"A review was removed", complaint_resolved → "A complaint was resolved", profile_updated → "Your profile changed", weights_changed/scheduled → "Your score was recalculated", manual_override/override_expired/override_removed/freeze/unfreeze → "Your score was reviewed by GuruConnect". admin_id, note and trigger_ref_id are never included.

BR-42.8 Cards everywhere. The compact ring on every TeacherCard (search, recommendations, favourites, compare) and the profile header renders from fields already present on the card/profile payload (trustScore, trustBand — sourced from the cached teachers.trust_score), so it needs no extra call; tapping it opens the same TrustScoreSheet as BR-42.5 without leaving the current screen.

6. Screen Wireframe Description

TrustScoreSheet — handle, heading "Dr. Ananya Iyer's trust score". Large ring "94 · Excellent". Four rows, each a label and a mini bar: "Verification ✓✓✓" (tap expands "Aadhaar verified · PAN verified · 2 certificates verified"), "Reviews — 4.9 from 312 reviews", "Complaints — No upheld complaints", "Profile — 95% complete". Footer line "GuruConnect checks identity, reviews, complaints and profile completeness to calculate this score." Link "How trust scores work" (static article, M53). Zero-reviews teacher shows "Reviews — Not enough reviews yet" in place of a bar.

MyTrustScore — header "My trust score". Large ring "82 · Very good" with "12 more points would take you to Excellent (90+)." underneath. Frozen banner (amber, BR-42.3) or override banner (blue, BR-42.4) shown above the ring when applicable, each with no dismiss (persists until the state clears). Six FactorCards in weight order (Reviews 25, Verification split into Aadhaar 20/Certificates 20, Complaints 15, Profile 10, PAN 10): label, "20 / 25 pts", thin bar, tip line in grey, action button when the tip implies one ("Verify Aadhaar" → M16 flow, "Add certificate" → M15, "Complete profile" → M17). Footer link "See score history →".

TrustScoreHistory — header "Score history". Segmented control "30 days / 90 days / 180 days". Line chart (0–100 y-axis) with dots on days the score changed; tapping a dot scrolls the list below to that entry. Timeline rows: date, "82 → 85" (green if up, red if down, never colour-only — an up/down arrow icon accompanies it), the neutral label from BR-42.7. Empty: "Your score hasn't changed in the last {days} days."

14. State Management

  • trustScoreKeys.public(teacherId) and trustScoreKeys.mine() persisted (staleTime 5 min); trustScoreKeys.history(days) persisted per range, refetched on pull-to-refresh.

15. Offline Handling

  • All three reads render from cache with "Updated 2 h ago" when offline; nothing in this module writes, so there is no offline queue.

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
trust_score_frozen Teacher "Your score is paused" / "GuruConnect is reviewing an account matter. This doesn't affect how your profile looks to families." /teacher/trust-score verification No
trust_score_unfrozen Teacher "Your score is active again" / "GuruConnect finished its review." /teacher/trust-score verification No
trust_score_overridden Teacher "Your score was adjusted" / "GuruConnect set your score to {overrideScore} until {date}." /teacher/trust-score verification No

In-app inbox only: none. Ordinary factor movement (a review published, a document approved) does not push from this module — it pushes from the module that owns that event (M34, M16).

17. Security Rules

  • The public endpoint never returns raw per-factor numbers, weights, inputs, admin ids, freeze/override flags, or anything from trust_score_logs — only the four grouped categories and their plain sentences.
  • GET /teacher/trust-score and its history are scoped to teacher_id = pid; there is no path for a teacher to view another teacher's detailed breakdown.
  • override_reason is gated by the system_settings flag (BR-42.4) so a sensitive internal note is never shown to the teacher unless the platform explicitly allows it.
  • Rate limits: 60/min per user on the public endpoint (cards render many at once — the client batches/dedupes identical teacher ids in a single screen rather than firing one call per card); 30/min on the teacher's own endpoints.

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Teacher has no trust_scores row yet (not yet approved) CONFLICT_STATE (details.reason = "not_computed") 409 Card shows "Trust score not available yet" instead of a ring
Teacher id unknown or deleted NOT_FOUND 404 Hide the trust section
days not a number VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Client never sends this — a malformed value is clamped before the request
Non-teacher calls /teacher/trust-score FORBIDDEN 403 Not reachable from any teacher-only screen; defensive only

  • T42.9 A teacher calls GET /teacher/trust-score/history?days=400 (invalid) — clamped client-side to 90, never sent to the server.
  • T42.10 Teacher not yet approved (no trust_scores row) → card and sheet show "Trust score not available yet", no crash.
  • T42.11 Ten TeacherCards for ten different teachers on one search results screen fire at most one batched request per unique teacher id, never ten redundant calls for a repeated id.
  • T42.12 Screen states: MyTrustScore loading/error/content; font scale 130% doesn't clip the six factor cards.

20. Audit Log Events

This module is entirely read-only. No app action here changes trust_scores, trust_score_weights or trust_score_logs — every write to those tables happens in Admin M36/M37 in response to events owned by other modules (M16 verification, M34 reviews, M43 complaints, M17 profile). Reads are not audit-logged, matching conventions §11.

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • A "what changed since last week" push summarising the biggest single mover, once teachers ask for more proactive updates than the raw history screen gives.
  • Per-category weight visibility for parents (e.g. showing that Reviews outweighs Profile completion) if user research shows it builds more trust than the current four-line summary.
  • Comparable trust-score context on CompareInstitutes-style teacher comparison, once teacher-to-teacher compare ships.
  • Localised (Hindi) plain-language sentences alongside the rest of the app's i18n rollout.
  • Admin portal additions: none — Admin M36/M37 already own every write and every admin-facing view of trust scores and their history.

Module 43 · Payment Gateway

Phase 12 · Payments · Used by: Parents, students, teachers and institute managers (every paid action in the app) · Depends on: M00, M04, M10, M46 (wallet, optional); Admin M05 (fees), Admin M40 (transactions, webhook receiver), Admin M41 (subscriptions) · New tables: none · Uses: transactions, payment_configurations, payment_webhook_events, wallet_ledger, subscriptions, teachers, institutes, institute_managers, leads, app_users, system_settings, audit_logs, user_notifications · Build estimate: 5–6 days

1. Module Purpose

The single way money moves from a user to GuruConnect in the app. It prices a purchase from the active payment_configurations version (Admin M05), adds or splits GST at 18 %, optionally redeems GuruConnect wallet credit (M46), creates a Razorpay order and a transactions row, opens Razorpay Standard Checkout through react-native-razorpay (UPI intent apps, UPI ID, cards, net banking), verifies the signature on the server, and shows a clear result — success, processing, failed or cancelled. The Razorpay webhook handled by Admin M40 is the source of truth: access is granted only when the gateway confirms capture. The module ships two reusable pieces used by every paying screen: the PaymentSheet (price breakdown and Pay button) and the PaymentResult screen. Callers: parent and student memberships (M10, M13), teacher registration fee (M15), institute registration fee (M22), contact unlock (M37) and renewals, premium and featured boosts (M44). Build this module's API and PaymentSheet before any purchase button; until then M10/M13 ship in "view plans" mode.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent in Mysuru paying by UPI, I want to tap Pay, finish in Google Pay and come back to a confirmed membership so that I can contact teachers right away.
  • As a new teacher, I want to pay the ₹499 registration fee with my debit card and see a GST-inclusive receipt so that my profile goes to verification.
  • As a parent on a weak 3G connection, I want the app to tell me "Payment processing" instead of "Failed" when my bank is slow so that I don't pay twice.
  • As an institute manager, I want to pay the institute registration by net banking from the office PC-linked account so that verification can start.
  • As a referred parent, I want my ₹100 wallet credit applied at checkout so that my first month costs less.
  • As finance, I want every order priced from the active fee version and confirmed by webhook so that what users pay always matches the admin configuration.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-43.1 Fee codes, purposes and who may pay.

Fee code transactions.purpose Payer role (payer_type) Context required Extra preconditions
TEACHER_REGISTRATION teacher_registration teacher (teacher) — First payment: teachers.verification_status in draft, reupload_requested and registration_transaction_id null. Renewal (context.renewal = true): approved teacher, registration period ends within 30 days or has ended
INSTITUTE_REGISTRATION institute_registration institute staff with staff_role = manager (institute, institute_id = iid) — Same rules as teacher, on institutes
PARENT_SUBSCRIPTION_MONTHLY / _YEARLY subscription parent (parent) — See BR-43.9
STUDENT_SUBSCRIPTION_MONTHLY / _YEARLY subscription student (student) — Student with parental_consent in not_required, confirmed
PREMIUM_TEACHER premium_listing teacher — verification_status = approved, account active, live registration period (when the registration fee is enabled); the new end date may not be more than 90 days from today (boost_limit)
FEATURED_TEACHER featured_listing teacher — As premium, plus a free featured slot in the teacher's primary city (limits.featured_slots_per_city, default 12)
CONTACT_UNLOCK contact_unlock parent, student leadId Lead owned by the requester (requester_user_id = sub), contact_unlocked = false, status not spam/closed

Any other role/fee combination → FORBIDDEN. A disabled fee (is_enabled = false) → CONFLICT_STATE details.reason = "fee_disabled"; callers follow Admin M05 FR-5.10 (skip payment, hide button).

BR-43.2 Price resolution. resolveFee(feeCode, now()) (Admin M05 FR-5.9) returns the single version in force. The quote and the order both call it; the order stores payment_configuration_id and fee_code so the user pays the version they saw. If the version id sent with the order differs from the one in force (an admin published between quote and Pay), the order is refused with CONFLICT_STATE details.reason = "price_changed" and the new quote in details.quote; the sheet refreshes and shows "The price was updated. Please review." The app never sends an amount that is charged; expectedPayablePaise is only compared.

BR-43.3 GST and wallet calculation (integers, paise, round half up).

  1. List total L: if gst_inclusive then L = amount_paise; else L = amount_paise + round(amount_paise × gst_rate_bps / 10000).
  2. Wallet (only when M46 is live and the user ticks "Use wallet balance"): maxRedeem = floor(L × wallet.max_redeem_percent / 100) (setting, default 50); W = min(walletBalance, maxRedeem); W = 0 when the balance is ≤ 0.
  3. Charged C = L − W (always ≥ 50 % of L, so never below Razorpay's ₹1 minimum for any seeded fee).
  4. Split: base = round(C × 10000 / (10000 + gst_rate_bps)), gst = C − base. Wallet credit is a discount before tax, so GST is on the amount actually paid.
  5. Stored on transactions: amount_paise = C, base_amount_paise = base, gst_paise = gst, discount_paise = W, metadata.listAmountPaise = L, metadata.walletRedeemedPaise = W.

Worked examples with the launch prices (all gst_inclusive, 1800 bps): Teacher registration ₹499 → base ₹422.88 + GST ₹76.12. Parent monthly ₹299 → ₹253.39 + ₹45.61. Parent monthly with ₹100 wallet → pay ₹199 = ₹168.64 + ₹30.36. Parent yearly ₹1,999 with ₹100 wallet → pay ₹1,899 = ₹1,609.32 + ₹289.68. Contact unlock ₹49 → ₹41.53 + ₹7.47.

BR-43.4 Wallet visibility. The wallet row is hidden unless /bootstrap features.walletEnabled is true and M46 is deployed (the server returns quote.wallet = null otherwise). When hidden, useWallet is ignored server-side. When shown with a zero balance the row is not rendered at all.

BR-43.5 Order creation (POST /payments/orders, Idempotency-Key). In one database transaction, holding pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('pay:' || user_id || ':' || fee_code)):

  1. Validate role, preconditions (BR-43.1) and price version (BR-43.2).
  2. Reuse an open order: if a created transaction exists for the same user, fee code and context, younger than 25 minutes, with the same payment_configuration_id and the same W, return it (no new Razorpay order). If an authorized transaction exists for the same key → CONFLICT_STATE details.reason = "payment_in_progress" with its transactionId; the app opens PaymentResult in processing state for it.
  3. Compute BR-43.3. If W > 0, insert wallet_ledger (entry_type = checkout_redemption, amount_paise = −W, transaction_id, idempotency_key = redeem:<transactionId>, description "Used at checkout · TXN-7702140"). The balance is re-read under the per-user lock pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('wallet:' || user_id)).
  4. Insert transactions (status = created, gateway = razorpay, direction = credit, purpose/payer from BR-43.1, institute_id for institutes, amounts, metadata = { context, listAmountPaise, walletRedeemedPaise, platform, appVersion, installId }).
  5. Call Razorpay POST /v1/orders { amount: C, currency: "INR", receipt: public_code, notes: { transactionId, feeCode, userId } } (timeout 8 s). On success store gateway_order_id. On Razorpay error roll back everything (wallet debit included) → GATEWAY_ERROR.
  6. Audit app.payment_started. Return checkout options (BR-43.6). Idempotency: the key and a hash of the body are stored in Redis idem:app:<userId>:<key> for 24 h; a replay with the same body returns the stored response; a different body → VALIDATION_FAILED details.reason = "idempotency_key_reused".

BR-43.6 Checkout options (built by the server, passed unchanged to RazorpayCheckout.open). key (public key id only; the secret never leaves the server), order_id, amount, currency, name: "GuruConnect", description (fee name), image (CDN logo), prefill { name, contact, email } of the signed-in user, readonly { contact: true }, theme { color: "#1B7F5A" }, method { upi: true, card: true, netbanking: true, wallet: false, emi: false, paylater: false }, config.display.preferences.show_default_blocks: true with UPI first, retry { enabled: true, max_count: 3 }, timeout: 900 (15 min), send_sms_hash: true (Android OTP autofill for card OTPs), notes.

BR-43.7 Client payment sequence.

  1. PaymentSheet loads GET /payments/quote; user taps Pay ₹199 → POST /payments/orders.
  2. Before opening Checkout the app writes usePendingPayment (MMKV): { transactionId, feeCode, returnTo, startedAt } — survives the app being killed while the UPI app is in front (common on 2 GB phones).
  3. RazorpayCheckout.open(options):
    • resolves { razorpay_payment_id, razorpay_order_id, razorpay_signature } → POST /payments/verify → PaymentResult.
    • rejects with code 0 / reason payment_cancelled → PaymentResult state cancelled after one status check (a UPI payment can succeed even when the user backs out).
    • rejects with code 2 (network) or any other error → one status check, then failed or processing depending on the server state.
  4. PaymentResult polls GET /payments/:id/status until a final state (BR-43.10). On a final state usePendingPayment is cleared.
  5. Cold start with a pending payment (app killed during UPI intent): M01 launch sequence checks usePendingPayment; if younger than 30 minutes it routes to PaymentResult for that transaction after the gates pass; older entries are checked once silently and cleared.

BR-43.8 Signature verification (POST /payments/verify). Server loads the transaction by id and user_id = sub, checks gateway_order_id = razorpayOrderId, computes HMAC_SHA256(order_id + "|" + payment_id, key_secret) and compares in constant time. Mismatch → PAYMENT_FAILED details.reason = "signature_mismatch", transaction unchanged, security log and Sentry alert (never trust a client "success"). Match → set gateway_payment_id, and status = authorized if still created/failed. Then the server fetches the payment from Razorpay (GET /v1/payments/:id, timeout 5 s): if captured, it runs the same idempotent PaymentCaptureService.apply(payment) that the webhook job uses; otherwise it returns processing. The client signature alone never grants access.

BR-43.9 Subscription purchase rules. Payer may buy when: no live row (trial, active, grace, free_access) → period starts at capture; a live trial → trial ends at capture and active starts (Admin M41 FR-41.2); a live active/grace ending within 30 days → the new period is queued to start at ends_at (stored in transactions.metadata.pendingPeriod, activated by the M41 job); a live active ending in more than 30 days → CONFLICT_STATE details.reason = "already_subscribed"; free_access → purchase hidden (fee off). A user-cancelled row whose ends_at is still in the future counts as active for these rules (the new period starts at its ends_at). Switching monthly → yearly follows the same queue rule. Price changes apply only to new purchases and renewals.

BR-43.10 Status model shown to the app.

transactions.status App state (status field) PaymentResult copy
created (no payment attempt yet or attempt in progress) pending "Waiting for payment…"
authorized, or created after a successful verify processing "Payment processing. This can take up to 5 minutes."
captured + fulfilment done success "Payment successful"
captured + fulfilment not yet done processing Same as processing (fulfilment normally < 2 s)
failed failed "Payment failed" + gateway reason
cancelled expired "This payment session expired. No money was taken."
refund_pending, refunded, partially_refunded refunded Links to M45 detail

Polling: every 2 s for 10 s, then every 5 s until 60 s; then the screen stays in processing with "We'll notify you when it's confirmed" and a Done button. The server, when asked for status of a transaction still created/authorized more than 20 s after verify, fetches the order's payments from Razorpay at most once per 10 s (Redis lock paysync:<id>), applying capture or failure idempotently. failed is not final for the order: Razorpay allows up to 3 attempts per order, so a later payment.captured on the same order moves failed → captured.

BR-43.11 Webhook is the source of truth (Admin M40 FR-40.1). POST /webhooks/razorpay (owned by Admin M40) stores every event in payment_webhook_events and processes it in a BullMQ job. This module defines what PaymentCaptureService.apply does on payment.captured, in one transaction, with SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the transaction row, skipping if already captured:

  1. Set status = captured, captured_at, gateway_payment_id, method (upi, card, netbanking), metadata.payerFingerprint = sha256(vpa or card id or bank code) (used by M46 fraud rules; the raw value is never stored), invoice number (Admin M40).
  2. Fulfil by purpose (each step checks current state first):
    • teacher_registration first payment: teachers.registration_transaction_id = id; the 12-month period is created at approval (Admin M16 FR-16.8). Renewal: insert the next subscriptions period (subscriber_type = teacher, fee_code = TEACHER_REGISTRATION, starting at the current ends_at or now if ended).
    • institute_registration: same on institutes (period starts at approval, Admin M23 FR-23.3).
    • subscription: Admin M41 FR-41.2 (BR-43.9).
    • premium_listing: teachers.is_premium = true, premium_until = greatest(now(), coalesce(premium_until, now())) + validity_days.
    • featured_listing: is_featured = true, featured_until the same way.
    • contact_unlock: leads.contact_unlocked = true, unlock_transaction_id = id.
  3. After commit: M46 referral qualification hook (first_payment), notification payment.captured (M47), invoice PDF job (Admin M40), meKeys change signalled through the push data. payment.failed sets failed, failure_code, failure_reason (unless already captured) and sends payment.failed. Orders still created after 30 minutes are set cancelled by the Admin M40 job; this module adds: if W > 0, post wallet_ledger redemption_refund (+W, idempotency_key = redeem_refund:<id>) in the same transaction. A late capture on a cancelled transaction is still captured and fulfilled; if its wallet redemption was already refunded, a new checkout_redemption (−W, idempotency_key = redeem_retry:<id>) is posted; the balance may go negative (M46 BR-46.9). If the purchase is no longer valid (lead already unlocked by another payment, subscription already bought), a system refund request (duplicate_charge) is created for Admin M40.

BR-43.12 UPI intent handling. Android 11+ needs package visibility for UPI apps: the Expo config plugin adds <queries><intent><action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/><data android:scheme="upi"/></intent></queries>. iOS LSApplicationQueriesSchemes: tez, phonepe, paytmmp, bhim, credpay, amazonpay. Checkout lists installed UPI apps; if none, "UPI ID" (collect) is offered. While the UPI app is in front the JS thread may be paused; when the app returns to foreground with a pending payment and no Checkout result within 5 s, the app starts status polling itself.

BR-43.13 Limits. At most 3 open (created, < 30 min) orders per user; POST /payments/orders 10/min and 30/hour per user; POST /payments/verify 20/min; GET /payments/:id/status 60/min. A user with 5 failed transactions in 24 h sees "Having trouble paying? Contact support." under the Pay button (payments keep working).

BR-43.14 Reusable components contract. Callers open the sheet with navigation.navigate('PaymentSheet', { feeCode, context, returnTo, title }). On success PaymentResult invalidates query keys by purpose (BR in @state) and its Continue button navigates to returnTo (e.g. { route: 'LeadDetail', params: { id } }). Callers never call Razorpay directly.
