17. Security Rules

  • POST /notifications/:id/opened is ownership-scoped (user_notifications.user_id = sub); a foreign id is a silent no-op, never an error that would let a caller probe for other users' notification ids.
  • No push payload (FCM data or notification) ever carries a phone number, full name beyond a first-name template variable, or a document/document number — matching conventions §13's no-PII-in-logs rule extended to push payloads, since FCM payloads pass through Google's infrastructure.
  • Deep links inside push data are validated against the same route registry as any other deep link (M00 BR-0.11) before being opened — a malformed or unknown deepLink in a push opens Home with the "not available" toast rather than crashing.
  • Quiet hours and category preferences are enforced server-side only; there is no client-side override (a user cannot force an urgent: false event through at 2 AM by any client setting).

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Notification id belongs to another user or doesn't exist — 200 Silent no-op (BR-47.5's ownership scoping; never surfaced to the user)
Offline when a tap fires the call — (queued) — Read state applied locally immediately; call replays on reconnect
OS permission previously denied, user taps "Turn on notifications" — — Client opens native app settings instead of re-prompting (OS limitation, not an API error)
Malformed/unknown deep link in a push payload — — Opens Home + toast "That link isn't available." (M00 BR-0.11)

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T47.1 Happy path (Maestro push_permission_and_tap): parent sends their first lead → PushPermissionExplainer appears once → allow → PUT /devices/me shows pushPermission: granted → a lead_declined push later arrives, app backgrounded → tap → app opens on LeadDetail → POST /notifications/:id/opened fires once.
  • T47.2 Deny permission → explainer does not reappear until a second meaningful moment ≥ 14 days later or a foregrounded push is missed; second explainer shows Open settings, not a repeat OS prompt.
  • T47.3 Two devices signed in → a push is delivered to both; tapping on device A marks it read; device B's badge clears on next foreground.
  • T47.4 Quiet hours (23:00 IST), non-urgent event → push_status stays pending until 08:00, then delivers; an urgent event at the same time delivers immediately.
  • T47.5 Category payments disabled in preferences → no push for payment.captured, but the transaction still appears in GET /notifications (M48) with push_status = skipped_pref.
  • T47.6 Admin M46 sends a campaign to 20,000 users → each recipient's user_notifications row has category = announcements, campaign_id set; a user who disabled announcements gets none, but a lead_new push to the same user still arrives.
  • T47.7 Tapping a campaign notification → POST /notifications/:id/opened sets both user_notifications.read_at and notification_recipients.status = opened; notifications.opened_count increments by exactly 1 even if tapped twice (idempotent).
  • T47.8 App killed, notification tapped (cold start) → getInitialNotification path opens the deep link after the M01 launch gates, and still calls opened.
  • T47.9 Foreground banner (notifee) for an incoming demo_reminder → auto-dismisses after 5 s if untapped; tapping it opens DemoDetail and calls opened.
  • T47.10 Offline tap on a notification → read state shown instantly; POST /notifications/:id/opened queued and sent once back online, deduplicated if the queue somehow retries.
  • T47.11 A revoked device (UNREGISTERED from FCM) receives no more pushes; the user's other active device still gets them.
  • T47.12 subscription.grace_started (M10) and subscription.renewal_failed (M44) firing for the same subscription lapse are treated as the same event client-side (single banner, not two).

20. Audit Log Events

No events of its own. POST /notifications/:id/opened is a read receipt, not an audit-worthy action (conventions §11 — reads and low-stakes interactions aren't audit-logged); the events that trigger a push are audited, if at all, by the module that owns the trigger.

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Rich push (images, action buttons — "Reply" inline for lead_message) once FCM's data payload size and Notifee's action-button support are worth the added complexity.
  • Per-user send-time optimisation (send within quiet hours' end at the time historically most opened) instead of a fixed 08:00 for delayed non-urgent pushes.
  • Consolidate near-duplicate events into one send when several fire within a short window for the same user (e.g. two leads within a minute), to reduce notification fatigue.
  • A dedicated events service (outside the shared Express/BullMQ stack) once push volume passes a few million sends/day.
  • SMS/WhatsApp fallback for urgent categories when a user has no active device and push has failed twice running.
  • Retire the pre-convention event names (BR-47.3) in a single migration once all clients on old dedupe-key formats have aged out (30-day user_notifications lookback is enough to confirm).

Module 48 · Notification Center

Phase 14 · Notifications · Used by: Any user · Depends on: M00 (owns the user_notifications table and the insert pipeline), M47 (event catalogue and tap-to-open tracking); Admin M46 (campaign copies land in the same inbox) · New tables: none · Uses: user_notifications · Build estimate: 2 days

1. Module Purpose

The inbox: every notification a user has ever received — a lead alert, a verification update, a payment receipt, or a copied admin campaign — in one scrollable, filterable list with an unread badge that also drives the Profile tab's badge dot. This module generates nothing; M00 inserts the rows and M47 defines what each event means and how tapping a push is tracked. Here, a user reads, filters by category, marks things read, and swipes away what they don't need — ordinary inbox housekeeping, nothing more.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want to see every notification I've had, even ones I dismissed from the system tray, so nothing important gets lost.
  • As a teacher, I want to filter to just Leads so I can scan for anything I missed while my phone was on silent.
  • As anyone, I want the unread badge on my Profile tab to clear once I've actually looked, not before.
  • As a user with 200 old notifications, I want the list to load fast and scroll smoothly without jank.
  • As anyone, I want to swipe away a reminder I don't need without having to open it first.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-48.1 Source and scope. GET /notifications reads user_notifications where user_id = sub, deleted_at IS NULL, and (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()) — a handful of purely in-app confirmations (e.g. subscription.cancelled, "Refund requested") are written with a short expires_at and quietly drop out of the inbox after a few days without needing a swipe; everything else stays until deleted or the 12-month retention job runs (BR-48.9).

BR-48.2 Category tabs. "All" plus only the categories that have at least one row for this user in the last 90 days (a parent who has never filed a complaint never sees a "Complaints" tab), in the fixed order from conventions §16 (account, verification, leads, demos, reviews, payments, subscription, referral, complaints, recommendations, announcements) with "All" pinned first. Each tab shows its own unread count as a small badge; switching tabs never marks anything read by itself.

BR-48.3 List (GET /notifications). Cursor-paginated, newest first, 20 per page, optional ?category=. Each row: title, body, category, deepLink, imageUrl (campaigns only), createdAt, read (read_at IS NOT NULL), campaignId (nullable — present only for a copied admin campaign, Admin M46).

BR-48.4 Unread count (GET /notifications/unread-count). Reads the Redis cache unread:<userId> that M00's NotificationService maintains (BR-0.7 — incremented on insert, decremented on read, recomputed from a COUNT query on a cache miss). Returns the total (drives the Profile tab badge and the app icon badge) and a per-category breakdown (drives BR-48.2's tab badges) in one call so the screen never needs two round-trips.

BR-48.5 Mark read (POST /notifications/read). Body is either { ids: [...] } (specific rows — used when a row is opened without navigating, see BR-48.8) or { all: true, category? } (every unread row, optionally scoped to one tab — the "Mark all read" action). Sets read_at = now() only where still null; already-read rows are silently skipped, never an error, and the call is safe to repeat. This path never touches notification_recipients — see BR-48.7.

BR-48.6 Swipe delete (DELETE /notifications/:id). Soft delete (deleted_at = now()), owner-scoped. The row list-item removes itself immediately and shows a snackbar "Notification deleted · Undo" for 4 seconds; the actual DELETE call fires only once the snackbar times out without an Undo tap, so an accidental swipe never reaches the server at all. There is no server-side undo after that window — deleting is final and the row does not come back.

BR-48.7 Read-from-list is not the same signal as opened-from-tap. Marking read here (BR-48.5) sets only user_notifications.read_at. It never sets notification_recipients.status/opened_at or increments notifications.opened_count for a copied campaign — that is exclusively M47's POST /notifications/:id/opened (BR-47.5), fired only when the user actually taps into the notification (from a push, from the foreground banner, or by tapping the row here per BR-48.8). This keeps Admin M46's "opened" funnel honest: scrolling past a campaign in the inbox without engaging it must not count as an open.

BR-48.8 Row tap. Tapping a row (not swiping) does three things in order: calls POST /notifications/:id/opened (M47 BR-47.5 — sets read_at if still null, and updates the campaign counters when applicable), then routes through deeplinks.open(deepLink) (M00 BR-0.11) if one exists. A row with no deepLink (a few in-app-only confirmations) instead expands in place (accordion) to show the full body text — there's nowhere else to send the user, but the message may be longer than the two-line preview.

BR-48.9 Retention. Rows older than 12 months are hard-deleted by a nightly job (no user action, no notice) — matching M00's scalability note on partitioning user_notifications. This is invisible to the user; nothing in the product surfaces "notifications older than a year are removed."

4. Screen List

Screen Route name Purpose
Notification center NotificationCenter Category tabs, the full inbox list, mark-all-read, swipe to delete

5. Screen Flow & Navigation

Diagram loads when this page is online…

Back on NotificationCenter returns to Profile (or wherever the bell icon lives in the current tab). A push tap that cold-starts the app does not pass through this screen — it opens the deep link directly (M47/M00) and this screen simply reflects the resulting read state next time it's opened.

6. Screen Wireframe Description

NotificationCenter — header "Notifications" with a text button Mark all read (top right, disabled/hidden when the current tab's unread count is 0). Horizontally scrollable category chips: "All 12", "Leads 4", "Payments 2", … (count shown only when > 0, hidden entirely at 0). Rows (FlashList, swipeable): category icon (colour matches its Android-channel group, M47 BR-47.7), title (bold if unread, with a small unread dot at the leading edge), body preview (2 lines, numberOfLines={2}), relative time ("2h ago", "Yesterday", "3 Sep"), campaign rows additionally show a small thumbnail from imageUrl. Swipe left reveals a red Delete action; releasing triggers BR-48.6. Pull-to-refresh. Infinite scroll with ListFooterLoader. Empty (a given tab has nothing): illustration, "No {category} notifications", body "You're all caught up."; the "All" tab's empty state instead reads "No notifications yet", "We'll let you know when something needs your attention." Loading: 8 skeleton rows. Error: ErrorState + Retry.

12. PostgreSQL Tables & Columns

Existing tables this module reads or writes (full definitions in the owning module)

Table Owner Purpose
user_notifications App M00 The in-app notification inbox for every user: transactional events and copies of admin campaigns.

user_notifications: this module reads for the list, unread count and tab set, and writes read_at (BR-48.5) and deleted_at (BR-48.6) — the only two columns it ever writes. Every other column (category, event_type, title, body, deep_link, image_url, data, campaign_id, dedupe_key, push_status, expires_at) is written once, at insert, by M00's NotificationService; this module never updates them.

13. Relationships

No database relationships (client-side module).

14. State Management

  • Query keys (notificationKeys): notificationKeys.list(category, cursor) (infinite, persisted first page per category), notificationKeys.unreadCount() (persisted, staleTime 15 s, refetched on app foreground and read anywhere the badge is shown, e.g. the Profile tab icon).
  • useMarkReadMutation/useMarkAllReadMutation/useDeleteNotificationMutation are optimistic (conventions §7 explicitly allows this for "mark read" and similarly reversible, idempotent actions): the row updates/disappears instantly; on a server error the row and unread count roll back with a toast "Couldn't update. Try again."
  • Every mutation invalidates notificationKeys.unreadCount(); delete and mark-read also patch the relevant notificationKeys.list page directly instead of a full refetch (avoids a visible reshuffle).

15. Offline Handling

  • The list and unread count render from the persisted cache offline ("Updated 2 h ago").
  • Mark read and delete are queue-offline (conventions §8 class 1 — both are idempotent and keyed by notification id; "notification read" is explicitly named there as an example): the optimistic UI applies immediately regardless of connectivity, and the call replays on reconnect.
  • Row tap's deep-link navigation works offline for any screen that itself renders from cache; POST /notifications/:id/opened (M47) queues the same way.

16. Push Notification Requirements

None from this module — it is the pure consumer of every event in M47's catalogue and sends nothing of its own.

17. Security Rules

  • Every operation is owner-scoped (user_id = sub); ids in a mark-read call are filtered server-side to the caller's own rows (an id belonging to someone else is silently dropped, not an error, so ids can't be probed).
  • Campaign imageUrls are public CDN URLs (Admin M46, gc-public); nothing in this screen exposes another user's data — every row was already scoped to sub at insert time by NotificationService.
  • No new PII exposure: a row's title/body is exactly what the originating module already decided was safe to put in a push (M47 BR-47.2's payload rule applies equally here, since the inbox row and the push share the same text).

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
id in ids/DELETE :id not owned by caller or already gone — 200 Silently ignored / no-op (never reveals whether the id ever existed)
ids array over 100 VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Client never sends more than 100; defensive only
Unknown category filter VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Client-side enum, can't happen from the UI
Offline mark-read/delete — (queued) — Optimistic UI applies now; call replays on reconnect

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T48.1 Happy path (Maestro notification_center_read_and_filter): teacher opens Notification Center → "All" shows mixed categories → switches to "Leads" tab → taps an unread row → row marked read, deep link opens LeadDetail, unread badge decrements by 1.
  • T48.2 "Mark all read" on the "Payments" tab → only payments-category rows update; other tabs' unread counts unchanged.
  • T48.3 Swipe a row → it disappears with an Undo snackbar; tapping Undo within 4 s restores it and no DELETE call is made; letting it time out calls DELETE and the row stays gone on next fetch.
  • T48.4 A campaign notification is tapped → notification_recipients.status becomes opened and notifications.opened_count increments by 1 (via M47); scrolling past ten other campaign rows without tapping them changes neither.
  • T48.5 A row with no deepLink (an in-app-only confirmation) is tapped → expands in place to show full body; no navigation occurs.
  • T48.6 Category tab set only shows categories with activity in the last 90 days; a parent who has never had a complaint never sees a "Complaints" tab.
  • T48.7 Two devices signed in: marking read on device A updates the unread badge on device B within one foreground refresh.
  • T48.8 Offline: list renders from cache; swiping a row updates the UI immediately and queues the delete; reconnect sends it once.
  • T48.9 200 notifications on the account → pagination returns 20 per page with a stable nextCursor, no duplicates or gaps across pages while new ones arrive concurrently.
  • T48.10 A notification with expires_at in the past (e.g. an old "Refund requested" confirmation) is absent from GET /notifications even though deleted_at is still null.
  • T48.11 Mark-read call for an id belonging to another user → 200 no-op, no row changed, no error surfaced.
  • T48.12 Nightly retention job removes a 13-month-old row → it was already invisible to the user well before deletion (no user-facing change).

20. Audit Log Events

No events. Reading, marking read and deleting one's own inbox items are routine, low-stakes actions on the user's own data (conventions §11 — reads and preference-level interactions aren't audit-logged); the underlying events that populate the inbox are audited, if at all, by the module that generated them.

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Inline notification grouping ("3 new leads" collapsing several lead_new rows from the same day) once volume makes a flat list noisy.
  • A quick "Mute this category" action right from a row's swipe menu, deep-linking into M20's preference switches instead of a separate settings trip.
  • Search within notifications once the list is long enough to need it (title/body full-text).
  • Rich campaign layouts (carousel, video) for announcements rows, matching whatever Admin M46 adds to campaign composition.
  • Move user_notifications to a partitioned table (by month) once the 12-month retention job is deleting a meaningful fraction of total rows nightly (M00's existing scalability note).

Module 49 · Report User

Phase 15 · Complaints · Used by: Parent, Student, Teacher, Institute staff (any signed-in role — "Any user") · Depends on: M00 (uploads, notifications), M37 (leads context, existing block-on-contact rule), M50 (view a filed report); Admin M43 (triage, SLA, enforcement), Admin M36 (trust score effect) · New tables: user_blocks · Uses: complaints, complaint_actions, complaint_attachments, leads, teachers, institutes, files, app_users, user_notifications, audit_logs · Build estimate: 4–5 days

1. Module Purpose

The safety entry point every profile, lead thread and review exposes. Parents and students can report a teacher or institute; teachers can report the parent or student on a lead; institute staff can report a parent or student who contacted them. A report creates a complaints case that Admin M43 triages and works, with an SLA and a full timeline. The module also owns blocking: either side of an interaction can block the other, which immediately stops contact, messages, calls, demos and reviews between the pair. The reporter's identity is never revealed to the person they reported, at any point in this app.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want to report a teacher who asked me to pay outside the app so that GuruConnect looks into it and I have a record.
  • As a teacher, I want to report a parent who was abusive in chat so that they can't keep contacting me.
  • As an institute counsellor, I want to report a parent who sent harassing messages to our enquiry inbox.
  • As a student on a slow connection, I want the report form to keep my typed description if my upload fails so that I don't have to start over.
  • As any user, I want to block someone without filing a report so that they simply can't reach me again.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-49.1 Who can report whom. reporter_type is derived from the caller's role (parent, student, teacher, institute_staff); reported_type is chosen on the form and constrained by role: parents/students → teacher or institute; teachers → parent or student; institute staff → parent or student. Reporting your own account, or a role your account cannot target, is rejected client-side and re-checked server-side (VALIDATION_FAILED). BR-49.2 Target resolution. For reported_type = teacher/institute the form takes a teacherId/instituteId (from the profile, a lead or a review); for parent/student it takes the reportedUserId, which must be the counterparty on a leadId the caller supplies (leads.requester_user_id for a teacher/institute reporting, or the lead's teacher/institute side for a learner reporting) — this prevents reporting an arbitrary stranger. leadId is optional only when reporting a teacher/institute directly from their profile (no prior contact needed, since anyone can misrepresent a profile). Target not found, deleted or already account_status = banned → NOT_FOUND. BR-49.3 Intake. POST /reports inserts one complaints row in a transaction: reporter_user_id = sub, reporter_type, reported_type, reported_user_id or reported_institute_id per BR-49.2's constraint (ck_complaints_target), lead_id if supplied, complaint_type (fraud, misconduct, fake_information, harassment, other), description (20–3,000 chars), status = 'open'. In the same transaction: one complaint_actions row (action = 'created', is_internal = true, admin_id = null), and one complaint_attachments row per confirmed fileId (purpose complaint_evidence, uploaded_by_type = 'app_user'). Idempotency-Key on the create so a retried submit never files twice. BR-49.4 Triage on create (mirrors Admin M43 FR-43.2 exactly, computed by the app's server, not the client). Severity: harassment, or a description match against system_settings key complaints.safety_keywords, or the reported party already has ≥ 2 complaints in the last 30 days → critical; fraud → high; misconduct → medium; fake_information/other → low. sla_due_at = created_at + 4 h (critical), 24 h (high), 72 h (medium/low). A critical case against a teacher freezes their trust score (Admin M36) until the case closes. BR-49.5 Evidence. Up to 5 attachments per report, image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf, ≤ 10 MB each, uploaded first via M00 presign with purpose = complaint_evidence (private bucket) and passed as confirmed fileIds. A user may not attach a file they don't own (files.uploaded_by_id != sub → FORBIDDEN). BR-49.6 Acknowledgement. On success, NotificationService.notify inserts user_notifications for the reporter only (category complaints, not urgent) with the case number; no notification is sent to the reported party at intake — they learn of enforcement only if and when an admin warns or suspends them (Admin M43 FR-43.4), never that a report exists. BR-49.7 Reporter identity is never shown to the reported party. Every response and screen the reported party can see (this module, M50, any warning/suspension notice) omits reporter_user_id, reporter_type's display name and the description's identifying details are only ever shown to Admin. The reported party sees only "A user reported you" plus the substance of any warning. BR-49.8 Rate limit. Max 5 reports created per rolling 24 h per reporter (LIMIT_REACHED, details.reason = "max_reports_per_day"); this is separate from the general 120 req/min limit. BR-49.9 Blocking (user_blocks, owned here). POST /blocks { blockedUserId, reason?, complaintId? } — blocking a user with no active identical row (blocker_user_id, blocked_user_id, deleted_at IS NULL) is idempotent: a second call while one is active returns the existing row rather than erroring. reason (0–500 chars, optional) and complaintId (optional, must belong to sub as reporter or reported party) are stored for context. In the same transaction: any leads row between the pair with status IN ('new','viewed','contacted') is set to closed, decline_reason = 'blocked' (mirrors M37's block-closes-leads rule); the pair can no longer create leads, send lead messages, book demos, leave or reply to reviews, or see each other's contact details — every one of those modules checks user_blocks before acting (BLOCKED). BR-49.10 Report-and-block together. The report form has an "Also block this user" switch (default on for harassment/fraud); when checked, POST /reports creates the block in the same transaction with complaint_id set to the new case, after the complaint insert succeeds. BR-49.11 Unblock. DELETE /blocks/:blockedUserId sets deleted_at = now() on the caller's active block row against that user (NOT_FOUND if none active). Unblocking does not reopen closed leads or undo a linked complaint's outcome. BR-49.12 Listing blocks. GET /blocks returns the caller's active blocks (blocker_user_id = sub, deleted_at IS NULL), newest first, with the blocked user's minimal display info (name, role, avatar) — the app never lists who has blocked the caller.

Block confirm (bottom sheet) BlockConfirmSheet Confirms a standalone block from a profile or chat

6. Screen Wireframe Description

ReportUser — header "Report {name}" (or "Report Dr. Ananya Iyer" / "Report GuruShiksha Academy"). Section "What happened?" — reason chips: Fraud / Misconduct / Fake information / Harassment / Other. Text area "Tell us what happened" placeholder "Be specific — dates, amounts, what was said…", counter "20 char minimum · 640/3,000". "Add evidence (optional)" — up to 5 thumbnails, "+ Add photo or PDF" opens image/document picker. ReportSubmitted — check illustration, heading "Report submitted", body "Case CS-4471 · We aim to respond within 24 hours for this type of report.", buttons "View my reports" (primary) and "Done" (secondary).

BlockedUsers — list rows: avatar, name, role label ("Teacher" / "Parent"), "Blocked 12 Sep 2026", trailing "Unblock" text button (opens confirm sheet "Unblock Rohan S.? They'll be able to contact you again."). Empty: "You haven't blocked anyone."

BlockConfirmSheet — heading "Block {name}?", body "They won't be able to message, call or send you leads. Any open enquiry between you will be closed.", optional short reason field, buttons "Block" (destructive) and "Cancel".

12. PostgreSQL Tables & Columns

14. State Management

  • reportDraftStore (Zustand + encrypted MMKV, keyed by targetType:targetId): { complaintType, description, fileIds, alsoBlock }, cleared on successful submit or explicit discard.
  • Query keys: blocksKeys.list. useSubmitReportMutation invalidates nothing here (M50 owns reportsKeys); useBlockMutation/useUnblockMutation invalidate blocksKeys.list and, optimistically, any cached lead/profile/review data involving that user (marks it blocked: true without a refetch, rolled back on error).

15. Offline Handling

  • Report submission is save draft, submit online (conventions §8 class 2): the draft survives app kills; "Submit report" is disabled offline with "You'll be able to submit when you're back online."
  • Evidence upload is online-only (conventions §8 class 3); the picker stays enabled so the user can select files offline, but the upload starts on reconnect.
  • Block/unblock are queue offline (idempotent, class 1): optimistic UI updates immediately; replayed FIFO on reconnect.
  • GET /blocks is a persisted query, readable offline from cache.

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
Report acknowledged Reporter "Report received" / "We've received case CS-4471 and will review it soon." gc://reports/:id complaints No
No push is ever sent to the reported party from this module (BR-49.7); any notice they receive about a warning or suspension comes from Admin M43's enforcement pipeline, not from the act of reporting.

17. Security Rules

  • Ownership: reportedUserId/leadId combinations are re-validated server-side against leads, never trusted from the client alone.
  • Evidence bucket is private (gc-private); viewed only via 60-second presigned GETs, owner (reporter) or an admin with complaints.read.
  • Reporter identity fields are stripped from every response shape the reported party's token can reach, not just hidden in the UI.
  • Abuse: the 5/day report limit and per-install analytics dedupe reduce mass/retaliatory reporting; repeated reports against the same target from the same reporter within 24 h are still accepted (admins see them as related cases) but flagged for review via the existing ≥ 2 complaints in 30 days → critical rule.
  • Self-report and reporting an account with no shared interaction history (learner reporting a parent/student, or either side reporting a target with no matching leadId) is rejected — there is no legitimate reason for it.
  • FLAG_SECURE on the evidence picker/preview screens (photos may contain payment or personal details).

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Missing/short description VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Inline under the text area
Target not found or banned NOT_FOUND 404 "This account is no longer available."
Role can't report this target VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Toast, form not submitted
Lead doesn't involve both parties VALIDATION_FAILED 422 "We couldn't find that conversation."
Daily report limit reached LIMIT_REACHED 429 Sheet with "Try again tomorrow"
Attached file not owned/active FORBIDDEN 403 File removed from the list, retry
Unblock a user not blocked NOT_FOUND 404 Toast "Already not blocked."; list refetched

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T49.1 Parent reports a teacher with a valid reason and 640-char description → 201, case number shown; Maestro flow report_teacher_happy_path.
  • T49.2 Description of 15 chars → inline validation, submit disabled.
  • T49.3 Teacher reports the parent from a lead thread with alsoBlock on → complaint created, block created, the lead is closed with decline_reason = "blocked".
  • T49.4 6th report in 24 h → LIMIT_REACHED.
  • T49.5 Reported party's own GET /reports (M50) never contains reporterUserId or the reporter's name.
  • T49.6 3 attachments upload, one fails (415) → other two still submit with the report; failed one shown with Retry, not blocking submit.
  • T49.7 Offline: description typed, app killed and reopened → draft restored; "Submit" disabled with offline hint; submits automatically prompt to retry once online (not auto-sent, since it's class 2 not class 1).
  • T49.8 POST /blocks called twice with the same blockedUserId (network retry) → one active row, no duplicate.
  • T49.9 Block created → any pending lead between the pair is closed; a new lead attempt afterwards → BLOCKED.
  • T49.10 Unblock → the pair can create a new lead again; old closed lead stays closed.
  • T49.11 Reporting a stranger teacher (no leadId, from their public profile) → allowed; reporting a stranger parent with no lead → VALIDATION_FAILED.
  • T49.12 A harassment report against a teacher already at 2 complaints this month → severity critical, slaDueAt = +4 h; trust score frozen (verified via Admin M36 read-only check in the test).

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • In-app two-way messaging on an open case (currently only via the resolve/dismiss message and info requests) — tracked as an Admin M43 scalability item too.
  • Automatic detection of payment-outside-app language in lead messages to pre-fill a report (shared with M37's contact-info detector).
  • A short "why block" taxonomy (harassment, spam, inappropriate) instead of free text, to feed abuse analytics.

Module 50 · Complaint History

Phase 15 · Complaints · Used by: Any user (as reporter or as the reported party) · Depends on: M49 (files the case); Admin M43 (owns triage, enforcement and closure) · New tables: none · Uses: complaints, complaint_actions, complaint_attachments, app_users, audit_logs · Build estimate: 2–3 days

1. Module Purpose

Lets any user see the safety cases they are involved in — either as the one who reported, or as the one who was reported — follow the status without seeing internal admin notes, reply when an admin asks for more information, and read the final outcome message. It is the app-side mirror of Admin M43's case timeline, filtered to what each side is allowed to see.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want to check on the report I filed against a teacher so that I know it's being looked at.
  • As a teacher, I want to see that someone reported me and reply to the admin's question so that I can give my side.
  • As a student, I want to read the outcome message once a case closes so that I know what happened.
  • As an institute counsellor, I want my case list to clearly separate reports I filed from ones filed against my institute's staff.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-50.1 My reports list. GET /reports returns complaints where reporter_user_id = sub OR reported_user_id = sub (or, for institute staff, reported_institute_id in an institute they actively manage), split into two client-side tabs by a side field the API adds per row: "filed" or "against_me". Cursor-paginated, newest created_at first; filter chips: status (open, in_review, awaiting_info, escalated, resolved, dismissed — grouped in the UI as Open / Closed) and side. BR-50.2 Case detail — reporter view. GET /reports/:id when reporter_user_id = sub: full reported summary (name, role, photo — the caller already knows who they reported), case number, type, severity, status, SLA state (open/in_review/etc. shown as a friendly stage, not raw SLA hours), and the outcome once closed (resolution, reporterMessage). No admin identity is shown, only "Support team". BR-50.3 Case detail — reported-party view. GET /reports/:id when reported_user_id = sub or the caller staffs reported_institute_id: the reporter object is never included (BR-49.7); the case is shown as "A user reported you" with the complaint type and a support-written summary line, never the raw description (which may itself identify the reporter). Only entries relevant to enforcement or information requests aimed at this side are shown; there is no separate outcome message field for this side — a warning or suspension arrives as its own notification (Admin M43 FR-43.4), not through this endpoint. BR-50.4 Timeline. Built from complaint_actions WHERE complaint_id = :id AND is_internal = false, oldest first. Each row is rendered by action: created ("Report filed" / "You were reported", depending on side), info_requested (shows note as the question, with a "Reply" button when it targets the viewer's side and status = 'awaiting_info'), note authored by an app user (a stored reply — see BR-50.5) shown as a chat bubble on "your" side, warning_issued/suspended/escalated/resolved/dismissed/reopened shown as status-change chips with the visible portion of their note. Rows where metadata would reveal the other party's identity are never sent to the app regardless of is_internal. BR-50.5 Reply to an information request. POST /reports/:id/reply { message }, allowed only when status = 'awaiting_info' and the most recent info_requested action's metadata.to equals the caller's side (reporter or reported) — otherwise CONFLICT_STATE (details.reason = "no_open_request"). In one transaction: insert complaint_actions (action = 'note', is_internal = false, note = message, admin_id = null, metadata = { "repliedBy": "reporter" | "reported" }), then update complaints.status = 'in_review' (mirrors Admin M43 FR-43.3 "reply received"). Each open information request accepts exactly one reply; a second attempt after replying (before a new request) → CONFLICT_STATE ("You've already replied. We'll follow up soon."). BR-50.6 Outcome message. When status IN ('resolved','dismissed'), the reporter's case detail shows reporterMessage as the closing line; the reported party's case detail never shows reporterMessage (it is written for the reporter) — they see only that the case is closed, plus any warning/suspension notice they separately received. BR-50.7 Reopen visibility. If Admin reopens a closed case (status → in_review via reopened), both sides simply see the status return to "In review" on next refresh/push; no extra action is needed from the app.

6. Screen Wireframe Description

MyReports — header "My reports", segmented control "Filed (3)" / "Against me (1)". Filter chip row "All · Open · Closed". Rows: case number "CS-4471", type pill "Fraud", status pill ("In review" amber, "Resolved" green, "Awaiting your reply" red with a dot when it's the viewer's turn), target name for Filed tab ("Dr. Ananya Iyer") or "A user" for Against-me tab, date "Filed 12 Sep 2026". We've taken action against this account." (green card). If open: sticky reply box "Type your reply…" with "Send" (disabled under 10 chars, hidden when not your turn).

ReportDetail (Against me) — header "Case CS-4471", status pill, body "A user reported you for Fraud on 12 Sep 2026.", no reporter details shown. (no reporter message shown here).

13. Relationships

Entity relationship diagram (tables this module uses; admins omitted)

14. State Management

  • Query keys: reportsKeys.list(side, status), reportsKeys.detail(id). useReplyToReportMutation invalidates reportsKeys.detail(id) and reportsKeys.list('*') (both tabs, since myTurn/status changed).
  • No Zustand store; the reply text is local component state (short-lived, not worth persisting).

15. Offline Handling

  • GET /reports and GET /reports/:id are persisted queries (24 h cache); read fully offline with "Updated 2 h ago".
  • Reply is online only (conventions §8 class 3) — it changes a case's SLA-relevant status and must reach the server; the reply box is disabled offline with a hint, and typed text is kept in local state until the screen closes so a brief drop doesn't lose it.

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
Information requested Whichever side (reporter or reported) "We need more information" / "Reply to case CS-4471 to help us investigate." gc://reports/:id complaints No
Case resolved/dismissed Reporter only "Update on your report" / "There's an update on case CS-4471." gc://reports/:id complaints No
The reported party gets no push when the case is merely created or merely resolved/dismissed (BR-49.6/BR-50.6) — only when their reply is needed or when a separate enforcement notice is sent (owned by Admin M43's pipeline, not this module).

17. Security Rules

  • Every row is scoped by reporter_user_id = sub OR reported_user_id = sub OR institute staff membership — never by an id in the request body.
  • The reported-party response shape is a distinct, smaller DTO with no reporter fields, built server-side (not a client-side filter of the reporter's shape), so a compromised client can't recover hidden fields.
  • Reply text is scanned by the same contact-info detector as review text (M34) and warned inline, though not blocked, since sharing a phone number with support staff here is legitimate; the description is a hint only, not a hard rule enforced server-side for this endpoint.
  • Rate limit: 10 replies/hour per user across all their cases.

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Reply outside an open window CONFLICT_STATE 409 Toast, refetch (box hides if truly closed)
Reply too short VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Inline under the reply box
Case not found / not yours NOT_FOUND 404 "This case is no longer available."

Module 51 · Account Settings

Phase 16 · Settings · Used by: Any user (parent, student, teacher, institute staff) · Depends on: M00 (uploads for profile photo), M04 (OTP, sessions, refresh — Active Sessions and Sign out reuse M04 endpoints directly); Admin M00 (app_users) · New tables: none · Uses: app_users, user_auth_identities, otp_challenges, app_sessions, audit_logs, user_notifications · Build estimate: 4–5 days

1. Module Purpose

The single place every user manages their identity and how they sign in: display name and app language, changing phone or email with OTP proof, setting or changing a password, linking or unlinking Google Sign-In, and reviewing/revoking the devices they're signed in on. It owns no new tables — it edits app_users and user_auth_identities and reuses M04's session endpoints — but it is the module every other settings screen (M52–M54) hangs off.

2. User Stories

  • As a teacher, I want to change my phone number after switching SIMs without losing my account or verification history.
  • As a parent, I want to set a password so I can sign in even if I don't have OTP access for a moment (foreign roaming, dead SIM).
  • As any user, I want to link my Google account so I have a backup way to sign in.
  • As a security-conscious teacher, I want to see every device signed into my account and sign out the ones I don't recognise.
  • As a student, I want to change my display language to Hindi and have the whole app switch immediately.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-51.1 GET /account. Returns fullName, phone (own number, shown in full — this is the owner, not another user), email, preferredLanguage, accountStatus, and authMethods: one entry per active user_auth_identities row (phone always present, password present once set, google present once linked) plus linkedGoogleEmail when linked. updatedAt from app_users is the If-Match version for PATCH /account. BR-51.2 PATCH /account. Updates full_name (2–80 chars) and/or preferred_language (en, hi, kn, ta, te, mr, bn) with If-Match; stale match → VERSION_CONFLICT. A language change updates i18next immediately app-wide (no restart) and is sent as Accept-Language on subsequent requests, driving push/email template language. BR-51.3 Change phone. POST /account/phone/otp { newPhone } — rejects if newPhone already belongs to another active app_users row (CONFLICT_DUPLICATE); creates an otp_challenges row (purpose = 'change_phone', channel = 'sms', destination = newPhone), 6-digit code, 10-minute expiry, resend after 30 s, 5 attempts before OTP_LOCKED (10 min lock). POST /account/phone/verify { code } checks the challenge (attempts, expires_at, consumed_at IS NULL), then in one transaction: app_users.phone = newPhone, phone_verified_at = now(), and the user_auth_identities row with provider = 'phone' gets provider_subject = newPhone. otp_challenges.consumed_at = now(). BR-51.4 Change email. Same shape as BR-51.3 with purpose = 'change_email', channel = 'email'; email is case-insensitive (citext) and checked for an existing active owner the same way; on success sets app_users.email, email_verified_at, and updates the password identity's email column if one exists (password sign-in uses email as the identifier). BR-51.5 Set or change password. PUT /account/password. If no active user_auth_identities row with provider = 'password' exists yet, this is a set: the request carries an otpCode verified against a fresh challenge with purpose = 'reset_password' sent to the phone or email on file (there is no old password to confirm, so the flow reuses the same server-side check as M04's forgot-password) plus newPassword; a password identity row is inserted (password_hash, password_updated_at). If a password identity already exists, this is a change: the request instead carries currentPassword, verified with a constant-time hash compare against password_hash (3 wrong attempts in an hour → locked_until set, OTP_LOCKED-style 429), and newPassword. Either way newPassword must be 8–72 chars with at least one upper-case letter, one lower-case letter and one digit, and must not equal the current password. On success: password_updated_at = now(), failed_attempts = 0, and every other app_sessions row for the user is revoked (revoked_reason = 'password_changed') — the current session is kept so the user isn't logged out of the device they're using. BR-51.6 Link Google. POST /account/identities/google { idToken } — the server verifies the token with Google's tokeninfo endpoint (audience must match the app's OAuth client id), extracting sub and email. If a different app_users already has a google identity with that provider_subject → CONFLICT_DUPLICATE ("This Google account is already linked to another profile."). Otherwise upserts the caller's google identity (provider_subject, email). BR-51.7 Unlink an identity. DELETE /account/identities/:id soft-deletes (deleted_at = now()) the named user_auth_identities row, only for provider IN ('password','google') — the phone identity can never be unlinked from here (it is the account's primary identifier; changing it is BR-51.3, not unlinking). Rejected with CONFLICT_STATE ("Add another way to sign in before removing this one.") if it would leave the account with zero active identities besides phone when phone sign-in is currently disabled for the account, or more simply: rejected only when it is the user's only active identity of any kind, which in practice never happens since phone is permanent — so this guard exists purely to keep the invariant true if a future migration ever allows unlinking phone. BR-51.8 Active sessions and sign-out. This screen calls M04's GET /auth/sessions (list of app_sessions: device model, platform, last_used_at, a current: true flag on sid from the token) and DELETE /auth/sessions/:id to revoke one. "Sign out" on this device calls M04's POST /auth/logout; "Sign out all other devices" calls M04's POST /auth/logout-all (keeps the current session). BR-51.9 Security notifications. Any successful phone change, email change, password change/set, or Google link/unlink sends user_notifications to the account (category account, not urgent) with the device/time, so an owner who didn't take the action is alerted.

Screen Route name Purpose

14. State Management

  • Query keys: accountKeys.me. Every successful mutation invalidates accountKeys.me; useSetOrChangePasswordMutation also invalidates M04's sessionsKeys.list (other sessions disappear).
  • No dedicated Zustand store; preferredLanguage on success also updates the global useSession claim copy so tab labels and dates re-render immediately.

15. Offline Handling

  • GET /account is a persisted query (readable offline).
  • PATCH /account (name/language) is save draft, submit online: editing is allowed offline, the Save button is disabled with a hint, and the local edit is kept until it can be sent.
  • Phone/email OTP, password changes, and Google link/unlink are online only (conventions §8 class 3) — every one of them is a security-sensitive action.

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
Phone changed Self "Phone number updated" / "Your sign-in number was changed to •••• 0001." gc://account account No
Email changed Self "Email updated" / "Your sign-in email was changed." gc://account account No
Password set/changed Self "Password updated" / "Your password was changed. If this wasn't you, contact support." gc://account account No
Google linked/unlinked Self "Google account linked" / "unlinked" gc://account account No

17. Security Rules

  • Every endpoint scopes by sub; there is no path that accepts another user's id.
  • PUT /account/password and the OTP-verify calls are rate-limited tighter than the default (10/hour) and never logged with the code or password itself.
  • FLAG_SECURE on ChangePhone, ChangeEmail and ChangePassword (OTP/credential entry).
  • Changing phone or email does not by itself revoke other sessions (BR-51.3/51.4 note) — only a password change does, since phone/email changes are already OTP-proven on the new destination and a stolen-device attacker who changes them would need OTP access anyway; sessions are still listed so the user can manually revoke any they don't recognise.
  • Google idToken is verified server-side on every call; the client never trusts the decoded token locally for identity.

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Stale If-Match on PATCH /account VERSION_CONFLICT 409 "Updated elsewhere. Review and save again."
New phone/email already active elsewhere CONFLICT_DUPLICATE 409 Inline on the field
Wrong OTP OTP_INVALID 422 Inline under the code field
Too many OTP attempts OTP_LOCKED 429 "Too many attempts. Try again in 10 minutes."
Wrong current password, 3rd time AUTH_REFRESH_INVALID-style lock (OTP_LOCKED) 429 "Too many attempts. Try again in an hour."
Weak new password VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Inline under the field
Google account linked elsewhere CONFLICT_DUPLICATE 409 "This Google account is linked to another profile."
Unlink the account's last identity CONFLICT_STATE 409 "Add another way to sign in first."

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T51.1 Update name and language → saved, app language switches immediately; Maestro flow account_update_profile.
  • T51.2 Change phone: request OTP, verify with correct code → phone updated, security push received.
  • T51.3 Change phone to a number already active on another account → CONFLICT_DUPLICATE before any OTP is sent.
  • T51.4 6th wrong OTP attempt → OTP_LOCKED for 10 minutes.
  • T51.5 First-time password set via OTP → password identity appears in authMethods; can now sign in with email + password (M04).
  • T51.6 Change existing password with wrong current password 3 times → locked; correct password blocked for an hour.
  • T51.7 Successful password change → all other sessions revoked (verified via GET /auth/sessions showing only current); current session still works.
  • T51.8 Link Google already linked to a second account → CONFLICT_DUPLICATE.
  • T51.9 Unlink Google when password also exists → succeeds; unlink password when Google doesn't exist and it's the only non-phone identity → still succeeds (phone always remains).
  • T51.10 Offline: name edited, Save disabled with hint; reconnect → Save enabled, submits.
  • T51.11 Sign out this device from ActiveSessions → returns to Login; sign out all other devices → current session unaffected, others gone from the list.

20. Audit Log Events

Event When Details
app.profile_updated PATCH /account succeeds changed fields (no values for sensitive ones)
app.phone_changed Phone verify succeeds masked old/new number
app.email_changed Email verify succeeds masked old/new email
app.password_changed Password set/change succeeds whether it was a first set
app.identity_linked / app.identity_unlinked Google link/unlink provider

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • Apple Sign-In as a second social provider once iOS volume justifies it.
  • Passkeys (WebAuthn) as a phishing-resistant alternative to password.
  • Step-up re-authentication (fresh OTP) before especially sensitive actions like unlinking the only backup identity.
  • Session naming ("iPhone 14 · Bengaluru") using IP geolocation, shown next to the device model.
  • Email change confirmation on both old and new addresses (currently only the new one is OTP-verified) once email deliverability is proven reliable.

Module 52 · Privacy Settings

Phase 16 · Settings · Used by: Any user · Depends on: M00, M51 (entry point); Admin M04 (legal document versions), M05/M06/M11/M14/M21 (write the initial terms/privacy consents at registration) · New tables: user_privacy_settings, user_consents · Uses: app_users, audit_logs · Build estimate: 3 days

1. Module Purpose

What a user shows to others and allows the platform to do with their data, and the DPDP Act 2023 consent record behind it. Owns user_privacy_settings (display and data-use toggles) and user_consents (an append-only, auditable ledger of every consent granted or withdrawn — terms, privacy policy, marketing, personalisation, parental consent, minor data processing). Also handles the "download my data" request.

2. User Stories

  • As a parent, I want to hide my area from teachers I haven't contacted yet so that I control who sees where I live.
  • As a teacher, I want to turn off personalised recommendations if I don't want my activity used that way.
  • As any user, I want to withdraw marketing consent without losing access to the app.
  • As a privacy-conscious student, I want to download a copy of my data.
  • As any user, I want to be told clearly when the Terms or Privacy Policy change and need my consent again.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-52.1 GET /privacy. Reads user_privacy_settings WHERE user_id = sub; a missing row (never toggled) returns the defaults: show_last_name = false, show_area_to_teachers = true, show_profile_in_search = true, allow_whatsapp_contact = true, allow_personalised_recommendations = true, allow_marketing_notifications = false, allow_analytics = true — the row is created lazily on first PATCH. BR-52.2 PATCH /privacy. Partial update of the six display/behaviour toggles (show_last_name, show_area_to_teachers, show_profile_in_search, allow_whatsapp_contact, allow_analytics) with If-Match on updated_at. allow_personalised_recommendations and allow_marketing_notifications can also be read here but are written only through POST /consents (BR-52.4), so the two screens stay in sync from one source of truth; PATCH /privacy rejects those two fields with VALIDATION_FAILED if sent (details.reason = "use_consents_endpoint"). BR-52.3 Effect of toggles. show_profile_in_search = false excludes teachers/institutes from M27/M28 search and M30 recommendations within one indexing cycle (≤ 15 min); allow_analytics = false makes M00's POST /events accept only app_open/crash (BR-0.10); allow_whatsapp_contact = false hides the WhatsApp share/contact option on the profile (M33, M37); show_last_name = false shows reviews and lead requester names as first name + last initial everywhere. BR-52.4 GET /consents / POST /consents. GET /consents returns, per consent_type, the latest user_consents row (granted, document_version, created_at) — this is a read of the most recent row per type, not a full history, though the raw history is retained for compliance. POST /consents { consentType, granted, method } always inserts a new row (append-only ledger; never updates) with user_id = sub, document_version = the current published version for that type (from system_settings), method (toggle from this screen, checkbox/otp/email_link from other flows), ip_address, install_id. For consentType IN ('marketing','personalisation'), the same transaction also upserts the matching user_privacy_settings boolean (allow_marketing_notifications, allow_personalised_recommendations) so GET /privacy and GET /consents never disagree. terms/privacy_policy/parental_consent/data_processing_minor consents are not withdrawable from this screen (withdrawing them means the account can't be used) — attempting granted: false on those types → CONFLICT_STATE ("You can't withdraw this while keeping your account. You can delete your account instead."). BR-52.5 Re-consent on document change. GET /consents includes requiresReconsent: true for terms/privacy_policy when the latest granted row's document_version is older than the currently published version (system_settings keys legal.terms_version, legal.privacy_version). When true, the app shows a blocking ReconsentSheet on next launch (dismissible only by agreeing) before any other screen; agreeing calls POST /consents { consentType, granted: true, method: 'checkbox' } with the new version. BR-52.6 Data export. POST /privacy/data-export starts a job that compiles the caller's data (profile, children, leads, reviews, transactions summary, complaints they filed, consent history) into a password-protected ZIP, uploaded to gc-private, and emails a 72-hour download link to the verified email on file (falls back to "add an email first" if none — CONFLICT_STATE, details.reason = "email_required"). No new table is added for this: the request is throttled with a Redis key export:<userId> (one request per 30 days; a second call inside the window → LIMIT_REACHED, details.reason = "export_cooldown", details.availableAt) and recorded in audit_logs (app.data_export_requested) rather than its own row.

<details><summary>DDL</summary>

CREATE TABLE user_privacy_settings (
  user_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Owner
  show_last_name boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false, -- Reviews show "Lakshmi V." when false
  show_area_to_teachers boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- Teachers see the area on leads
  show_profile_in_search boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- Teachers/institutes: listed in search (false = paused listing)
  allow_whatsapp_contact boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- Show a WhatsApp button once contact is unlocked
  allow_personalised_recommendations boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- Use search history and children for recommendations
  allow_marketing_notifications boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- Announcements and offers
  allow_analytics boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true, -- Product analytics events
  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- Updated
);

CREATE TRIGGER trg_user_privacy_settings_updated BEFORE UPDATE ON user_privacy_settings FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION set_updated_at();

</details>

user_consents

Record of every consent given or withdrawn (terms, privacy policy, parental consent, marketing), as required by the DPDP Act 2023.

Column Type Null Default Constraints / References Description
id uuid no gen_random_uuid() PK Primary key
user_id uuid no — FK → app_users.id (on delete cascade) Data principal
consent_type text no — CHECK consent_type IN ('terms','privacy_policy','marketing','personalisation','parental_consent','data_processing_minor') What
document_version text no — — e.g. privacy-2026-09
granted boolean no — — true = given, false = withdrawn
method text no — CHECK method IN ('checkbox','otp','toggle','email_link') How it was captured
guardian_phone text yes — — For parental consent: verified guardian phone
ip_address inet yes — — IP
install_id uuid yes — — Install
created_at timestamptz no now() — When

<details><summary>DDL</summary>

CREATE TABLE user_consents (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), -- Primary key
  user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES app_users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, -- Data principal
  consent_type text NOT NULL CHECK (consent_type IN ('terms','privacy_policy','marketing','personalisation','parental_consent','data_processing_minor')), -- What
  document_version text NOT NULL, -- e.g. privacy-2026-09
  granted boolean NOT NULL, -- true = given, false = withdrawn
  method text NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('checkbox','otp','toggle','email_link')), -- How it was captured
  guardian_phone text, -- For parental consent: verified guardian phone
  ip_address inet, -- IP
  install_id uuid, -- Install
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() -- When
);
CREATE INDEX idx_user_consents_user ON user_consents (user_id, consent_type, created_at DESC);

</details>

14. State Management

  • Query keys: privacyKeys.settings, privacyKeys.consents. Both invalidate each other on the two consent types that are shared; useRequestDataExportMutation has no cache effect beyond a success toast.
  • useAppFlags gains reconsentBlockedUntilAgreed: boolean, checked by the root navigator before any other route.

15. Offline Handling

  • GET /privacy and GET /consents are persisted queries.
  • All writes here (PATCH /privacy, POST /consents, data export) are online only — they affect what the platform is allowed to do with the user's data and must be confirmed by the server, not queued speculatively.

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
Data export ready Self "Your data export is ready" / "Check lakshmi.v@gmail.com for your download link." gc://account/privacy account No
Email is the primary channel for the export link itself (it's a downloadable file, not something to open in-app); the push is a heads-up only.

17. Security Rules

  • user_privacy_settings/user_consents rows are always scoped to sub; no endpoint accepts another user's id.
  • The export ZIP is password-protected (a one-time code shown in-app, not in the email) and the R2 object is deleted by a job after the 72-hour link expiry.
  • ip_address/install_id are stored on each user_consents row for DPDP audit purposes but never surfaced back to the user or any other module.
  • Withdrawing allow_analytics takes effect on the next POST /events call; events already batched client-side before the toggle are still flushed (they were captured under the prior consent) but no new ones are queued.

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Stale If-Match VERSION_CONFLICT 409 "Updated elsewhere. Review and save again."
Withdraw terms/privacy/parental/minor consent CONFLICT_STATE 409 Explains the account-vs-consent tradeoff, offers Delete account
Marketing/personalisation sent to PATCH /privacy VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Handled client-side (never actually reaches the server)
Export requested twice within 30 days LIMIT_REACHED 429 Sheet shows the next available date
No verified email for export CONFLICT_STATE 409 "Add an email address first." → M51

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T52.1 First-ever GET /privacy (no row) → documented defaults returned; first PATCH creates the row.
  • T52.2 Turn off "Appear in search results" → teacher no longer appears in M27 search within the next indexing pass (integration test against the search index job).
  • T52.3 POST /consents {marketing:false} → user_consents gets a new row, user_privacy_settings.allow_marketing_notifications flips to false, GET /privacy reflects it immediately.
  • T52.4 Attempt to withdraw terms → CONFLICT_STATE.
  • T52.5 Bump legal.terms_version in system_settings → next GET /consents returns requiresReconsent: true; app shows the blocking sheet on launch; agreeing clears the flag.
  • T52.6 Request data export → 202, cooldown recorded; second request the same day → LIMIT_REACHED with the correct availableAt.
  • T52.7 Turn off allow_analytics → subsequent POST /events from M00 only accepts app_open/crash.
  • T52.8 Offline: toggles disabled with hint; no optimistic flip (this module's writes are online-only, unlike M40's favourites).

Module 53 · Help & Support

Phase 16 · Settings · Used by: Any user (FAQ browsing also Public, signed out) · Depends on: M00 (uploads, bootstrap support contacts), M40 (link a ticket to a transaction); Admin (ticket queue is an Admin portal addition — see Scalability) · New tables: faqs, support_tickets, support_ticket_messages · Uses: transactions, files, app_users, user_notifications, audit_logs · Build estimate: 4 days

1. Module Purpose

The help centre and support-ticket system: searchable FAQs by audience and category, the contact options shown from GET /bootstrap, and a ticketing flow with automatic device diagnostics, evidence attachments, a conversation thread, and a post-resolution rating. Not for safety reports — those are M49/M50's complaints; this module is for account, payment, verification, technical and feedback issues.

2. User Stories

  • As a new parent, I want to search "how do I add a child" and get an answer instantly without contacting anyone.
  • As a teacher whose payment failed, I want to raise a ticket linked to that specific transaction so support has the context already.
  • As a student on a 2G connection, I want the ticket form to attach my device info automatically so I don't have to describe my phone.
  • As any user, I want to see all my past tickets and reopen one instead of starting over.
  • As any user, I want to rate the support I received once my ticket is resolved.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-53.1 GET /faqs. Returns published FAQs (is_published = true, deleted_at IS NULL) matching audience IN ('all', :role) (signed out → 'all' only), optionally filtered by category (getting_started, account, payments, verification, leads_demos, reviews, safety, privacy) and a free-text q matched against question and answer_md (server-side ILIKE, ranked by a simple relevance score — exact question match first, then word overlap), ordered by sort_order within category. Cached client-side 24 h (masters-style ETag on the max updated_at). BR-53.2 POST /faqs/:id/feedback { helpful }. Atomically increments helpful_yes or helpful_no. Limited to one vote per (installId, faqId) per 24 h via a Redis key (RATE_LIMITED silently ignored client-side — the button just shows "Thanks for your feedback" either way, since a soft double-vote isn't worth surfacing an error for). BR-53.3 Contact options. HelpHome also renders support.email, support.phone, support.whatsapp, support.hours from GET /bootstrap (M01) — tapping opens the mail/dialer/WhatsApp app; these are not endpoints owned here. BR-53.4 Create a ticket. POST /support/tickets { category, subject, transactionId?, message, attachmentFileIds? } inserts one support_tickets row (status = 'open', priority = 'normal' unless category = 'payment' and transactionId maps to a transactions row with status = 'failed' in the last 24 h → priority = 'high') plus, in the same transaction, one support_ticket_messages row (author_type = 'app_user', author_id = sub, body = message, attachment_file_ids). app_version, device_info ({ platform, osVersion, appVersion, buildNumber, deviceModel, netType }) are attached automatically by the client, never typed by the user; ticket_number is server-assigned (ST- + a per-year sequence, matching the case_number pattern used for complaints). transactionId, if given, must belong to sub (FORBIDDEN otherwise). BR-53.5 Attachments. Up to 5 files per message, image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf, ≤ 10 MB each, purpose support_attachment (private), uploaded via M00 presign first, same shape as M49's evidence. BR-53.6 Conversation. POST /support/tickets/:id/messages { clientMessageId, body, attachmentFileIds? } — allowed while status IN ('open','awaiting_user','in_progress','resolved'); closed tickets reject with CONFLICT_STATE ("This ticket is closed. Start a new one.") and the app hides the composer, showing "Start a new ticket" instead. ON CONFLICT (author_id, client_message_id) DO NOTHING then return the existing row (idempotent offline replay, same pattern as M37 lead messages). A user message on a resolved ticket reopens it to in_progress. first_response_at is set by the admin side (read-only here) and shown as "Typically replies within 4 hours" context copy on the ticket list, derived from a rolling average, not a per-ticket promise. BR-53.7 Rating. POST /support/tickets/:id/rating { rating } (1–5), allowed only when status IN ('resolved','closed') and rating IS NULL (already-rated → CONFLICT_STATE, details.reason = "already_rated"); sets support_tickets.rating. BR-53.8 List and detail. GET /support/tickets (cursor, newest first, filter by status); GET /support/tickets/:id returns the ticket plus every support_ticket_messages row (author_type drives the bubble side: app_user = right/"You", admin = left/"Support", system = centred note e.g. "Ticket assigned to Priya").

Table Owner Purpose

14. State Management

  • Query keys: faqsKeys.list(category, q) (persisted), ticketsKeys.list(status), ticketsKeys.detail(id).
  • useSendTicketMessageMutation is optimistic (appends the bubble immediately with a "sending" state, reconciled by clientMessageId when the server response/queue flush returns).

15. Offline Handling

  • FAQs are persisted and fully readable offline (public, no personal data).
  • Ticket creation is save draft, submit online (class 2): draft kept per category; diagnostics are recomputed fresh at submit time (not from the draft, since network type may have changed).
  • Ticket messages are queue offline (class 1, idempotent via clientMessageId) exactly like M37 lead messages — sent automatically on reconnect, shown as "Sending…" then "Sent".
  • Rating is online only (simple, infrequent, no benefit to queuing).

16. Push Notification Requirements

Event Recipient Title / Body Deep link Category Urgent
Support replied Ticket owner "Support replied" / "New message on ST-10042." gc://support/tickets/:id account No
Ticket resolved Ticket owner "Your ticket is resolved" / "ST-10042 has been marked resolved. Let us know how we did." gc://support/tickets/:id account No

17. Security Rules

  • Every ticket/message query scoped by user_id = sub; a ticket id belonging to another user → NOT_FOUND (not FORBIDDEN, so ticket existence isn't leaked).
  • device_info never includes IMEI/serial, only OS/app version and model.
  • Attachment bucket private, 60-second presigned GET, viewable by the owner and support staff only.
  • FAQ endpoints are public and cached at the CDN edge for 5 minutes (no personal data).

18. Error Handling

Scenario Code HTTP App behaviour
Message on a closed ticket CONFLICT_STATE 409 Composer hidden, "Start a new ticket" shown
Rate an already-rated ticket CONFLICT_STATE 409 Rating banner hidden, refetch
Rate a ticket that isn't resolved/closed CONFLICT_STATE 409 Rating control hidden client-side (defensive only)
transactionId not owned by caller FORBIDDEN 403 Picker never lists it; defensive error if raced
Subject/message too short VALIDATION_FAILED 422 Inline under the field

19. Testing Scenarios

  • T53.1 Search "refund" → matching FAQs ranked by relevance; tapping one opens FaqDetail.
  • T53.2 👍 then 👎 on the same FAQ within a minute → only the first counts; second is silently absorbed, UI still thanks the user.
  • T53.3 Create a payment ticket linked to a failed transaction → priority = "high"; ticket appears at the top of "My tickets".
  • T53.4 Send a message while offline → shows "Sending…"; reconnect → delivered once, no duplicate (clientMessageId).
  • T53.5 Admin resolves a ticket (simulated via seed) → push received, rating banner appears; rate 4★ → banner disappears, second rating attempt blocked.
  • T53.6 Message on a closed ticket → CONFLICT_STATE, composer replaced with "Start a new ticket".
  • T53.7 5 attachments upload, submit → all 5 linked to the first message.
  • T53.8 GET /support/tickets/:id for a ticket owned by another user → NOT_FOUND.
  • T53.9 Signed-out user opens Help → sees only audience = all FAQs, no "My tickets" section (prompted to sign in).
  • T53.10 Diagnostics attached automatically match the device under test (platform, appVersion) without any user input.

20. Audit Log Events

Event When Details
app.support_ticket_created POST /support/tickets category, priority, whether a transaction was linked
app.support_ticket_rated POST /support/tickets/:id/rating rating value
Ticket messages themselves are not separately audited (conventions §11 excludes ordinary conversational content; the ticket creation event already captures that a case was opened).

21. Future Scalability Notes

  • In-app live chat for technical/account categories during support hours, falling back to async tickets outside them.
  • Suggested FAQs ranked by the user's own recent activity (e.g. a failed payment surfaces the refund FAQ first).
  • CSAT trend dashboard from support_tickets.rating (Admin side).
  • Canned replies and macros for support agents (Admin side).
  • Admin portal additions: a Support Tickets queue (list, filters by category/priority/status, assignment, SLA-style first-response tracking, reply composer with saved macros, rating dashboard) — support_tickets/support_ticket_messages have no admin screens in the Admin SRS pack today; this module's data model is ready for them.

Module 54 · Delete Account

Phase 16 · Settings · Used by: Any user · Depends on: M51 (entry point), M04 (OTP, sessions), M40 (invoices retained), M42/M46 (referrals, wallet); Admin M43 (open-complaint blocker), Admin M40 (invoice retention), Admin M28/M31 (role rows erased) · New tables: account_deletion_requests · Uses: app_users, app_sessions, user_devices, subscriptions, complaints, referrals, wallet_ledger, transactions, teacher_reviews, institute_reviews, audit_logs, user_notifications · Build estimate: 3–4 days

1. Module Purpose

Lets a user permanently delete their account, as Google Play and the App Store require of any app that lets people create one: reachable in-app without contacting support, OTP-confirmed, with a 30-day grace period to change their mind, clear blockers when deletion isn't safe yet (an open safety case, a pending referral payout), and a precise line between what is erased, what is anonymised, and what is retained for legal reasons (GST invoices, safety records).

2. User Stories

  • As a parent who found a tutor, I want to delete my account in a couple of taps without emailing anyone.
  • As a teacher, I want to know why I can't delete yet if I have an open complaint, and what to do about it.
  • As anyone who changes their mind, I want cancelling deletion to be as easy as signing back in.
  • As a privacy-conscious user, I want to know exactly what happens to my reviews, payments and referral rewards when my account is gone.

3. Business Rules & Logic

BR-54.1 GET /account/deletion. Returns the caller's current request, if any (none when there isn't one), plus a live blocker check computed fresh on every call (not cached), so the screen always reflects reality:

Blocker Condition details.reason
Open safety case A complaints row with reporter_user_id = sub OR reported_user_id = sub, status IN ('open','in_review','awaiting_info','escalated') open_complaint
Pending referral payout A referrals row with referrer_user_id = sub, status = 'qualified' (reward not yet released) pending_referral_payout
Negative wallet balance SUM(wallet_ledger.amount_paise) WHERE user_id = sub < 0 negative_wallet_balance
None of these are permanent — the screen tells the user what will resolve each one (case closes, referral reward releases on schedule, balance is settled by a future credit) and lets them retry later; there is no way to force through a blocker from the app.
BR-54.2 Request OTP. POST /account/deletion/otp sends a code (otp_challenges, purpose = 'delete_account') to the phone on file (or email if phone sign-in isn't the primary method), same throttling as other OTP purposes (30 s resend, 5 attempts → OTP_LOCKED). Blockers are not checked at this step — only at confirmation — so a user isn't told about a blocker before proving it's really them.
BR-54.3 Confirm deletion. POST /account/deletion { code, reasonCode, reasonText? } verifies the OTP, re-runs the blocker check from BR-54.1; any active blocker → 409 CONFLICT_STATE (details.reason = the blocker's reason, details.blockers = the full list) and no row is created. With no blockers: inserts account_deletion_requests (status = 'scheduled', reason_code one of found_teacher, not_useful, privacy, too_many_notifications, duplicate_account, other, reason_text ≤ 500 chars optional, scheduled_for = now() + 30 days). app_users.account_status is not changed to suspended — the account stays fully usable during the grace period (BR-54.4) except that active subscriptions with auto_renew = true are set auto_renew = false immediately (no surprise renewal into a deleted account).
BR-54.4 Grace period and cancelling by signing in. For 30 days the account works normally, with a persistent, dismiss-but-reappearing banner "Account scheduled for deletion on 26 Oct 2026" on Home and Account Settings. POST /account/deletion/cancel (no OTP required — being signed in with a valid session is proof enough, since cancelling only reduces harm) sets status = 'cancelled', cancelled_at = now(); the banner disappears and the account continues exactly as before. Signing in during the grace period does not cancel automatically — the user must tap the banner's "Cancel deletion" action — but any sign-in is what makes that action reachable, which is what "cancelling by signing in" means in practice.
BR-54.5 Execution (job at scheduled_for, only if still status = 'scheduled'). Sets status = 'processing', then in one transaction per user:
  • Erased: full_name → "Deleted user", phone/email → null, profile_photo_file_id → null (file deleted from R2); app_users.deleted_at = now(); role row (parents/students/teachers/institute_managers) deleted_at = now(); user_devices rows deleted and FCM tokens revoked; user_search_history, saved_searches, user_favorites, draft data — deleted outright.
  • Anonymised (kept for platform integrity, delinked from identity): teacher_reviews/institute_reviews authored by the user keep their star rating and text (removing them would unfairly change a teacher's/institute's score) but the author is shown as "Former user" once author's app_users row is scrubbed — no separate flag needed, since the join simply resolves to the scrubbed name; complaints rows keep reporter_user_id/reported_user_id pointing at the scrubbed app_users row (required by ON DELETE RESTRICT) and are retained 3 years after closure per Admin M43's own retention rule, then anonymised there.
  • Retained for legal reasons: transactions (and their invoice PDFs) are kept in full for 8 years under GST/Income Tax record-keeping rules, unmodified — a scrubbed app_users row still satisfies the foreign key; wallet_ledger history is kept (immutable ledger) but any positive balance is forfeited: one final row is appended (entry_type = 'expiry', amount_paise = the negative of the remaining balance, description = "Forfeited on account deletion"), zeroing it (there is no cash payout capability in v1 — see M42/M46 scalability).
  • app_sessions: every row revoked (revoked_reason = 'account_deleted'). subscriptions: any still-active row set status = 'cancelled', cancelled_by_type = 'system', cancel_reason = 'account_deleted'.
  • account_deletion_requests.status = 'completed', completed_at = now(), erasure_report = a small JSON summary (counts of rows erased/anonymised/retained per table) for support's future reference if the user ever asks what happened. BR-54.6 Store-policy compliance. The "Delete account" entry point sits directly in Account Settings (M51), reachable within two taps of app open, without requiring the user to contact support first — satisfying Google Play's Data safety / Account deletion requirement and Apple's App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1(v). It performs full data erasure per BR-54.5, not a mere deactivation, and works from within the app itself (BR-54.2/54.3), matching both platforms' requirement that in-app deletion be at least as capable as a request made another way. BR-54.7 Notifications. Scheduling sends an immediate push + email (category account) with the exact deletion date and a one-tap cancel deep link; a reminder push + email 3 days before execution; after execution, a final email only (no device tokens remain) confirming the account has been deleted, sent to the email address captured just before it was scrubbed.
